   331	    }
   332	
   333	    /// Derive every legacy-to-digest aggregate id map to a fixed point, then
   334	    /// rewrite typed references before rebuilding the target rows. The fixed
   335	    /// point matters when one aggregate groups by a reference to another.
   336	    /// Every pass is inside the adoption writer transaction, so no reader can
   337	    /// observe a dangling intermediate reference.
   338	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   339	    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain], previous: Option<&crate::schema::Schema>, activation_tx: Option<&crate::store::Tx<'_>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   340	        let mut legacy: LegacyIdentities = Vec::new();
   341	        let mut definitions = BTreeMap::<String, Vec<LegacyGroupField>>::new();
   342	        let identity_schema = previous.unwrap_or(self.schema);
   343	        for maintain in identity_schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
   344	            definitions.insert(maintain.target.clone(), legacy_group_fields(identity_schema, None, maintain));
   345	        }
   346	        let mut sequence_identity_map = LegacyIdentityMap::new();
   347	        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
   348	            // The durable legacy address is the predecessor's canonical
   349	            // logical group tuple. Decode that address with predecessor types:
   350	            // candidate projection may already have removed predecessor group
   351	            // columns when adoption also changes the maintain declaration.
   352	            let identity_maintain = match previous {
   353	                Some(schema) => match schema.maintain_for(&maintain.target)
   354	                    .filter(|old| old.private.is_none() && old.row_key.is_none()) {
   355	                    Some(old) => old,
   356	                    None => continue,
   357	                },
   358	                None => maintain,
   359	            };
   360	            let fields = legacy_group_fields(identity_schema, None, identity_maintain);
   361	            let mut rows = Vec::new();
   362	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   363	            loop {
   364	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   365	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   366	                for (row, encoded) in page {
   367	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   368	                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   369	                    let address = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(&old).ok()
   370	                        .filter(|key| key.len() == fields.len());
   371	                    let values = match address {
   372	                        Some(key) => key,
   373	                        None => identity_maintain.group_fields().iter().map(|field| Ok(row.field(field)?.clone()))
   374	                            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?,
   375	                    };
   376	                    let key: Vec<_> = fields.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
   377	                    rows.push((old, key));
   378	                }
   379	            }
   380	            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
   381	            for old in self.tx.sequence_ids(&maintain.target)? {
   382	                let values = decode_legacy_sequence_identity(&old, &fields);
   383	                if let Some(values) = values {
   384	                    let key = fields.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
   385	                    insert_sequence_identity(&maintain.target, old, key, &definitions, &mut sequence_identity_map);
   386	                }
   387	            }
   388	        }
   389	
   390	        // A removed aggregate can leave parent-counter history even after its
   391	        // derived rows and every allocating row are gone. The store marker
   392	        // covers that retained custody too: translate it from predecessor
   393	        // types now so reintroducing the same maintained target cannot revive
   394	        // a legacy address under a current marker.
   395	        if let Some(previous) = previous {
   396	            for maintain in previous.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain|
   397	                maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()
   398	                    && !maintains.iter().any(|current| current.target == maintain.target)) {
   399	                let fields = legacy_group_fields(previous, None, maintain);
   400	                for old in self.tx.sequence_ids(&maintain.target)? {
   401	                    let values = decode_legacy_sequence_identity(&old, &fields);
   402	                    if let Some(values) = values {
   403	                        let key = fields.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
   404	                        insert_sequence_identity(&maintain.target, old, key, &definitions, &mut sequence_identity_map);
   405	                    }
   406	                }
   407	            }
   408	        }
   409	
   410	        // Row references retain the established contract: only a stored
   411	        // aggregate target proves an old address. Sequence custody is broader;
   412	        // its parent key persists after target/source/child deletion, so its
   413	        // independently decoded legacy tuple joins the same fixed point.
   414	        let ids = settle_legacy_maintained_ids(&legacy, &BTreeMap::new())?;
   415	        let sequence_legacy: LegacyIdentities = sequence_identity_map.into_iter()
   416	            .map(|(target, rows)| (target, rows.into_iter().collect())).collect();
   417	        let sequence_ids = settle_legacy_maintained_ids(&sequence_legacy, &ids)?;
   418	
   419	        // Sequence counters are keyed by the referenced parent table and id,
   420	        // independently of any surviving allocating row. Translate them from
   421	        // the same target-specific maps before rows are rebuilt; colliding
   422	        // old/current counters retain the larger high-water value.
   423	        // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — digest adoption re-keys dependent sequence custody in the same transaction.
   424	        let mut rewritten = self.tx.rewrite_sequence_ids(&sequence_ids)?;
   425	
   426	        // Release retention is part of the store: a hidden row or column may
   427	        // still name an aggregate target that remains active through adoption.
   428	        // Rewrite its image and reference ledger in this transaction too.
   429	        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(match activation_tx {
   430	            Some(tx) => crate::store::dormant::rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(tx, &ids)?,
   431	            None => 0,
   432	        });
   433	
   434	        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
   435	            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
   436	                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
   437	                .collect();
   438	            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
   439	        }).collect();
   440	        for (name, table, columns) in references {
   441	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   442	            loop {
   443	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   444	                if page.is_empty() { break; }
   445	                for (old, encoded) in page {
   446	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
   447	                    let mut next = old.clone();
   448	                    let mut changed = false;
   449	                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
   450	                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
   451	                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
   452	                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
   453	                        }
   454	                    }
   455	                    if changed {
   456	                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
   457	                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
   458	                    }
   459	                }
   460	            }
   461	        }
   462	        Ok(rewritten)
   463	    }

   465	    /// Build one aggregate from the rows in the store: the target's rows go,
   466	    /// then every source row contributes once. A schema change that adds or
   467	    /// redefines a `maintain` calls this, so a count over existing rows is
   468	    /// right from its first read (day two, LLP 2000.000 §11.2).
   469	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   470	    pub(crate) fn rebuild_maintain(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   471	        let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
   472	        let saved = self.column_rebuild;
   473	        self.column_rebuild |= maintain.private.is_some();
   474	        let result = self.rebuild_maintain_inner(maintain);
   475	        self.column_rebuild = saved;
   476	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   477	        result
   478	    }
   479	
   480	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   481	    fn rebuild_maintain_inner(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   482	        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.rebuild_row_view(maintain); }
   483	        let target = self.schema.table(&maintain.target).expect("validated");
   484	        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   485	        let target_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64);
   486	        self.meter.heap(target_bytes.saturating_mul(256))?;
   487	        loop {
   488	            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   489	            if page.is_empty() { break; }
   490	            for (existing, key) in page {
   491	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   492	                self.refuse_timeline_write(&maintain.target, crate::schema::Effect::Delete)?;
   493	                let entries = self.tx.delete(&maintain.target, target, &existing)?;
   494	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   495	                self.row_changed(&maintain.target, Some(&existing), None, Origin::Maintained)?;
   496	            }
   497	        }
   498	        let source = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   499	        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(source).saturating_mul(256))?;
   500	        let mut totals: BTreeMap<String, (Vec<Value>, i128)> = BTreeMap::new();
   501	        bounds = Bounds::default();
   502	        loop {
   503	            let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.source, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
   504	            if page.is_empty() { break; }
   505	            for (mut image, key) in page {
   506	                self.rebuilt_source_rows += 1;
   507	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   508	                materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, source);
   509	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   510	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
   511	                if !maintain.selected(&image) { continue; }
   512	                // @ref LLP 3000.028#6 — a total unique owner key has one contribution; backfill streams bounded pages instead of retaining all lifetime keys in a totals map.
   513	                if maintain.own_keys.is_some() {
   514	                    let heap = self.meter.used.heap_bytes;
   515	                    self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
   516	                    self.apply_aggregate(maintain, maintain.source_key(&image), 1, Some(true))?;
   517	                    self.meter.used.heap_bytes = heap;
   518	                    continue;
   519	                }
   520	                self.meter.heap(target_bytes)?;
   521	                let key = maintain.source_key(&image);
   522	                let change = delta(maintain, &image, 1)?;
   523	                let entry = match totals.entry(canonical_json(&key)) {
   524	                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(entry) => {
   525	                        self.meter.used.heap_bytes -= target_bytes;
   526	                        entry.into_mut()
   527	                    }
   528	                    std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => entry.insert((key, 0)),
   529	                };
   530	                entry.1 = entry.1.checked_add(change).ok_or_else(|| aggregate_overflow(maintain))?;
   531	            }
   532	        }
   533	        for (_, (key, change)) in totals {
   534	            if change != 0 || self.live_sum(maintain) {
   535	                self.apply_aggregate(maintain, key, change, Some(true))?;
   536	            }
   537	        }
   538	        Ok(())
   539	    }
   540	
   541	    fn live_sum(&self, maintain: &Maintain) -> bool {
   542	        matches!(maintain.kind, MaintainKind::Sum { .. }) && self.schema.table(&maintain.source).is_some_and(|source| source.is_expiring())
   543	    }
   544	
   545	    /// A zero sum is still a group while source rows remain: one signed
   546	    /// contribution may expire before the other. Keep its candidate row so
   547	    /// a scan, snapshot and offline replica can discover the later live sum.
   548	    fn aggregate_source_present(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   549	        // One returned source image and its encoded key (MemoryRows also materializes count_prefix).
   550	        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]).saturating_mul(2);
   551	        self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| {
   552	            let source = &runner.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
   553	            let index = maintain.contribution_index();
   554	            if !source.indexes.contains_key(&index) { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("maintain {} needs its contribution index", maintain.target))); }
   555	            runner.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   556	            let present = runner.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.count_prefix(allowance, &maintain.source, &index, key, 1))? != 0;
   557	            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — a local positive witness keeps zero; absence needs complete, currently held source coverage.
   558	            if !present && runner.device && !runner.aggregate_source_complete(maintain, key)? {
   559	                runner.unknown_fact(&maintain.source, &index, key, "zero-sum occupancy");
   560	                return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("the zero-sum group's source occupancy is not known locally; queued without a predicted row".into()));
   561	            }
   562	            Ok(present)
   563	        })
   564	    }
   565	
   566	    fn aggregate_source_complete(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   567	        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
   568	        if source.sync.as_ref().is_none_or(|sync| sync.horizon.is_some()) || self.schema.maintain_subset_unknown(&maintain.target) { return Ok(false); }
   569	        // The target has the same bare audience keys, but no source horizon.
   570	        if !self.upsert_absence_proven(&maintain.target, "byGroup", &target_group_key(maintain, key))? { return Ok(false); }
   571	        for (name, index) in &source.indexes {
   572	            let values = index.columns().iter().map_while(|column| maintain.by.iter().position(|field| field == column).map(|n| key[n].clone())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
   573	            if self.retained_group(&maintain.source, name, &values)? { return Ok(false); }
   574	        }
   575	        Ok(true)
   576	    }

   578	    fn apply_aggregate(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, key: Vec<Value>, change: i128, source_present: Option<bool>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

+### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
+
+Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
+64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
+`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
+The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
+identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
+adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
+address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
+
+The store metadata marker `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` binds persisted
+aggregate targets to that function. Opening or adopting a store without the
+marker — including a 0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON
+of the group key — atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate
+target from its source rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic
+generation. A failure rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation
+together. Adoption advice counts that rebuild even when schema/program bytes
+are unchanged. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
+it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
+zero.
+

-**Expiry is not a delete.** A parent whose `expire at` passes is absent from
-that moment, and the sweep removes it physically; neither fires an action.
-A child of an expiring parent outlives it unless the child declares the same
-lifetime (`read through`, or its own `expire at`). The writes card says so.
+**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
+is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
+can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
+sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
+expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
+bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
+not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
+constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
+
+A live `restrict` child keeps the expired root physically stored and the sweep
+continues to later due keys. The retained root remains logically unreadable.
+Short sweeps preserve a per-table scan continuation, so repeated bounded calls
+cannot restart forever at the same restricted or read-through-retained roots;
+after reaching the end they wrap for roots whose blockers were removed.
+Expired children are not live restrict witnesses, as in step 4. A read-through
+child remains the stricter physical exception because its stored image depends
+on its parent. Any error after an earlier cascade or set-null write rolls back
+the whole retirement transaction. A restricted root alone is an expected
+deferred cleanup, not an error for the sweep as a whole.

+/// Activation marker for the maintained-row address function. A missing or

+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_META: &str = "maintained_id_version";
+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION: &str = "sha256-v1";

+/// The id of a maintained row is a fixed-size digest of its typed group key.

+/// id. Domain separation makes future encodings explicit migrations.

+#[test]
+fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
+    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);
+    let long = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".repeat(100_000))]);
+    assert_eq!(short.len(), 64);
+    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(short, long);
+    assert_ne!(short, crate::value::digest(&[Value::String("x".into())]));

+
+#[test]
+fn missing_identity_marker_rebuilds_a_principal_reference_and_max_text_group() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table parents:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  owner: principal\n  parent: parents\n  token: text <=64\n  amount: int\n  public\nview totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    let owner = format!("user:{}", "o".repeat(59));
+    let parent = "p".repeat(64);
+    let token = "t".repeat(64);
+    assert_eq!((owner.len(), parent.len(), token.len()), (64, 64, 64));
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("owner", Value::Id(owner.clone())),
+            ("parent", Value::Id(parent.clone())), ("token", Value::String(token.clone())), ("amount", Value::Int(7))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(owner), Value::Id(parent), Value::String(token)]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    let after = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn identity_redeployment_rebuilds_the_ungrouped_empty_tuple() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  public\nview total: count entries\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into()))]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("total").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("$global").unwrap(), &Value::Bool(true));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    let after = e.store().rows("total").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("$global").unwrap(), &Value::Bool(true));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+}

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_capability_upgrades_legacy_wire_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let schema = compile("table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n");
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    // A pre-migration stored schema may already have a carrier for unrelated
+    // capabilities. Decode it once, then stamp the digest identity capability
+    // on every newly published schema/projection.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap();
+    assert!(encoded.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}

+    // Server expiry is a physical retirement with the schema's declared
+    // referential effects. Devices receive that one committed closure just as
+    // they receive an authored parent delete.
+    let expiring = r#"
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public 'parents'
+  sync public
+table cascadeChildren:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  public 'cascadeChildren'
+  sync public
+table nullableChildren:
+  parent: parents ? on delete set null
+  public 'nullableChildren'
+  sync public
+"#;
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(expiring);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeChildren".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c")), ("parent", id("p"))])),
+        ("nullableChildren".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("n")), ("parent", id("p"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("expiry-actions", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 0);
+    let from = d.state().unwrap().0;
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 100).unwrap(), 1);
+    d.apply(&stream_page(&mut e, "alice", from), false).unwrap();
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeChildren").is_empty());
+    let nullable = d.store().raw_rows("nullableChildren");
+    assert_eq!(nullable.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(nullable[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+    host.close("expiry-actions", d);
+
     // Every referencing group is public and held: the cascade predicts, deleting the held tasks.
     let (mut e, b) = compile(PUBLIC);
     assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "setup", "alice", &[]), "ok");
@@ -173,6 +209,55 @@ mutation drop(id: parents):
     host.close("retained-cascade", d);
 }
 
+#[test]
+fn authoritative_memory_sweeps_resume_and_wrap_past_restricted_roots() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut store = snapback4_device::memory::MemoryStore::new();
+    store.activate_server_at(bound.schema, 0).unwrap();
+    store.seed_server_at([
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "continuation reaches the free root within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(store.raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(store.raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("root").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+
+    // The cursor is after z. A lower new key is found after the scan wraps;
+    // each restricted root still consumes one bounded visit.
+    store.seed_server_at([("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", id("aa-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10)),
+    ]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "a wrapped scan reaches the new lower key within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(!store.raw_rows("roots").iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("aa-free")));
+}

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..05a91f6ddf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+//! Expiry is a physical delete trigger for referential actions (LLP 3000.039
+//! §3). These cases cover scheduled cleanup, commit-end retirement and
+//! same-id replacement of an expired row against the real engine.
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState, value::object};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn id(value: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(value.into()) }
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+const SWEEP: &str = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+  sync public
+"#;
+
+#[test]
+fn sweep_applies_every_action_and_advances_past_a_restricted_root() {
+    let mut e = engine(SWEEP);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("ca")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    for expected in [0, 0, 0, 1] {
+        assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), expected, "a one-row sweep must advance its physical scan position");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["a-blocked", "b-blocked", "c-blocked"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["ca"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    for blocker in ["ba", "bb", "bc"] { e.seed_delete("blockers", blocker).unwrap(); }
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_late_cascade_refusal_rolls_back_earlier_set_null_writes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'children'
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children
+  read through .child
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("n")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    let error = e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", "{error:?}");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &id("p"), "the prior set-null write rolled back");
+    for table in ["roots", "children", "grandchildren"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_retirement_and_expired_same_id_replacement_apply_actions() {
+    let source = format!(r#"{SWEEP}
+mutation bornExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'born', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert cascadeKids {{id: 'born-c', root: 'born'}}
+  insert nullableKids {{id: 'born-n', root: 'born'}}
+  return null
+mutation bornRestricted():
+  insert roots {{id: 'blocked', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert blockers {{id: 'blocked-b', root: 'blocked'}}
+  return null
+mutation replaceExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'old', expiresAt: null}}
+  return null
+"#);
+    let mut e = engine(&source);
+    let sent = e.mutate("bornExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    let refused = e.mutate("bornRestricted", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty(), "the refused birth and its blocker roll back together");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("blockers").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(1))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("old-c")), ("root", id("old"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replaceExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty(), "same-id cleanup cannot orphan the expired predecessor's child");
+}
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c6754a981f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
+//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
+use rusqlite::Connection;
+use std::{
+    fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
+table entries:
+  group: text <=256
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
+  public
+mutation add(group: text <=256, amount: int):
+  insert entries {group, amount}
+query total(group: text <=256):
+  return totals[group]
+"#;
+
+struct Temp(PathBuf);
+impl Temp {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            std::time::SystemTime::now()
+                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+                .unwrap()
+                .as_nanos()
+        ));
+        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
+        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), SOURCE).unwrap();
+        Self(path)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Temp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
+    }
+}
+
+fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
+    Connection::open(store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_rebuilds_legacy_aggregate_ids_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        baseline.is_file(),
+        "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}",
+        baseline.display()
+    );
+    let version = Command::new(&baseline).arg("--version").output().unwrap();
+    assert!(version.status.success());
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).contains("0.4.28"),
+        "unexpected baseline: {:?}",
+        version
+    );
+
+    let dir = Temp::new();
+    let group = "x".repeat(200);
+    let args = serde_json::json!({"group": group, "amount": 7}).to_string();
+    let written = Command::new(&baseline)
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args(["run", "add", &args, "--as", "alice", "--now", "1", "--json"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        written.status.success(),
+        "{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&written.stderr)
+    );
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let legacy = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert!(
+        legacy.len() > snapback4_core::rows::MAX_ID_BYTES,
+        "the frozen binary must have written the oversized legacy address"
+    );
+    let before: u64 = Connection::open(&store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let opened = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"))
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args([
+            "run",
+            "total",
+            &serde_json::json!({"group": group}).to_string(),
+            "--as",
+            "alice",
+            "--now",
+            "2",
+            "--json",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        opened.status.success(),
+        "stdout={} stderr={}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stderr)
+    );
+    let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&opened.stdout).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(answer["data"]["value"], 7, "{answer}");
+
+    let digest = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(digest, legacy);
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    let (after, marker): (u64, String) = (
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap(),
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+            [snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap(),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        after > before,
+        "identity adoption must publish a new device generation"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(marker, snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION);
+
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SOURCE.into())]);

    93	    pub(super) fn physical_children(
    94	        &mut self,
    95	        parent: &str,
    96	        id: &Value,
    97	    ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    98	        self.physical_children_outside(parent, id, &BTreeSet::new())

   100	
   101	    /// Whether a read-through child remains outside a delete's cascade
   102	    /// closure. Children in `deleting` are removed first by deletion_order and
   103	    /// therefore do not physically retain their parent.
   104	    pub(super) fn physical_children_outside(
   105	        &mut self,
   106	        parent: &str,
   107	        id: &Value,
   108	        deleting: &BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
   109	    ) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   110	        let children: Vec<_> = self
   111	            .schema
   112	            .children(parent)
   113	            .map(|(n, _, _)| {
   114	                // Only identities from this child table can appear in its
   115	                // index scan. Identities from other closure tables cannot
   116	                // consume a row in this table's prefix.
   117	                let inside = deleting.iter().filter(|(table, _)| table == n).count();
   118	                (n.clone(), inside.saturating_add(1))
   119	            })
   120	            .collect();
   121	        // Reserve the complete schema-fixed probe set before its first seek.
   122	        // Never short-circuit on an occupied table, including at low ceilings.
   123	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — the seeks draw from the request's physical allowance; occupancy never selects the logical charge.
   124	        let heap = children.iter().map(|(name, limit)| super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[name]).saturating_mul(*limit as u64)).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   125	        let probes = children.iter().map(|(_, limit)| *limit as u64).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   126	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, probes), (MeterKind::Steps, probes), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {
   127	            let mut occupied = false;
   128	            for (name, limit) in &children {
   129	                let rows = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, *limit)?;
   130	                occupied |= rows.into_iter().any(|(row, _)| row.field("id").ok().and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
   131	                    .is_none_or(|child| !deleting.contains(&(name.clone(), child.to_owned()))));
   132	            }
   133	            Ok(occupied)
   134	        })
   135	    }

   137	    // A deadline suffix skips an arbitrary expired backlog in one seek.
   138	    pub(super) fn refuse_live_children(
   139	        &mut self,
   140	        parent: &str,
   141	        id: &Value,
   142	    ) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   143	        let children: Vec<_> = self
   144	            .schema
   145	            .children(parent)
   146	            .map(|(n, _, _)| n.clone())
   147	            .collect();
   148	        if children.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }
   149	        let now = self
   150	            .context
   151	            .now
   152	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("delete clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   153	        let heap = children
   154	            .iter()
   155	            .map(|n| super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[n]).saturating_mul(3))
   156	            .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   157	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — three schema-fixed seeks per child table, each drawn from the request's physical allowance.
   158	        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::Examined, children.len() as u64 * 3), (MeterKind::Steps, children.len() as u64 * 3), (MeterKind::HeapBytes, heap)], |runner, scope| {
   159	            if runner.device {
   160	                let occupied = runner.device_work(|runner| runner.current_children(parent, id, &children))?;
   161	                return if occupied { Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent)) } else { Ok(()) };
   162	            }
   163	            for name in &children {
   164	                let never = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone(), Value::Null], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?;
   165	                let finite = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds { gt: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() }, Dir::Asc, 1)?;
   166	                if !never.is_empty() || !finite.is_empty() {
   167	                    return Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent));
   168	                }
   169	                // §3.3 forbids physical removal even when §6's live probe is empty.
   170	                // The author's implementation ruling keeps this case fail-closed.
   171	                if !runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?.is_empty() {
   172	                    return Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent));
   173	                }
   174	            }
   175	            Ok(())
   176	        })
   177	    }

   179	    pub(super) fn parent_has_children(&self, parent: &str) -> RuntimeError {
   180	        RuntimeError::Structural {
   181	            code: "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN",
   182	            message: format!("{parent} at {} has stored children; delete its live read-through children and sweep expired children, then retry `delete {parent}[id]` (guide rules)", self.statement_site),
   183	        }
   184	    }

   186	    // @ref LLP 3000.014#5 — retained history cannot terminally refuse a
   187	    // current delete. Mismatched, expired or uncovered witnesses must queue.
   188	    fn current_children(&mut self, parent: &str, id: &Value, children: &[String]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   189	        if children.is_empty() { return Ok(false); }
   190	        let uncertain = || RuntimeError::Prediction("parent deletion needs complete matching current child coverage; queued without a row".into());
   191	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   192	        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[parent]))?;
   193	        // Device-only work over held state: the token counts it on the device's separate physical allowance.
   194	        let parent_id = id.as_str()?.to_owned();
   195	        let parent_row = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.get(scope, parent, &parent_id))?.ok_or_else(uncertain)?;
   196	        for name in children {
   197	            let table = &self.schema.tables[name];
   198	            let through = table.through.as_ref().unwrap();
   199	            if !self.child_coverage(name, through, &parent_row)? { return Err(uncertain()); }
   200	            let table_scratch = self.meter.mark();
   201	            // Expected captures plus a reusable row/cursor, reserved before seeking.
   202	            self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(table).saturating_mul(3))?;
   203	            let mut expected = crate::value::object([] as [(&str, Value); 0]);
   204	            stamp(&self.schema.tables[parent], through, &parent_row, &mut expected)?;
   205	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   206	            loop {
   207	                let scratch = self.meter.mark();
   208	                self.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   209	                self.meter.step(through.fields.len() as u64 + 1)?;
   210	                let page = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.scan_metered(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 1, &mut runner.meter))?;
   211	                let Some((row, key)) = page.into_iter().next() else { break };
   212	                if self.engine_action && self.tx.retained_row(name, &row)? { return Err(uncertain()); }
   213	                if !self.tx.retained_row(name, &row)? {
   214	                    if self.expired(table, &row)
   215	                        || !(self.tx.current_row(name, &row)? || self.is_provisional(name, &row)?)
   216	                        || !capture_matches(through, &expected, &row) { return Err(uncertain()); }
   217	                    return Ok(true);
   218	                }
   219	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key).map(|key| key.into_iter().skip(1).collect());
   220	                self.meter.release_heap(scratch);
   221	            }
   222	            self.meter.release_heap(table_scratch);
   223	        }
   224	        Ok(false)
   225	    }
   226	}

   228	pub(super) fn capture_matches(through: &Through, expected: &Value, row: &Value) -> bool {
   229	    through.fields.keys().map(String::as_str).chain([PARENT_DEADLINE])
   230	        .all(|field| row.field(field).ok() == expected.field(field).ok())
   231	}

   233	pub(super) fn stamp(
   234	    parent: &Table,
   235	    through: &Through,
   236	    image: &Value,
   237	    row: &mut Value,
   238	) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   239	    let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, parent);
   240	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = row {
   241	        for (capture, source) in &through.fields {
   242	            fields.insert(capture.clone(), image.field(source)?.clone());
   243	        }
   244	        fields.insert(
   245	            PARENT_DEADLINE.into(),
   246	            parent
   247	                .deadline(&image)
   248	                .map(Value::Int)
   249	                .unwrap_or(Value::Null),
   250	        );
   251	    }
   252	    Ok(())
   253	}

    13	/// Rotate a sweep's table order after the last table that consumed a bounded
    14	/// visit. Per-table row cursors alone can starve every later table when an

    16	pub(crate) fn resume_expiry_tables(

    28	    tables
    29	}

    35	/// Only inherited batches need staging. Preserve the streaming path for

    37	pub(crate) fn ancestor_order<'a, I>(
    38	    schema: &Schema,
    39	    rows: I,
    40	) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = (String, Value)> + 'a>
    41	where
    42	    I: IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
    43	    I::IntoIter: 'a,

    45	    if schema.tables.values().all(|t| t.through.is_none()) {

    47	    }

    49	    let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
    50	    rows.sort_by_key(|(name, _)| order.iter().position(|n| n == name).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));

    64	fn sample(samples: &mut Vec<String>, row: &Value, reference: &str, parent: &str) {
    65	    fn bounded(text: &str) -> &str {

   109	fn correspondence(

   111	    parent: &RuleExpr,
   112	) -> Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, String>> {
   113	    if child.is_uniformly_readable() && parent.is_uniformly_readable() {
   114	        return Some(Default::default());
   115	    }
   116	    fn walk(
   117	        a: &serde_json::Value,
   118	        b: &serde_json::Value,

   120	    ) -> bool {

   160	impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
   161	    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {

   273	                "missing, ambiguous or disagreeing predecessor audience correspondence",
   274	                &samples,
   275	            ));
   276	        }
   277	    }
   278	    for name in next.through_order() {
   279	        let table = &next.tables[&name];
   280	        let Some(t) = &table.through else {
   281	            continue;
   282	        };
   283	        let parent = &next.tables[&t.parent];
   284	        let recapture = previous.table(&name).and_then(|t| t.through.as_ref()) != Some(t);
   285	        let mut invalid = 0;
   286	        let mut samples = Vec::new();
   287	        rows(tx, &name, |old| {
   288	            let mut row = old.clone();
   289	            // @ref LLP 3000.000.000#2-retain-by-default — restored audience/deadline captures retain their original lifetime.
   290	            let historical = retained.contains(&name) && old.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).is_ok();
   291	            if recapture && (!historical || t.fields.keys().any(|field| old.field(field).is_err()))
   292	            {
   293	                let parent_row = old
   294	                    .field(&t.reference)
   295	                    .ok()
   296	                    .and_then(|id| id.as_str().ok())
   297	                    .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
   298	                    .transpose()?
   299	                    .flatten();
   300	                // @ref LLP 3000.014#7-activation — previous-schema expiry was retired before projection; a newly due deadline must propagate, not veto adoption.
   301	                let Some(parent_row) = parent_row else {
   302	                    invalid += 1;
   303	                    sample(&mut samples, &old, &t.reference, &t.parent);
   304	                    return Ok(());
   305	                };
   306	                if historical {
   307	                    let mut fresh = row.clone();
   308	                    super::through::stamp(parent, t, &parent_row, &mut fresh)?;
   309	                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
   310	                        for field in t.fields.keys().filter(|field| old.field(field).is_err()) {
   311	                            fields.insert(field.clone(), fresh.field(field)?.clone());
   312	                        }
   313	                    }
   314	                } else {
   315	                    super::through::stamp(parent, t, &parent_row, &mut row)?;
   316	                }
   317	            }
   318	            table.recompute_deadline(&mut row)?;
   319	            let before = previous.table(&name).and_then(|table| table.deadline(&old));
   320	            if table
   321	                .deadline(&row)
   322	                .is_some_and(|after| before.is_none_or(|before| after < before))
   323	            {
   324	                *shortened.entry(name.clone()).or_default() += 1;
   325	            }
   326	            tx.put(&name, table, &row, Some(&old))?;
   327	            Ok(())
   328	        })?;
   329	        if invalid > 0 {
   330	            return Err(refusal(&name, invalid, "missing parent", &samples));
   331	        }
   332	    }
   333	    Ok(shortened)
   334	}

   336	/// Trusted restoration validates the existing immutable captures; it never stamps them.
   337	pub fn validate_restore(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, now: i64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   338	    for name in schema.through_order() {
   339	        let table = &schema.tables[&name];
   340	        let Some(t) = &table.through else {
   341	            continue;
   342	        };
   343	        let parent = &schema.tables[&t.parent];
   344	        let mut invalid = 0;
   345	        let mut samples = Vec::new();
   346	        rows(tx, &name, |row| {
   347	            let found = row
   348	                .field(&t.reference)
   349	                .ok()
   350	                .and_then(|v| v.as_str().ok())
   351	                .map(|id| tx.get(&t.parent, id))
   352	                .transpose()?
   353	                .flatten();
   354	            let matches = found.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| {
   355	                (!parent.expired(p, now) || table.expired(&row, now)) && {
   356	                    let p = crate::schema::row_image(p, parent);
   357	                    t.fields
   358	                        .iter()
   359	                        .all(|(field, source)| row.field(field).ok() == p.field(source).ok())
   360	                        && row.field(PARENT_DEADLINE).ok()
   361	                            == Some(&parent.deadline(&p).map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null))
   362	                }
   363	            });
   364	            if !matches {
   365	                invalid += 1;
   366	                sample(&mut samples, &row, &t.reference, &t.parent);
   367	            }
   368	            Ok(())
   369	        })?;
   370	        if invalid > 0 {
   371	            return Err(refusal(
   372	                &name,
   373	                invalid,
   374	                "restored captures do not match a live parent",
   375	                &samples,
   376	            ));
   377	        }
   378	    }
   379	    Ok(())
   380	}

   382	pub fn validate_indexes(tx: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   383	    for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
   384	        let mut checks: Vec<_> = table
   385	            .indexes
   386	            .iter()
   387	            .filter(|(_, i)| i.unique)
   388	            .map(|(name, i)| (name, i.components.len(), 1, true))
   389	            .collect();
   390	        for constraint in &table.constraints {
   391	            if let crate::schema::Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
   392	                let (index, _) = table
   393	                    .indexes
   394	                    .iter()
   395	                    .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().starts_with(by))
   396	                    .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} cap has no index")))?;
   397	                checks.push((index, by.len(), u64::from(*max), false));
   398	            }
   399	        }
   400	        for (index, width, max, nulls_distinct) in checks {
   401	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   402	            let mut previous = None;
   403	            let mut count = 0;
   404	            loop {
   405	                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
   406	                if page.is_empty() {
   407	                    break;
   408	                }
   409	                for (_, key) in page {
   410	                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
   411	                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
   412	                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
   413	                    bounds.after = Some(full);
   414	                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
   415	                        continue;
   416	                    }
   417	                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
   418	                        count += 1;
   419	                    } else {
   420	                        previous = Some(group);
   421	                        count = 1;
   422	                    }
   423	                    if count > max {
   424	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
   425	                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
   426	                        )));
   427	                    }
   428	                }
   429	            }
   430	        }
   431	    }
   432	    Ok(())
   433	}

   435	impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
   436	    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
   437	    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
   438	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   439	        &mut self,
   440	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   441	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   443	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   444	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   448	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
   449	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   450	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   451	        for (name, row) in rows {
   452	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   453	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   454	            self.upsert(
   455	                &name,
   456	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   457	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   458	            )?;
   459	        }
   460	        self.check_final_exists()?;
   461	        Ok(count)
   462	    }
   463	
   464	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}
