   208	                // The bounded probes have completed. Their occupancy is not
   209	                // disclosed by the collision's logical meter or heap peak.
   210	                self.meter.restore(mark);
   211	                return Err(if predecessor.is_some() {
   212	                    RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} already has a row with id {id}"))
   213	                } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "parent identity has stored children") });
   214	            }
   215	        }
   216	        if let Some(existing) = &predecessor {
   217	            if !self.expired(table, &existing) {
   218	                return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} already has a row with id {id}")));
   219	            }
   220	            // The expired predecessor is internal authorization work, not a
   221	            // disclosed examination (LLP 3000.015 §§1–2).
   222	            self.retire_expired_row(table_name, existing)?;
   223	        }
   224	        // Retiring an expired predecessor can cascade a source row whose
   225	        // contribution determines this image's maintained columns. Initialize
   226	        // them from the post-retirement private totals. Maintained columns are
   227	        // forbidden from constraints and authority, so the earlier collision
   228	        // and authorization preflights need only the authored image.
   229	        let row = self.birth_columns(table_name, row)?;
   230	        super::validate::validate_before_slots(self.schema, table_name, &row)?;
   231	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — an authored plain insert predicts unproved; a later refusal is then the server's
   232	        // to report. The engine's own timeline writes are not the author's prediction.
   233	        if let Some(index) = proof.filter(|_| {
   234	            !if_absent && upsert_index.is_none() && !self.unproved_write && self.timeline_authority.is_none()
   235	        }) {
   236	            // An earlier unknown fact already makes this prediction unproved.
   237	            // Otherwise the proof's own unknown fact is not the prediction's.
   238	            self.unproved_write = self.missing_fact.is_some();
   239	            if !self.unproved_write {
   240	                let beyond = self.beyond_horizon;
   241	                let proved = self.device_work(|runner| runner.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row));
   242	                (self.beyond_horizon, self.missing_fact) = (beyond, None);
   243	                match proved { Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(_)) => self.unproved_write = true, other => other? }
   244	            }
   245	        }
   246	        // Retirement released every logical key and cap slot. Treat the new
   247	        // image as a fresh insert: an unchanged secondary key can now belong
   248	        // to another live row and must be probed again.
   249	        self.check_constraints(table_name, None, &row, Effect::Insert)?;
   250	        self.commit_sequences(table_name, &row)?;
   251	        self.commit_receipt_counter(table_name, &row)?;
   252	        let row = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, None, row, image_bytes)?;
   253	        validate_row(self.schema, table_name, &row)?;
   254	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   255	            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &row, None)
   256	        })?;
   257	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, None, Some(&row), entries)?;
   258	        self.row_changed(table_name, None, Some(&row), Origin::Source)?;
   259	        Ok(true)
   260	    }
   261	
   262	    pub(super) fn update(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   263	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   264	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   265	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   266	            ));
   267	        }
   268	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   269	            runner.update_attempt(table_name, key, patch)
   270	        })
   271	    }
   272	
   273	    fn update_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   274	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
   275	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &patch, false)?;
   276	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &patch)?;
   277	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &patch)?;
   278	        if patch.as_object()?.contains_key("id") {
   279	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} update patch cannot change id")));
   280	        }
   281	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   282	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &patch, false)?;
   283	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   284	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   285	        })? else {
   286	            return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]));
   287	        };
   288	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].sync.is_none() { return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])); }
   289	        let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   290	            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   291	        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
   292	        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;
   293	        self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &patch, copy)
   294	    }
   295	
   296	    pub(super) fn upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   297	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   298	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   299	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   300	            ));
   301	        }
   302	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   303	            runner.upsert_attempt(table_name, key, row)
   304	        })
   305	    }
   306	
   307	    fn upsert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   308	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   309	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &row, false)?;
   310	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &row)?;
   311	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &row)?;
   312	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   313	        if row.field("id")?.as_str()? != id {
   314	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} upsert row id must equal its key")));
   315	        }
   316	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &row, true)?;
   317	        match self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   318	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   319	        })? {
   320	            Some(old) => {
   321	                let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   322	                    && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   323	                let row = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, row, readable)?;
   324	                // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — an existing row receives a patch; omitted columns keep their values.
   325	                let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &row, readable)?;
   326	                self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &row, copy)
   327	            }
   328	            None if self.device && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])? =>
   329	            {
   330	                Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]))
   331	            }
   332	            None => self.insert_upsert(table_name, "byId", row),
   333	        }
   334	    }
   335	
   336	    pub(super) fn insert_upsert(&mut self, table_name: &str, addressed_index: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   337	        self.refuse_upsert_owned(table_name)?;
   338	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#5 — trusted fixture imports preserve the constraint layer.
   339	        if self.context.is_system() {
   340	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| match error {
   341	                RuntimeError::Input(message) => RuntimeError::Constraint(message),
   342	                other => other,
   343	            });
   344	        }
   345	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].through.is_some() {
   346	            // A read-through child's insert arm keeps the hidden-target word for every authority refusal.
   347	            return self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()).map_err(|e| match e {
   348	                RuntimeError::Rule {..} | RuntimeError::Input(_) => self.no_write_target(), other => other,
   349	            });
   350	        }
   351	        match self.insert_attempt(table_name, row, false, Some(addressed_index)).map(|_| ()) {
   352	            Err(RuntimeError::Input(_)) => Err(self.no_write_target()),
   353	            result => result,
   354	        }
   355	    }
   356	
   357	    fn replace(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   358	        self.authorize_update_fields(table_name, &old, &new, patch, readable)?;
   359	        self.replace_authorized(table_name, old, new, readable, patch, copy)
   360	    }
   361	
   362	    /// `copy` is the merged image's lawful price, charged again for an engine slot copy.
   363	    pub(super) fn replace_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value, new: Value, readable: bool, patch: &Value, copy: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   364	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;
   365	        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, patch, false)?;
   366	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, patch)?;
   367	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, patch)?;
   368	        self.authorize_fields(table_name, &old, patch)?;
   369	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   370	        for path in definition.columns.keys().filter(|field| {
   371	            definition.engine_field(field) && field.as_str() != crate::schema::through::DEADLINE
   372	        }) {
   373	            if old.field(path).ok() != new.field(path).ok() {
   374	                return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_RECORDED_FIELD", message: format!("engine replacement changed stored attribution at {table_name}.{path} (guide maintains)") } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   375	            }
   376	        }
   377	        let mut new = new;
   378	        self.schema.tables[table_name].recompute_deadline(&mut new)?;
   379	        // @ref LLP 3000.017#2.2 — extending life re-admits the new image.
   380	        if self.schema.tables[table_name].stamp_ephemeral(&mut new, self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?
   381	            && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &new)? {
   382	            return Err(if readable { RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.into(), effect: Effect::Update } } else { self.no_write_target() });
   383	        }
   384	        let new = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, new, Some(&old), (!readable).then_some(patch))?;
   385	        if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str())) { return Err(if readable { error } else { self.no_write_target() }); }
   386	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &new, Effect::Update)?;
   387	        let new = self.prepare_event_slots(table_name, Some(&old), new, copy)?;
   388	        // A predicting device keeps another owner's omitted private field as an omission.
   389	        super::validate::validate_projection(self.schema, table_name, &new, self.device.then_some(self.context.viewer.as_str()))?;
   390	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated");
   391	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   392	            runner.tx.put(table_name, table, &new, Some(&old))
   393	        })?;
   394	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), Some(&new), entries)?;
   395	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), Some(&new), Origin::Source)
   396	    }
   397	
   398	    pub(super) fn delete(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   399	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   400	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   401	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   402	            ));
   403	        }
   404	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| runner.delete_attempt(table_name, id))
   405	    }
   406	
   407	    fn delete_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, id: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   408	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   409	        self.refuse_receipt_scope_delete(table_name)?;
   410	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   411	        self.reserve_write_rules(table, &[Effect::Read, Effect::Delete])?;
   412	        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — delete prepays hidden contribution work before fetching its old image, with the same attempt lifetime as update.
   413	        self.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
   414	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   415	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   416	        })? else {
   417	            return Err(RuntimeError::Require { site: Some(self.statement_site.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".to_owned(), message: None });
   418	        };
   419	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — a delete that consults referencing rows needs read authority on its row first.
   420	        let readable =
   421	            !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)? && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   422	        if (self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some() || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name)) && !readable
   423	        {
   424	            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "read rule");
   425	            return Err(self.no_write_target());
   426	        }
   427	        if !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Delete, None, &old)? {
   428	            return Err(if readable {
   429	                RuntimeError::Rule { table: table_name.to_owned(), effect: Effect::Delete }
   430	            } else { self.no_write_target() });
   431	        }
   432	        self.delete_authorized(table_name, old)
   433	    }
   434	
   435	    pub(super) fn delete_authorized(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   436	        let old = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   437	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, &old)?;
   438	            // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — the actions may have changed the root (a maintained column mirrored from its children): remove its current image.
   439	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
   440	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id))?.unwrap_or(old)
   441	        } else { old };
   442	        self.delete_row(table_name, old)
   443	    }
   444	
   445	    /// A delete's own removal of one row, its rules already decided: receipt
   446	    /// membership, the read-through child probe, constraints, maintains and
   447	    /// the partition event. A referential cascade removes each row this way.
   448	    pub(super) fn delete_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   449	        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
   450	        self.receipt_member_removed(table_name, &old)?;
   451	        self.refuse_live_children(table_name,old.field("id")?)?;
   452	        self.check_constraints(table_name, Some(&old), &old, Effect::Delete)?;
   453	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   454	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, &old)
   455	        })?;
   456	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(&old), None, entries)?;
   457	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(&old), None, Origin::Source)
   458	    }
   459	
   460	    /// Remove a row the engine itself retires (an expired one): no rule and
   461	    /// no constraint stands between the engine and its own sweep, while
   462	    /// aggregates and partition events apply as for any delete.
   463	    pub(super) fn remove(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   464	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
   465	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   466	        let entries = self.maintain_scratch(self.contribution_heap(table), |runner| {
   467	            runner.tx.delete(table_name, table, old)
   468	        })?;
   469	        self.charge_source_indexes(table, Some(old), None, entries)?;
   470	        self.row_changed(table_name, Some(old), None, Origin::Source)
   471	    }
   472	
   473	    /// Physically retire one row whose upper lifetime ended. Expiry bypasses
   474	    /// the root's authored delete rule and constraints, but it does not bypass
   475	    /// the schema's declared effects on rows that reference the root. A
   476	    /// read-through child still retains the expired parent physically.
   477	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — expiry cleanup runs the same closure/restrict/set-null actions as an authored delete.
   478	    pub(super) fn retire_expired_row(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   479	        if self.physical_children(table_name, old.field("id")?)? { return Ok(false); }
   480	        let current = if self.schema.is_referenced(table_name) {
   481	            self.apply_reference_actions(table_name, old)?;
   482	            // A cascade may maintain a column on the root; delete its current
   483	            // physical image so index and cap entries match what is stored.
   484	            let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?;
   485	            self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))?
   486	                .unwrap_or_else(|| old.clone())
   487	        } else {
   488	            old.clone()
   489	        };
   490	        self.remove(table_name, &current)?;
   491	        Ok(true)
   492	    }
   493	
   494	    /// At a program commit's end, retire every source row the commit changed
   495	    /// or inserted whose lifetime has already ended: its final
   496	    /// image was never live at a commit boundary, so it leaves no row for a
   497	    /// later sweep to announce. Inside the commit the
   498	    /// row existed as written (an insert-then-update still works). Engine
   499	    /// bookkeeping, unmetered: the program's metering is already recorded.
   500	    /// Server execution and device prediction both run it so a predicted
   501	    /// final image cannot omit cascade, set-null or restrict effects. Its work,
   502	    /// returned, stays
   503	    /// linear in the rows retired: each aggregate row takes one net change
   504	    /// and each audience key is scanned for a live row once. Seeds and loads
   505	    /// ordinarily keep their rows for the sweep; row-keyed view sources use
   506	    /// `retire_seeded_view_sources` to preserve their count-basis contract.
   507	    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — a row whose lifetime ended by its own commit's end never exists at a commit boundary.
   508	    pub(crate) fn retire_expired_births(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   509	        let Some(now) = self.context.now else { return Ok(Default::default());
   510	        };
   511	        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#3 — an expired final image never grants a new recipient the row's id.
   512	        // The tracker covers synced and unsynced source tables alike. Each
   513	        // distinct entry prepaid its tree node, strings and this vector slot;
   514	        // the rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
   515	        // A row that existed before the commit and ends it already expired is
   516	        // retired too: accounted from the partitions it was in at the commit's
   517	        // start, it revokes there and announces nothing to a partition it only
   518	        // entered with its expiring image.
   519	        let mut changed: Vec<(String, String)> = std::mem::take(&mut self.expiry_rows).into_iter().collect();
   520	        if changed.is_empty() {
   521	            return Ok(Default::default());
   522	        }
   523	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   524	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   525	        changed.sort_by_key(|(name,id)| {
   526	            (std::cmp::Reverse(order.iter().position(|n| n == name)),id.clone(),
   527	            )
   528	        });
   529	        // Server execution already reserved this bookkeeping in the source
   530	        // writes. Device prediction instead runs the walk inside its separate
   531	        // bounded physical-work meter: exhausting that allowance queues the
   532	        // intent, never publishes a partial closure or refuses the write.
   533	        let meter = if self.device_work_active { None } else {
   534	            Some(std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort)))
   535	        };
   536	        self.retiring = Some(Default::default());
   537	        let retired = changed.iter().try_for_each(|(table_name, id)| {
   538	            let Some(row) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, id))? else { return Ok(());
   539	            };
   540	            let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   541	            if table.expired(&row, now) { self.retire_expired_row(table_name, &row).map(|_| ()) } else { Ok(()) }
   542	        });
   543	        let aggregates = self.retiring.take().map(|retiring| retiring.aggregates).unwrap_or_default();
   544	        let retired = retired.and_then(|()| self.apply_retired_aggregates(aggregates));
   545	        let work = meter.map(|meter| std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, meter).used).unwrap_or_default();
   546	        retired.map(|()| work)
   547	    }
   548	
   549	    /// Seed writes historically retire only already-expired sources of
   550	    /// row-keyed views. Keep that narrow boundary while routing their removal
   551	    /// through the common action and net-maintenance path.
   552	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.5 — ordinary expired fixtures remain stored; derived row-view sources cannot revive after clock rollback.
   553	    #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
   554	    pub(crate) fn retire_seeded_view_sources(&mut self) -> Result<crate::meter::Metered, RuntimeError> {
   555	        let schema = self.schema;
   556	        self.expiry_rows.retain(|(table, _)| schema.maintains.iter()
   557	            .any(|maintain| maintain.source == table.as_str() && maintain.row_key.is_some()));
   558	        self.retire_expired_births()
   559	    }
   560	
   561	    /// A column with a declared default takes it when the written row leaves
   562	    /// it out, before validation and before the asset facts, so the row the
   563	    /// rules and the constraints see is the complete one.
   564	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — omitted defaults use the clock and viewer of the host running the insert.
   565	    pub(super) fn with_defaults(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<Supplied, RuntimeError> {
   566	        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
   567	        if !table.defaults.keys().any(|name| {
   568	            row.as_object().is_ok_and(|fields| !fields.contains_key(name))
   569	        }) {
   570	            return Ok(row);
   571	        }
   572	        let row = row.defaults(table,self.context.now.ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Input("write clock is not pinned".into()))?,&self.context.viewer)?;
   573	        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
   574	        Ok(row)
   575	    }
   576	
   577	    /// An `image`/`video` column names an upload by id; the row carries the
   578	    /// facts the server established about it (type, bytes, dimensions,
   579	    /// duration), never the client's word for them. The upload must be the
   580	    /// writer's own and of the column's kind and size. The system principal
   581	    /// may name an asset that was never uploaded: a fixture's placeholder,
   582	    /// metadata only, never served.
   583	    // Web stores hold received asset facts, never the authoritative upload ledger.
   584	    #[cfg(not(feature = "sqlite"))]

    48	impl Schema {
    49	    /// Whether rows of `name` take part in referential actions, as child or
    50	    /// parent: an ordinary durable application table. Ephemeral rows, engine
    51	    /// derivations and receipt/timeline bookkeeping keep their own lifetimes.
    52	    pub fn actionable(&self, name: &str) -> bool {

    59	    /// Every reference into `parent` a delete consults (all but `keep`), in
    60	    /// (child, column) order.
    61	    pub fn referencing<'a>(&'a self, parent: &str) -> Vec<Referencing<'a>> {
    62	        // A plain loop into a vector: iterator adapters monomorphize per call site on the web device.
    63	        let mut out = Vec::new();
    64	        for (child, table) in &self.tables {
    65	            for (column, action) in &table.on_delete {
    66	                if action.acts() && matches!(table.columns.get(column).map(ColumnType::required), Some(ColumnType::Ref { table: target }) if target == parent) {
    67	                    out.push(Referencing { child, table, column, action: *action });
    68	                }
    69	            }
    70	        }
    71	        out
    72	    }

    83	        if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) {

    95	    /// The cap bounding a reference's children: `cap N by <column>` exactly,
    96	    /// or one when the reference itself is a plain unique key. A nullable
    97	    /// reference may have many nulls, but a parent delete probes one non-null
    98	    /// parent id, whose unique group still has at most one row.
    99	    pub fn reference_cap(&self, child: &str, column: &str) -> Option<u32> {
   100	        let table = self.table(child)?;
   101	        let declared = table.constraints.iter().find_map(|c| match c {
   102	            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.len() == 1 && by[0] == column => Some(*max),

   116	    /// actions, and the tables its actions read. A function of the schema, so

   118	    pub fn action_tables(&self, parent: &str) -> ActionTables {
   119	        let mut out = ActionTables::default();
   120	        let mut queue = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   121	        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
   122	        while let Some(table) = queue.pop() {
   123	            if !visited.insert(table.clone()) { continue; }
   124	            for r in self.referencing(&table) {

   154	    /// A table that reaches itself through cascade and `read through` edges.
   155	    pub fn deletion_cycle(&self) -> Option<String> {
   156	        fn visit<'a>(schema: &'a Schema, name: &'a str, path: &mut Vec<&'a str>, done: &mut BTreeSet<&'a str>) -> Option<String> {
   157	            if path.contains(&name) { return Some(name.to_owned()); }
   158	            if !done.insert(name) { return None; }
   159	            path.push(name);
   160	            for (child, _) in &schema.tables {
   161	                if schema.deletion_precedes(child, name) && let Some(cycle) = visit(schema, child, path, done) { return Some(cycle); }
   162	            }
   163	            path.pop();
   164	            None
   165	        }
   166	        let mut done = BTreeSet::new();
   167	        self.tables.keys().find_map(|name| if self.tables[name].on_delete.values().any(|a| *a == OnDelete::Cascade) || self.is_referenced(name) {
   168	            let mut path = Vec::new();
   169	            visit(self, name, &mut path, &mut done)
   170	        } else { None })
   171	    }

   178	    /// The most rows of each table one delete of a `parent` row can reach

   180	    /// edge multiplies by its cap, and edges into a table add up. `None` when
   181	    /// the cascade graph from `parent` is cyclic or a cascade lacks its cap.
   182	    pub fn closure_bounds(&self, parent: &str) -> Option<Vec<(String, u64)>> {
   183	        // Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.
   184	        let mut reach: Vec<String> = vec![parent.to_owned()];
   185	        let mut edges: Vec<(usize, usize, u64)> = Vec::new();
   186	        let mut at = 0;
   187	        while at < reach.len() {
   188	            let table = reach[at].clone();

   190	                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }

   195	            at += 1;
   196	        }
   197	        // Kahn's order over the reached cascade subgraph; a leftover table is a cycle.
   198	        let mut indegree = vec![0_usize; reach.len()];
   199	        for &(_, child, _) in &edges { indegree[child] += 1; }
   200	        let mut bounds = vec![0_u64; reach.len()];
   201	        bounds[0] = 1;
   202	        let mut ready: Vec<usize> = (0..reach.len()).filter(|&t| indegree[t] == 0).collect();

   225	    /// closure is unbounded (a cycle or a missing cap) or a written table has no

   247	                // identity from that table and then inspect one outside

   302	        price[2] = price[2].saturating_add(1);
   303	        // The closure's identities (table and id) are held until the last
   304	        // delete, with the root's and one page of child ids.
   305	        // A set-null group is gathered whole (at most its cap) before it is cleared.

   330	
   331	    // @ref LLP 3000.039#5.1 — two event images per priced row write, plus bounded keys and audience transitions, retained for the request lifetime.
   332	    fn retained_action_heap(&self, parent: &str, writes: u64) -> Option<u64> {
   333	        let mut per_write = 0;
   334	        for (table, _) in self.closure_bounds(parent)? {
   335	            for reference in self.referencing(&table) {
   336	                if reference.action.writes() {
   337	                    let events = self.write_reservation(reference.child)?.action_events?;
   338	                    per_write = per_write.max(events.heap_per_write);
   339	                }
   340	            }
   341	        }
   342	        Some(writes.saturating_mul(per_write))
   343	    }
   344	
   345	    /// One engine write (delete or set-null update) of a `table` row: fetch and
   346	    /// write it, its index entries (a `words(..)` index at its token bound), a
   347	    /// row copy, and the source-write price the engine exports for the table.
   348	    fn unit_write(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Price> {
   349	        let table = self.table(name)?;
   350	        let plan = self.write_reservation(name)?;
   351	        if plan.server_only { return None; }
   352	        let entries = table.indexes.values().map(|index| match index.word_component() {
   353	            Some((_, fields)) => fields.iter().filter_map(|f| table.columns.get(f)).map(|kind| match kind.required() {
   354	                ColumnType::Text { max } => u64::from(*max), _ => 0,
   355	            }).sum::<u64>().min(crate::words::MAX_TOKENS_PER_ROW as u64),
   356	            None => 1,
   357	        }).fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add);
   358	        let row = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(table);
   359	        // The row copy and every phase's heap are held together until the
   360	        // write's attempt ends (an asset phase beside a column recount): a sum.
   361	        let mut unit = [4 + 2 * entries, 2 * entries, 1, 1, row.saturating_mul(4), 0, 0];
   362	        for phase in 0..=reservations::VIEW_READ {
   363	            add(&mut unit, plan.price(phase));
   364	        }
   365	        // The lifetime hook reserves all child-table witnesses while source
   366	        // phases are still held. Device verification additionally holds the
   367	        // parent and a child scratch image; every host prices the same peak.
   368	        let mut lifetime = 0_u64;
   369	        let mut child_peak = 0_u64;
   370	        for (_, child, _) in self.children(name) {
   371	            let scratch = crate::engine::row_copy_ceiling(child).saturating_mul(3);
   372	            lifetime = lifetime.saturating_add(scratch);
   373	            child_peak = child_peak.max(scratch);
   374	        }
   375	        if lifetime > 0 { unit[4] = unit[4].saturating_add(lifetime).saturating_add(child_peak).saturating_add(row); }
   376	        Some(unit)
   377	    }
   378	}

   380	/// The tables a delete's actions may write or read (`Schema::action_tables`).
   381	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
   382	pub struct ActionTables {
   383	    pub written: BTreeSet<String>,
   384	    pub read: BTreeSet<String>,
   385	}
   386	
   387	/// Whether any rule of any table, or the child's own sync, reads `column` of
   388	/// `child` — directly, as a probe key or equality on `child`, or as a hop.
   389	fn carries_authority(schema: &Schema, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
   390	    fn term_reads(term: &RuleTerm, own: bool, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
   391	        match term {
   392	            RuleTerm::Field(f) | RuleTerm::OldField(f) | RuleTerm::NextField(f) => own && f == column,
   393	            RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => {
   394	                (own && term.reference_source().is_some_and(|(c, _)| c == column))
   395	                    || term.references().any(|(table, field)| table == child && field == column)
   396	            }
   397	            RuleTerm::Viewer | RuleTerm::Literal(_) => false,
   398	        }
   399	    }
   400	    fn rule_reads(schema: &Schema, rule: &RuleExpr, own: bool, child: &str, column: &str) -> bool {
   401	        match rule {
   402	            RuleExpr::Public { .. } | RuleExpr::Allow | RuleExpr::Deny => false,
   403	            RuleExpr::Eq(a, b) | RuleExpr::Ne(a, b) | RuleExpr::Compare(_, a, b) => term_reads(a, own, child, column) || term_reads(b, own, child, column),
   404	            RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| rule_reads(schema, item, own, child, column)),
   405	            RuleExpr::Not(inner) => rule_reads(schema, inner, own, child, column),
   406	            RuleExpr::Exists { table, index, key, equalities, .. } | RuleExpr::Created { table, index, key, equalities, .. } => {
   407	                let probes_column = table == child && (equalities.iter().any(|(field, _)| field == column)
   408	                    || schema.table(child).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|c| c == column)));
   409	                probes_column || key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_, t)| t)).any(|term| term_reads(term, own, child, column))
   410	            }
   411	        }
   412	    }
   413	    schema.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| {
   414	        let own = name == child;
   415	        [&table.rules.read, &table.rules.insert, &table.rules.update, &table.rules.delete].iter().any(|rule| rule_reads(schema, rule, own, child, column))
   416	            || table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key }
   417	                if (target == child && schema.table(child).and_then(|t| t.index(index)).is_some_and(|i| i.columns().iter().take(key.len()).any(|c| c == column)))
   418	                    || key.iter().any(|term| term_reads(term, own, child, column))))
   419	    })
   420	}

   422	/// Why `column` cannot be cleared by its parent's delete, if it cannot: a
   423	/// value that carries authority or meaning beyond "which parent this row has".
   424	// @ref LLP 3000.039#2.2 — set null never changes any rule's verdict, moves a row between audiences, or rewrites a fact resolved through the reference.
   425	pub fn set_null_refusal(schema: &Schema, name: &str, table: &Table, column: &str) -> Option<String> {
   426	    let audience = table.sync.as_ref().is_some_and(|sync| std::iter::once((&sync.audience, sync.horizon.as_ref()))
   427	        .chain(sync.also.iter().map(|arm| (&arm.audience, arm.horizon.as_ref())))
   428	        .any(|(audience, horizon)| match audience {
   429	        Audience::Public => false,
   430	        Audience::Column(c) => c == column,
   431	        Audience::Target { prefix, .. } => prefix.iter().any(|c| c == column),
   432	    } || horizon.is_some_and(|h| table.index(&h.by).is_some_and(|i| i.uses_column(column)))));
   433	    let maintained = schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.source == name && m.by.iter().any(|by| by.trim_start_matches('.').starts_with(&format!("{column}."))));
   434	    if !table.columns.get(column).is_some_and(ColumnType::is_optional) { Some("the reference is required; declare it optional (`?`) or choose cascade".into()) }
   435	    else if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == column) { Some("a read-through reference is required and immutable".into()) }
   436	    else if table.immutable_fields().any(|f| f == column) { Some("the column is immutable".into()) }
   437	    else if table.written_by.contains_key(column) { Some("the column is written by its field owner".into()) }
   438	    else if table.sequences.values().any(|p| p == column) { Some("a sequence counts within it".into()) }
   439	    else if table.recorded.values().any(|r| r.reference == column) || maintained { Some("a recorded or maintained path resolves through it".into()) }
   440	    else if carries_authority(schema, name, column) { Some("a rule reads it, so clearing it would change that rule's verdict; a reference that carries authority chooses cascade, restrict or keep".into()) }
   441	    else if audience { Some("the sync audience or horizon uses it, so clearing it would move the row between partitions".into()) }
   442	    else if table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::Cap { by, .. } if by.iter().any(|b| b == column) && by.len() != 1)) { Some(format!("a cap groups by it with other columns; its only cap is `cap N by {column}`")) }
   443	    else { None }
   444	}

   446	/// Why rows of `name` cannot be deleted or cleared by another row's delete.

   449	    if table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::AppendOnly)) { Some(format!("{name} is append only")) }
   450	    else if !table.written_by.is_empty() { Some(format!("{name} has field-owned (`written by`) columns, whose owners the schema singled out")) }
   451	    else if schema.maintains.iter().filter(|m| m.source == name || m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.table == name))
   452	        .flat_map(|m| [Some(m.target.as_str()), m.private.as_ref().map(|owner| owner.table.as_str())]).flatten()
   453	        .any(|destination| schema.table(destination).is_some_and(|t| t.sync.is_some() && t.written_by.values().any(|authority| !authority.audience))) {
   454	        Some(format!("{name}'s derived writes deliver private fields, whose recipient authorization has no fixed action price"))
   455	    }
   456	    else if schema.timeline_member(name) { Some(format!("a timeline orders {name}'s writes")) }
   457	    else if schema.maintains.iter().any(|m| m.row_key.as_ref().is_some_and(|k| k.table == name)) { Some(format!("{name} is a row-keyed view's member table, whose writes may recount a group outside any fixed price")) }

+### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
+
+Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
+64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
+`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
+The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
+identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
+adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
+address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
+
+The store metadata marker `maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` binds persisted
+aggregate targets to that function. Opening or adopting a store without the
+marker — including a 0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON
+of the group key — atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate
+target from its source rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic
+generation. A failure rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation
+together. Adoption advice counts that rebuild even when schema/program bytes
+are unchanged. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
+`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
+it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
+zero.
+
 ### 3.1 F1: maintained columns
 
 F1 is LLP 3000.007.001, unchanged. Its value here is ranking. With `likeCount`

-entry in one transaction. Deleting or expiring a never-opened row creates no

+expired. When the expiry is due, retirement removes the root and pending-opening
+entry and applies its declared `on delete cascade`, `set null` and `restrict`
+actions in one transaction (LLP 3000.039 §3). A live restrict child or physical
+read-through child may retain the root physically, but the expired root remains
+absent from all logical reads. Cleanup advances past such retained roots and
+preserves its bounded scan position across calls; cascade/set-null writes and
+the root removal either commit together or roll back together. The same action
+path governs a row born expired at commit and an expired predecessor retired
+for a same-id insertion, so neither inline cleanup path can create an orphan.
+

-**Expiry is not a delete.** A parent whose `expire at` passes is absent from
-that moment, and the sweep removes it physically; neither fires an action.
-A child of an expiring parent outlives it unless the child declares the same
-lifetime (`read through`, or its own `expire at`). The writes card says so.
+**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
+is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
+can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
+sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
+expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
+bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
+not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
+constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.
+
+A live `restrict` child keeps the expired root physically stored and the sweep
+continues to later due keys. The retained root remains logically unreadable.
+Short sweeps preserve a per-table scan continuation, so repeated bounded calls
+cannot restart forever at the same restricted or read-through-retained roots;
+after reaching the end they wrap for roots whose blockers were removed.
+Expired children are not live restrict witnesses, as in step 4. A read-through
+child remains the stricter physical exception because its stored image depends
+on its parent. Any error after an earlier cascade or set-null write rolls back
+the whole retirement transaction. A restricted root alone is an expected
+deferred cleanup, not an error for the sweep as a whole.

+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_META: &str = "maintained_id_version";
+pub const MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION: &str = "sha256-v1";

+/// The id of a maintained row is a fixed-size digest of its typed group key.

+#[test]
+fn maintained_identity_is_fixed_size_and_domain_separated() {
+    let short = maintained_id(&[Value::String("x".into())]);

+    assert_eq!(short.len(), 64);
+    assert_eq!(long.len(), 64);

+#[test]
+fn missing_identity_marker_rebuilds_a_principal_reference_and_max_text_group() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table parents:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  owner: principal\n  parent: parents\n  token: text <=64\n  amount: int\n  public\nview totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    let owner = format!("user:{}", "o".repeat(59));
+    let parent = "p".repeat(64);
+    let token = "t".repeat(64);
+    assert_eq!((owner.len(), parent.len(), token.len()), (64, 64, 64));
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("owner", Value::Id(owner.clone())),
+            ("parent", Value::Id(parent.clone())), ("token", Value::String(token.clone())), ("amount", Value::Int(7))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(owner), Value::Id(parent), Value::String(token)]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    let after = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(7));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn identity_redeployment_rebuilds_the_ungrouped_empty_tuple() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  public\nview total: count entries\n  public\n";
+    let initial = compile(SOURCE);
+    let mut e = Engine::new_at(Store::memory().unwrap(), initial.schema, initial.programs, 0).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into()))]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[]);
+    let before = e.store().rows("total").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(before.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("$global").unwrap(), &Value::Bool(true));
+    assert_eq!(before[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    assert_eq!(preview(&mut e, &next.schema).aggregate_rows, 1);
+    let generation = e.generation();
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    assert!(e.generation() > generation);
+    let after = e.store().rows("total").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(after.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("id").unwrap(), &Value::Id(expected));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("$global").unwrap(), &Value::Bool(true));
+    assert_eq!(after[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+}

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_capability_upgrades_legacy_wire_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let schema = compile("table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n");
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    // A pre-migration stored schema may already have a carrier for unrelated
+    // capabilities. Decode it once, then stamp the digest identity capability
+    // on every newly published schema/projection.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap();
+    assert!(encoded.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}
+

+    // Server expiry is a physical retirement with the schema's declared
+    // referential effects. Devices receive that one committed closure just as
+    // they receive an authored parent delete.
+    let expiring = r#"
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public 'parents'
+  sync public
+table cascadeChildren:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  public 'cascadeChildren'
+  sync public
+table nullableChildren:
+  parent: parents ? on delete set null
+  public 'nullableChildren'
+  sync public
+"#;
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(expiring);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("parents".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeChildren".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c")), ("parent", id("p"))])),
+        ("nullableChildren".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("n")), ("parent", id("p"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("expiry-actions", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 0);
+    let from = d.state().unwrap().0;
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 100).unwrap(), 1);
+    d.apply(&stream_page(&mut e, "alice", from), false).unwrap();
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeChildren").is_empty());
+    let nullable = d.store().raw_rows("nullableChildren");
+    assert_eq!(nullable.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(nullable[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+    host.close("expiry-actions", d);
+
     // Every referencing group is public and held: the cascade predicts, deleting the held tasks.
     let (mut e, b) = compile(PUBLIC);
     assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "setup", "alice", &[]), "ok");
@@ -173,6 +209,55 @@ mutation drop(id: parents):
     host.close("retained-cascade", d);
 }
 
+#[test]
+fn authoritative_memory_sweeps_resume_and_wrap_past_restricted_roots() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut store = snapback4_device::memory::MemoryStore::new();
+    store.activate_server_at(bound.schema, 0).unwrap();
+    store.seed_server_at([
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "continuation reaches the free root within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(store.raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(store.raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("root").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+
+    // The cursor is after z. A lower new key is found after the scan wraps;
+    // each restricted root still consumes one bounded visit.
+    store.seed_server_at([("roots".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+        ("id", id("aa-free")), ("expiresAt", snapback4_core::Value::Int(10)),
+    ]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let wrapped_removed: u64 = (0..4).map(|_| store.sweep_server_at(10, 1).unwrap()).sum();
+    assert_eq!(wrapped_removed, 1, "a wrapped scan reaches the new lower key within one bounded turn per due root");
+    assert!(!store.raw_rows("roots").iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("aa-free")));
+}
+
 #[test] fn reference_actions_memory() { run(&mut Memory::new()); }
 #[test] fn reference_actions_sqlite() { run(&mut Sqlite::new("reference-actions")); }
 
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..05a91f6ddf
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-sim/tests/expiry_reference_actions.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,140 @@
+//! Expiry is a physical delete trigger for referential actions (LLP 3000.039
+//! §3). These cases cover scheduled cleanup, commit-end retirement and
+//! same-id replacement of an expired row against the real engine.
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState, value::object};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+fn id(value: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(value.into()) }
+
+fn engine(source: &str) -> Engine {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap()
+}
+
+const SWEEP: &str = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'cascade kids'
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  root: roots
+  public 'blockers'
+  sync public
+"#;
+
+#[test]
+fn sweep_applies_every_action_and_advances_past_a_restricted_root() {
+    let mut e = engine(SWEEP);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("a-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("b-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("c-blocked")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("z-free")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("ca")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nz")), ("root", id("z-free"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("ba")), ("root", id("a-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bb")), ("root", id("b-blocked"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("bc")), ("root", id("c-blocked"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    for expected in [0, 0, 0, 1] {
+        assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 1).unwrap(), expected, "a one-row sweep must advance its physical scan position");
+    }
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["a-blocked", "b-blocked", "c-blocked"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().iter().map(|r| r.field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["ca"]);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    for blocker in ["ba", "bb", "bc"] { e.seed_delete("blockers", blocker).unwrap(); }
+    assert_eq!(e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap(), 3);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn a_late_cascade_refusal_rolls_back_earlier_set_null_writes() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  public 'roots'
+table nullableKids:
+  root: roots ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'nullable kids'
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by root
+  public 'children'
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children
+  read through .child
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("n")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+        ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+
+    let error = e.sweep_expired(10, 10).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", "{error:?}");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &id("p"), "the prior set-null write rolled back");
+    for table in ["roots", "children", "grandchildren"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn commit_retirement_and_expired_same_id_replacement_apply_actions() {
+    let source = format!(r#"{SWEEP}
+mutation bornExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'born', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert cascadeKids {{id: 'born-c', root: 'born'}}
+  insert nullableKids {{id: 'born-n', root: 'born'}}
+  return null
+mutation bornRestricted():
+  insert roots {{id: 'blocked', expiresAt: now}}
+  insert blockers {{id: 'blocked-b', root: 'blocked'}}
+  return null
+mutation replaceExpired():
+  insert roots {{id: 'old', expiresAt: null}}
+  return null
+"#);
+    let mut e = engine(&source);
+    let sent = e.mutate("bornExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("root").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+
+    let refused = e.mutate("bornRestricted", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().is_empty(), "the refused birth and its blocker roll back together");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("blockers").unwrap().is_empty());
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(1))])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("old-c")), ("root", id("old"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replaceExpired", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("expiresAt").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty(), "same-id cleanup cannot orphan the expired predecessor's child");
+}
diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c6754a981f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4/tests/aggregate_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+//! A store written by the frozen 0.4.28 binary adopts digest-addressed
+//! aggregate rows before the current engine serves it.
+use rusqlite::Connection;
+use std::{
+    fs,
+    path::{Path, PathBuf},
+    process::Command,
+};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"use personas alice
+table entries:
+  group: text <=256
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .group
+  public
+mutation add(group: text <=256, amount: int):
+  insert entries {group, amount}
+query total(group: text <=256):
+  return totals[group]
+"#;
+
+struct Temp(PathBuf);
+impl Temp {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "snapback4-maintained-id-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            std::time::SystemTime::now()
+                .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+                .unwrap()
+                .as_nanos()
+        ));
+        fs::create_dir_all(path.join("snapback")).unwrap();
+        fs::write(path.join("snapback/schema.q"), SOURCE).unwrap();
+        Self(path)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Temp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);
+    }
+}
+
+fn aggregate_id(store: &Path) -> String {
+    Connection::open(store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT r.id FROM r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t WHERE c.name='totals'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+}
+
+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires frozen 0.4.28 binary via SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN"]
+fn a_0_4_28_store_rebuilds_legacy_aggregate_ids_and_fences_old_devices() {
+    let baseline = PathBuf::from(
+        std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN")
+            .expect("set SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN to the frozen 0.4.28 snapback4 binary"),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        baseline.is_file(),
+        "SNAPBACK4_BASELINE_BIN is not a file: {}",
+        baseline.display()
+    );
+    let version = Command::new(&baseline).arg("--version").output().unwrap();
+    assert!(version.status.success());
+    assert!(
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).contains("0.4.28"),
+        "unexpected baseline: {:?}",
+        version
+    );
+
+    let dir = Temp::new();
+    let group = "x".repeat(200);
+    let args = serde_json::json!({"group": group, "amount": 7}).to_string();
+    let written = Command::new(&baseline)
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args(["run", "add", &args, "--as", "alice", "--now", "1", "--json"])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        written.status.success(),
+        "{}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&written.stderr)
+    );
+    let store = dir.0.join(".snapback4/store.sqlite");
+    let legacy = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert!(
+        legacy.len() > snapback4_core::rows::MAX_ID_BYTES,
+        "the frozen binary must have written the oversized legacy address"
+    );
+    let before: u64 = Connection::open(&store)
+        .unwrap()
+        .query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let opened = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_snapback4"))
+        .current_dir(&dir.0)
+        .args([
+            "run",
+            "total",
+            &serde_json::json!({"group": group}).to_string(),
+            "--as",
+            "alice",
+            "--now",
+            "2",
+            "--json",
+        ])
+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        opened.status.success(),
+        "stdout={} stderr={}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stdout),
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&opened.stderr)
+    );
+    let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&opened.stdout).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(answer["data"]["value"], 7, "{answer}");
+
+    let digest = aggregate_id(&store);
+    assert_eq!(digest.len(), 64);
+    assert_ne!(digest, legacy);
+    let conn = Connection::open(&store).unwrap();
+    let (after, marker): (u64, String) = (
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='generation'",
+            [],
+            |row| row.get::<_, String>(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap()
+        .parse()
+        .unwrap(),
+        conn.query_row(
+            "SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+            [snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+            |row| row.get(0),
+        )
+        .unwrap(),
+    );
+    assert!(
+        after > before,
+        "identity adoption must publish a new device generation"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(marker, snapback4_core::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION);
+
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), SOURCE.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let required =
+        snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&bound.schema.public_projection());
+    assert!(
+        required
+            .capabilities
+            .contains(&"maintained-id-sha256-v1".to_owned())
+    );
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities
+        .retain(|capability| capability != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(
+        refusal.message.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1"),
+        "{refusal:?}"
+    );
+}

+#[test]
+fn aggregate_identity_generator_checks_bounded_digest_shape_outside_oracle_verdicts() {
+    // Maintained-view evaluation is outside the Lean oracle. Exercise its
+    // physical identity as an explicit generator invariant, so these cases
+    // cannot be counted as oracle passes merely because they are unsupported.
+    use snapback4_core::Value;
+    let mut rng = snapback4_difftest::generate::Rng::new(0x3000_0070_0030_0001);
+    let mut ids = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
+    for n in 0..256 {
+        let key = if n == 0 {
+            vec![]
+        } else {
+            let principal = format!("p{:063}", rng.next());
+            let reference = format!("r{:063}", rng.next());
+            let len = rng.pick(65) as usize;
+            let token = format!("{:016x}", rng.next()).repeat(4)[..len].to_owned();
+            vec![Value::Id(principal), Value::Id(reference), Value::String(token),
+                 Value::Int((rng.next() & ((1 << 53) - 1)) as i64)]
+        };
+        let id = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        assert_eq!(id.len(), 64, "seeded case {n}: {key:?}");
+        assert!(id.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_hexdigit() && !byte.is_ascii_uppercase()));
+        assert!(snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(&id));
+        assert_eq!(id, snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key));
+        assert!(ids.insert(id), "unexpected digest collision in generated corpus");
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn generated_composite_aggregate_groups_keep_fixed_digest_identities() {
+    let source = r#"table parents:
+  insert <- allow
+  read <- allow
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  parent: parents
+  token: text <=64
+  amount: int
+  insert <- allow
+  read <- allow
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token
+  read <- allow
+mutation add(row: id, owner: principal, parent: parents, token: text <=64):
+  insert entries {id: row, owner, parent, token, amount: 1}
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    let principal = "p".repeat(64);
+    let parent = "r".repeat(64);
+    e.seed([("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id(parent.clone()))]))]).unwrap();
+    for n in 0..32 {
+        let token = format!("{n:02}{}", "x".repeat(62));
+        let result = e.mutate("add", None, Context::new(&principal, BTreeMap::from([
+            ("row".into(), Value::Id(format!("e{n}"))),
+            ("owner".into(), Value::Id(principal.clone())),
+            ("parent".into(), Value::Id(parent.clone())),
+            ("token".into(), Value::String(token)),
+        ]))).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(result.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{result:?}");
+    }
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 32);
+    for row in rows {
+        let Value::Id(id) = row.field("id").unwrap() else { panic!("aggregate id") };
+        assert_eq!(id.len(), 64);
+        assert!(snapback4_core::value::identity_fits(id));
+        assert_eq!(id, &snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&[
+            row.field("owner").unwrap().clone(), row.field("parent").unwrap().clone(),
+            row.field("token").unwrap().clone(),
+        ]));
+    }
+}

--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+import Quarry.Store
+
+/-!
+# Maintained aggregate identity
+
+The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
+tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
+cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
+store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
+lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
+and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
+identity while publishing the new version.
+-/
+
+namespace Quarry
+
+/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
+migration. -/
+def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
+
+/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
+not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
+to this logical model. -/
+def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
+  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
+    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
+    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
+
+theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
+  simp [maintainedIdV1]
+
+/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
+byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
+theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
+  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
+  omega
+
+def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
+  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
+
+structure MaintainedState where
+  version : Nat
+  rows : List Row
+
+/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
+identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
+states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
+def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
+    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
+  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
+example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
+  maintainedIdV1_length _
+
+end Quarry
