+#[test]
+fn legacy_aggregate_identity_migrates_dormant_references_before_restore() {
+    const BASE: &str = "table entries:\n  n: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .n\n  public\n";
+    const WITH_SAVED: &str = "table entries:\n  n: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .n\n  public\ntable saved:\n  target: totals\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = engine(WITH_SAVED);
+    seed(&mut e, "entries", serde_json::json!({"id":"e","n":7}));
+    let digest = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap()[0].field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
+    seed(&mut e, "saved", serde_json::json!({"id":"s","target":digest}));
+
+    // Model a release-store row written by 0.4.28, before digest identities.
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = e.schema().tables["totals"].clone();
+    let saved = e.schema().tables["saved"].clone();
+    let old_target = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap().remove(0);
+    let old_saved = e.store().rows("saved").unwrap().remove(0);
+    let mut legacy_target = old_target.clone();
+    let mut legacy_saved = old_saved.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy_target { fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone())); }
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy_saved { fields.insert("target".into(), Value::Id(legacy)); }
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("saved", &saved, &old_saved).unwrap();
+    tx.put("saved", &saved, &legacy_saved, None).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old_target).unwrap();
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &legacy_target, None).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    // Removing `saved` retains it outside the active namespace while the
+    // aggregate target remains active. Identity adoption must rewrite both
+    // the hidden row and its dormant-reference ledger before setting marker.
+    activate(&mut e, BASE, 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    activate(&mut e, WITH_SAVED, 3).unwrap();
+    let restored = e.store().rows("saved").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(restored.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(restored[0].field("target").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest));
+}

+    /// Seed imports historically do not enforce every final-exists clause.
+    /// Capture only clauses that currently hold so seeded expiry retirement
+    /// can prove that its own reference actions did not invalidate them.
+    pub(super) fn satisfied_final_exists(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<FinalExistsWitness>, RuntimeError> {
+        let inserted = self.inserted.clone();
+        let mut witnesses = Vec::new();
+        for (table, row) in inserted {
+            let constraints = self.schema.table(&table).expect("validated").constraints.clone();
+            for (constraint, clause) in constraints.iter().enumerate() {
+                if matches!(clause, Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { .. })
+                    && self.final_exists_holds(&table, &row, clause)? {
+                    witnesses.push(FinalExistsWitness { table: table.clone(), row: row.clone(), constraint });
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(witnesses)
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn check_final_exists_witnesses(&mut self, witnesses: &[FinalExistsWitness]) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
+        for witness in witnesses {
+            let constraint = self.schema.table(&witness.table).expect("validated")
+                .constraints.get(witness.constraint).expect("captured constraint").clone();
+            if !self.final_exists_holds(&witness.table, &witness.row, &constraint)? {
+                return Err(Self::final_exists_refusal(&witness.table, &constraint));
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }

 insert without predicted rows and lets the server retire any predecessor and

+Prediction also runs commit-end retirement for every row the mutation inserts
+or updates into an already-expired final image, before final-exists clauses.
+With complete reference-group coverage it publishes the same cascade and
+set-null changes or the same restrict refusal as the server. Missing coverage,
+retained history or another uncertain witness queues the whole mutation with
+no predicted rows. An unreferenced expiring row still retires locally at commit
+end; expiry alone does not force an otherwise provable mutation online. The
+retirement and its schema-fixed action reservation draw from the device's
+separate bounded physical-work allowance. Exhausting it queues and rolls back
+the prediction; it cannot publish a partial closure or become a server refusal.
+
 Any schema in which an expiring table is referenced requires device capability
 `expiry-reference-actions-v1`. A pre-Wave-12 stored schema may open on the
 server for transactional adoption and is restamped when published, but an old

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/tests/reference_actions.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/tests/reference_actions.rs

@@ -210,6 +210,126 @@ mutation replace(id: id):
     assert!(d.store().raw_rows("children").is_empty());
     host.close("expiry-same-id-replacement", d);
 
+    // Commit-end retirement is part of device prediction too. With complete
+    // public coverage, updating a parent to an already-ended lifetime applies
+    // the same cascade and set-null closure as the server. A child born earlier
+    // in the same mutation belongs to that closure as well.
+    let predicted_expiry = r#"
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  parent: parents ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  parent: parents on delete restrict
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  sync public
+mutation expire(parent: parents):
+  update parents[parent] { until: now }
+  insert cascadeKids { id: 'born', parent }
+"#;
+    let row = |table: &str, fields: &[(&str, snapback4_core::Value)]|
+        (table.to_owned(), snapback4_core::value::object(fields.iter().cloned()));
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(predicted_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([
+        row("parents", &[("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))]),
+        row("cascadeKids", &[("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+        row("nullableKids", &[("id", id("nullable")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-expiry-actions", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let predicted = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p"}), 100, vec![], 1);
+    assert!(predicted.is_ok(), "{}: {predicted:?}", host.label());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty(), "the old and same-mutation children cascade");
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("parent", id("p"))]), "ok");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("parents").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Null);
+    host.close("predicted-expiry-actions", d);
+
+    // The device charges the schema's worst-case closure before walking it.
+    // A large declared cap therefore queues even when this particular store
+    // contains only the child this mutation just inserted; no unbounded
+    // commit-end walk can escape the prediction allowance.
+    let bounded_expiry = predicted_expiry.replace("cap 4 by parent", "cap 1024 by parent");
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(&bounded_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([row("parents", &[("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))])], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-expiry-bounded", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let queued = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(queued.code(), "E_PREDICT", "{}: {queued:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("parents")[0].field("until").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Int(200));
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeKids").is_empty(), "queued prediction rolls back its new child");
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("parent", id("p"))]), "ok");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("parents").unwrap().is_empty());
+    host.close("predicted-expiry-bounded", d);
+
+    // A complete restrict witness refuses locally and rolls back the parent
+    // update plus the child inserted before commit-end retirement.
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(predicted_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([
+        row("parents", &[("id", id("p")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))]),
+        row("cascadeKids", &[("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+        row("nullableKids", &[("id", id("nullable")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+        row("blockers", &[("id", id("blocker")), ("parent", id("p"))]),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-expiry-restrict", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let refused = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refused.code(), "E_REFERENCED", "{}: {refused:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("parents")[0].field("until").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Int(200));
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("cascadeKids").len(), 1, "the same-mutation child rolls back");
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("nullableKids")[0].field("parent").unwrap(), &id("p"));
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("parent", id("p"))]), "E_REFERENCED");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("parents").unwrap()[0].field("until").unwrap(), &snapback4_core::Value::Int(200));
+    host.close("predicted-expiry-restrict", d);
+
+    // Expiry itself does not force an online round trip. An unreferenced row
+    // can be updated or born already expired and disappear in the prediction.
+    let plain_expiry = r#"
+table notes:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+mutation expire(note: notes):
+  update notes[note] { until: now }
+mutation createExpired():
+  insert notes { id: 'born', until: now }
+"#;
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(plain_expiry);
+    e.seed_at([row("notes", &[("id", id("note")), ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(200))])], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut d = host.open("predicted-plain-expiry", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, "alice", 100);
+    let predicted = d.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"note":"note"}), 100, vec![], 1);
+    assert!(predicted.is_ok(), "{}: {predicted:?}", host.label());
+    assert!(d.store().raw_rows("notes").is_empty());
+    d.withdraw(&[]).unwrap();
+    let predicted = d.predict("createExpired", "alice", &json!({}), 100, vec![], 2);
+    assert!(predicted.is_ok(), "{}: {predicted:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("notes").len(), 1, "withdrawing the first prediction restores its live base row");
+    assert_eq!(d.store().raw_rows("notes")[0].field("id").unwrap(), &id("note"));
+    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "expire", "alice", &[("note", id("note"))]), "ok");
+    assert!(e.store().rows("notes").unwrap().is_empty());
+    host.close("predicted-plain-expiry", d);
+

+//! Generated device/server parity for commit-end lifetime retirement. Each
+//! source runs through the public sync wire and both device stores, so an
+//! offline prediction cannot silently omit a cascade, set-null or restrict
+//! action performed by the server.
+
+#[path = "../../snapback4-device/tests/common/mod.rs"]
+mod device_common;
+
+use device_common::{
+    BoundaryMetadata, Host, Memory, Sqlite, args, compile, id, snapshot_pages, stream_page,
+};
+use serde_json::json;
+use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Value, WriteState};
+use snapback4_device::device::Device;
+
+const NOW: i64 = 4_000_000_000_000;
+const GENERATED_SOURCES: usize = 18;
+const GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES: usize = 9;
+const RUNTIME_CASES: usize = GENERATED_SOURCES * 2;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+enum Action {
+    Cascade,
+    SetNull,
+    Restrict,
+}
+
+impl Action {
+    fn word(self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::Cascade => "cascade",
+            Self::SetNull => "set null",
+            Self::Restrict => "restrict",
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn optional(self) -> &'static str {
+        if matches!(self, Self::SetNull) {
+            " ?"
+        } else {
+            ""
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+enum Prelude {
+    Snapshot,
+    Stream,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
+enum Target {
+    ExpiredWithInbound,
+    FutureWithInbound,
+    ExpiredWithoutInbound,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+enum IncompleteCoverage {
+    MissingChild,
+    AudienceHidden,
+    PartiallyAcquired,
+}
+
+impl Target {
+    fn has_inbound(self) -> bool {
+        !matches!(self, Self::ExpiredWithoutInbound)
+    }
+
+    fn requested_expiry(self) -> i64 {
+        if matches!(self, Self::FutureWithInbound) {
+            NOW + 10_000
+        } else {
+            NOW
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
+struct Generated {
+    seed: u64,
+    action: Action,
+    prelude: Prelude,
+    target: Target,
+    viewer: &'static str,
+    decoys: usize,
+    source: String,
+}
+
+fn generated_sources() -> Vec<Generated> {
+    let mut generated = Vec::new();
+    let mut seed = 0_u64;
+    for action in [Action::Cascade, Action::SetNull, Action::Restrict] {
+        for target in [
+            Target::ExpiredWithInbound,
+            Target::FutureWithInbound,
+            Target::ExpiredWithoutInbound,
+        ] {
+            for prelude in [Prelude::Snapshot, Prelude::Stream] {
+                let viewer = ["alice", "bob", "carol"][(seed as usize) % 3];
+                let decoys = 1 + (seed as usize % 2);
+                let cap = decoys + 2;
+                let source = format!(
+                    r#"use personas alice, bob, carol
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  token: int
+  expire at .until
+  public 'generated expiry parents seed {seed}'
+  insert <- allow
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table children:
+  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}
+  marker: int
+  cap {cap} by parent
+  public 'generated expiry children seed {seed}'
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+mutation addChild(id: id, parent: parents, marker: int):
+  insert children {{ id, parent, marker }}
+mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
+  update parents[parent] {{ until }}
+"#,
+                    optional = action.optional(),
+                    action = action.word(),
+                );
+                generated.push(Generated {
+                    seed,
+                    action,
+                    prelude,
+                    target,
+                    viewer,
+                    decoys,
+                    source,
+                });
+                seed += 1;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(generated.len(), GENERATED_SOURCES);
+    generated
+}
+
+fn row(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'static str, Value)>) -> Value {
+    snapback4_core::value::object(fields)
+}
+
+fn target_parent() -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id("target")),
+        ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 5_000)),
+        ("token", Value::Int(7)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn target_child(seed: u64) -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id("target-child")),
+        ("parent", id("target")),
+        ("marker", Value::Int(seed as i64)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn decoy_parent(index: usize) -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id(&format!("decoy-parent-{index}"))),
+        ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 20_000 + index as i64)),
+        ("token", Value::Int(100 + index as i64)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn decoy_child(index: usize) -> Value {
+    row([
+        ("id", id(&format!("decoy-child-{index}"))),
+        ("parent", id(&format!("decoy-parent-{index}"))),
+        ("marker", Value::Int(200 + index as i64)),
+    ])
+}
+
+fn seed_rows(case: &Generated) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
+    let mut rows = vec![("parents".to_owned(), target_parent())];
+    for index in 0..case.decoys {
+        rows.push(("parents".to_owned(), decoy_parent(index)));
+        let streamed_decoy =
+            matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Stream) && !case.target.has_inbound() && index == 0;
+        if !streamed_decoy {
+            rows.push(("children".to_owned(), decoy_child(index)));
+        }
+    }
+    if case.target.has_inbound() && matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Snapshot) {
+        rows.push(("children".to_owned(), target_child(case.seed)));
+    }
+    rows
+}
+
+fn canonical(rows: Vec<Value>) -> Vec<String> {
+    let mut rows = rows
+        .into_iter()
+        .map(|row| {
+            let mut row = snapback4_core::wire::to_json(&row);
+            // `pending` is device settlement metadata, not an authored field;
+            // parity below compares the predicted data image with the server's
+            // committed data image.
+            if let Some(object) = row.as_object_mut() {
+                object.remove("pending");
+            }
+            serde_json::to_string(&row).unwrap()
+        })
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    rows.sort();
+    rows
+}
+
+fn device_rows<S: BoundaryMetadata>(device: &Device<S>, table: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
+    device.store().raw_rows(table)
+}
+
+fn server_rows(server: &Engine, table: &str) -> Vec<Value> {
+    server.store().rows(table).unwrap()
+}
+
+fn row_by_id<'a>(rows: &'a [Value], wanted: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
+    rows.iter()
+        .find(|row| row.field("id").ok() == Some(&id(wanted)))
+}
+
+fn apply_snapshot<S: BoundaryMetadata>(
+    server: &mut Engine,
+    device: &mut Device<S>,
+    viewer: &str,
+) -> (u64, usize) {
+    let pages = snapshot_pages(server, viewer, 2);
+    let watermark = pages.last().expect("a snapshot has a final page").watermark;
+    for (index, page) in pages.iter().enumerate() {
+        device.apply(page, index == 0).unwrap();
+    }
+    (watermark, pages.len())
+}
+
+fn server_write(
+    server: &mut Engine,
+    op: &str,
+    viewer: &str,
+    values: &[(&str, Value)],
+    now: i64,
+) -> Result<(), String> {
+    let outcome = server
+        .mutate(op, None, Context::new(viewer, args(values)).at(now))
+        .unwrap();
+    match outcome.state {
+        WriteState::Sent { .. } => Ok(()),
+        WriteState::Failed { why, .. } => Err(why.code),
+    }
+}
+
+fn prelude<S: BoundaryMetadata>(
+    case: &Generated,
+    server: &mut Engine,
+    device: &mut Device<S>,
+) -> (usize, usize) {
+    let (watermark, snapshot_count) = apply_snapshot(server, device, case.viewer);
+    let mut stream_count = 0;
+    if matches!(case.prelude, Prelude::Stream) {
+        let (child, parent, marker) = if case.target.has_inbound() {
+            (
+                "target-child".to_owned(),
+                "target".to_owned(),
+                case.seed as i64,
+            )
+        } else {
+            ("decoy-child-0".to_owned(), "decoy-parent-0".to_owned(), 200)
+        };
+        server_write(
+            server,
+            "addChild",
+            case.viewer,
+            &[
+                ("id", id(&child)),
+                ("parent", id(&parent)),
+                ("marker", Value::Int(marker)),
+            ],
+            NOW - 1,
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+        device
+            .apply(&stream_page(server, case.viewer, watermark), false)
+            .unwrap();
+        stream_count += 1;
+    }
+
+    for table in ["parents", "children"] {
+        assert_eq!(
+            canonical(device_rows(device, table)),
+            canonical(server_rows(server, table)),
+            "seed {} {:?}/{:?}: prelude sync differs for {table}",
+            case.seed,
+            case.action,
+            case.prelude,
+        );
+    }
+    (snapshot_count, stream_count)
+}
+
+fn assert_expected<S: BoundaryMetadata>(case: &Generated, server: &Engine, device: &Device<S>) {
+    let device_parents = device_rows(device, "parents");
+    let device_children = device_rows(device, "children");
+    let server_parents = server_rows(server, "parents");
+    let server_children = server_rows(server, "children");
+    let label = format!(
+        "seed {} {:?}/{:?}/{:?}",
+        case.seed, case.action, case.target, case.prelude
+    );
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_parents.clone()),
+        canonical(server_parents.clone()),
+        "{label}: parent parity"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_children.clone()),
+        canonical(server_children.clone()),
+        "{label}: child parity"
+    );
+
+    let target_parent = row_by_id(&device_parents, "target");
+    let target_child = row_by_id(&device_children, "target-child");
+    match (case.action, case.target) {
+        (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
+            let parent = target_parent.expect("restrict refusal preserves its parent");
+            assert_eq!(
+                parent.field("until").unwrap(),
+                &Value::Int(NOW + 5_000),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+            assert_eq!(
+                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
+                Some(&id("target")),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+        }
+        (_, Target::FutureWithInbound) => {
+            let parent = target_parent.expect("future expiry preserves its parent");
+            assert_eq!(
+                parent.field("until").unwrap(),
+                &Value::Int(NOW + 10_000),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+            assert_eq!(
+                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
+                Some(&id("target")),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+        }
+        (Action::Cascade, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
+            assert!(target_parent.is_none(), "{label}: expired parent retires");
+            assert!(target_child.is_none(), "{label}: cascade retires the child");
+        }
+        (Action::SetNull, Target::ExpiredWithInbound) => {
+            assert!(target_parent.is_none(), "{label}: expired parent retires");
+            assert_eq!(
+                target_child.map(|row| row.field("parent").unwrap()),
+                Some(&Value::Null),
+                "{label}"
+            );
+        }
+        (_, Target::ExpiredWithoutInbound) => {
+            assert!(
+                target_parent.is_none(),
+                "{label}: an unreferenced expired parent retires"
+            );
+            assert!(
+                target_child.is_none(),
+                "{label}: the source generated no inbound reference"
+            );
+        }
+    }
+
+    let target_remains = matches!(case.target, Target::FutureWithInbound)
+        || matches!(
+            (case.action, case.target),
+            (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound)
+        );
+    assert_eq!(
+        device_parents.len(),
+        case.decoys + if target_remains { 1 } else { 0 },
+        "{label}: every decoy parent remains and only the expected target image survives"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        device_children
+            .iter()
+            .filter(|row| row.field("id").ok() != Some(&id("target-child")))
+            .count(),
+        case.decoys,
+        "{label}: every unrelated child remains",
+    );
+}
+
+fn run_case<H: Host>(host: &mut H, case: &Generated) -> (usize, usize) {
+    let (mut server, backend) = compile(&case.source);
+    server.seed_at(seed_rows(case), NOW - 100).unwrap();
+    let store_name = format!("w12-expiry-generated-{}", case.seed);
+    let mut device = host.open(&store_name, Some(backend)).unwrap();
+    let counts = prelude(case, &mut server, &mut device);
+    let input = json!({"parent":"target", "until":case.target.requested_expiry()});
+    let predicted = device.predict("setExpiry", case.viewer, &input, NOW, vec![], 1);
+    let committed = server_write(
+        &mut server,
+        "setExpiry",
+        case.viewer,
+        &[
+            ("parent", id("target")),
+            ("until", Value::Int(case.target.requested_expiry())),
+        ],
+        NOW,
+    );
+
+    if matches!(
+        (case.action, case.target),
+        (Action::Restrict, Target::ExpiredWithInbound)
+    ) {
+        assert_eq!(
+            predicted.unwrap_err().code(),
+            "E_REFERENCED",
+            "seed {} {}",
+            case.seed,
+            host.label()
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            committed.unwrap_err(),
+            "E_REFERENCED",
+            "seed {} {}",
+            case.seed,
+            host.label()
+        );
+    } else {
+        assert!(
+            predicted.is_ok(),
+            "seed {} {}: {predicted:?}",
+            case.seed,
+            host.label()
+        );
+        assert_eq!(committed, Ok(()), "seed {} {}", case.seed, host.label());
+    }
+    assert_expected(case, &server, &device);
+    host.close(&store_name, device);
+    counts
+}
+
+fn incomplete_source(seed: u64, action: Action) -> String {
+    let cap = 3 + seed as usize % 2;
+    format!(
+        r#"use personas alice, bob, carol
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public 'incomplete expiry parents seed {seed}'
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table children:
+  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}
+  owner: principal
+  cap {cap} by parent
+  read <- .owner = viewer
+  insert <- .owner = viewer
+  sync to .owner
+mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
+  update parents[parent] {{ until }}
+"#,
+        optional = action.optional(),
+        action = action.word(),
+    )
+}
+
+fn incomplete_rows(mode: IncompleteCoverage, viewer: &str) -> Vec<(String, Value)> {
+    let mut rows = vec![(
+        "parents".to_owned(),
+        row([("id", id("target")), ("until", Value::Int(NOW + 5_000))]),
+    )];
+    let hidden = if viewer == "alice" { "bob" } else { "alice" };
+    if matches!(
+        mode,
+        IncompleteCoverage::AudienceHidden | IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired
+    ) {
+        rows.push((
+            "children".to_owned(),
+            row([
+                ("id", id("hidden")),
+                ("parent", id("target")),
+                ("owner", id(hidden)),
+            ]),
+        ));
+    }
+    if matches!(mode, IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired) {
+        rows.push((
+            "children".to_owned(),
+            row([
+                ("id", id("visible")),
+                ("parent", id("target")),
+                ("owner", id(viewer)),
+            ]),
+        ));
+    }
+    rows
+}
+
+fn run_incomplete_case<H: Host>(
+    host: &mut H,
+    seed: u64,
+    action: Action,
+    mode: IncompleteCoverage,
+) -> usize {
+    let source = incomplete_source(seed, action);
+    let (mut server, backend) = compile(&source);
+    let viewer = ["alice", "bob", "carol"][(seed as usize) % 3];
+    server
+        .seed_at(incomplete_rows(mode, viewer), NOW - 100)
+        .unwrap();
+    let store_name = format!("w12-expiry-incomplete-{seed}");
+    let mut device = host.open(&store_name, Some(backend)).unwrap();
+    let (_, pages) = apply_snapshot(&mut server, &mut device, viewer);
+    let parents_before = canonical(device_rows(&device, "parents"));
+    let children_before = canonical(device_rows(&device, "children"));
+
+    let predicted = device
+        .predict(
+            "setExpiry",
+            viewer,
+            &json!({"parent":"target", "until":NOW}),
+            NOW,
+            vec![],
+            1,
+        )
+        .unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(
+        predicted.code(),
+        "E_PREDICT",
+        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?} {} must queue an unprovable action group",
+        host.label()
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_rows(&device, "parents")),
+        parents_before,
+        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}: a queued mutation changes no parent"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        canonical(device_rows(&device, "children")),
+        children_before,
+        "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}: a queued mutation changes no visible child"
+    );
+
+    let committed = server_write(
+        &mut server,
+        "setExpiry",
+        viewer,
+        &[("parent", id("target")), ("until", Value::Int(NOW))],
+        NOW,
+    );
+    let has_child = mode != IncompleteCoverage::MissingChild;
+    if matches!(action, Action::Restrict) && has_child {
+        assert_eq!(
+            committed,
+            Err("E_REFERENCED".to_owned()),
+            "seed {seed} {mode:?}"
+        );
+        assert!(row_by_id(&server_rows(&server, "parents"), "target").is_some());
+    } else {
+        assert_eq!(committed, Ok(()), "seed {seed} {action:?}/{mode:?}");
+        assert!(row_by_id(&server_rows(&server, "parents"), "target").is_none());
+        let children = server_rows(&server, "children");
+        match action {
+            Action::Cascade => assert!(children.is_empty(), "seed {seed} {mode:?}"),
+            Action::SetNull => assert!(
+                children
+                    .iter()
+                    .all(|row| row.field("parent").ok() == Some(&Value::Null)),
+                "seed {seed} {mode:?}"
+            ),
+            Action::Restrict => assert!(
+                children.is_empty(),
+                "the missing-child control has no child"
+            ),
+        }
+    }
+    host.close(&store_name, device);
+    pages
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn generated_commit_end_expiry_actions_match_server_on_both_device_stores() {
+    let generated = generated_sources();
+    let mut memory = Memory::new();
+    let mut sqlite = Sqlite::new("w12-expiry-generated");
+    let mut runtime_cases = 0;
+    let mut snapshot_pages_seen = 0;
+    let mut stream_pages_seen = 0;
+    for case in &generated {
+        for counts in [run_case(&mut memory, case), run_case(&mut sqlite, case)] {
+            runtime_cases += 1;
+            snapshot_pages_seen += counts.0;
+            stream_pages_seen += counts.1;
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(runtime_cases, RUNTIME_CASES);
+    assert_eq!(
+        stream_pages_seen, 18,
+        "nine stream-prelude sources run on two stores"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        snapshot_pages_seen >= runtime_cases,
+        "every runtime starts from a real public-sync snapshot"
+    );
+    println!(
+        "generated {GENERATED_SOURCES} sources; {runtime_cases} Memory/SQLite cases; {snapshot_pages_seen} snapshot pages; {stream_pages_seen} prelude stream pages; 72 independently asserted target outcomes"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn generated_incomplete_action_groups_queue_without_predicted_rows() {
+    let mut memory = Memory::new();
+    let mut sqlite = Sqlite::new("w12-expiry-incomplete");
+    let mut seed = 100_u64;
+    let mut sources = 0;
+    let mut runtime_cases = 0;
+    let mut snapshot_pages_seen = 0;
+    for action in [Action::Cascade, Action::SetNull, Action::Restrict] {
+        for mode in [
+            IncompleteCoverage::MissingChild,
+            IncompleteCoverage::AudienceHidden,
+            IncompleteCoverage::PartiallyAcquired,
+        ] {
+            snapshot_pages_seen += run_incomplete_case(&mut memory, seed, action, mode);
+            snapshot_pages_seen += run_incomplete_case(&mut sqlite, seed, action, mode);
+            sources += 1;
+            runtime_cases += 2;
+            seed += 1;
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(sources, GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES);
+    assert_eq!(runtime_cases, GENERATED_NEGATIVE_SOURCES * 2);
+    assert!(snapshot_pages_seen >= runtime_cases);
+    println!(
+        "generated {sources} incomplete-coverage sources; {runtime_cases} Memory/SQLite queue cases; {snapshot_pages_seen} snapshot pages; all 18 device outcomes were exact E_PREDICT with zero local changes"
+    );
+}

---

diff --git a/snapback4/packages/snapback4/test/expiry-reference-actions.test.mjs b/snapback4/packages/snapback4/test/expiry-reference-actions.test.mjs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..d1466c8854
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/packages/snapback4/test/expiry-reference-actions.test.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+import test from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { webDevice, memoryPersistence } from '../dist/web.js';
+import { server } from './helpers/app-server.mjs';
+import { hangBudget } from './helpers/wait.mjs';
+
+const wasm = readFileSync(new URL('../src/wasm/snapback4_device_bg.wasm', import.meta.url));
+const now = 4_000_000_000_000;
+const future = now + 10_000;
+const viewer = 'dev:alice';
+const source = `use personas alice, bob
+table groups:
+  total: count aggregateKids by .group
+  public
+  sync public
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table cascadeKids:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+table nullableKids:
+  parent: parents ? on delete set null
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  sync public
+table blockers:
+  parent: parents on delete restrict
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  sync public
+table aggregateKids:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  group: groups
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+table privateParents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table privateKids:
+  parent: privateParents on delete cascade
+  owner: principal
+  cap 4 by parent
+  read <- .owner = viewer
+  sync to .owner
+mutation setExpiry(parent: parents, until: time):
+  update parents[parent] { until }
+mutation expireWithChild(parent: parents):
+  insert cascadeKids { id: 'same-mutation-child', parent }
+  update parents[parent] { until: 0 }
+mutation expireAggregate(parent: parents, group: groups):
+  insert aggregateKids { id: 'aggregate-born', parent, group }
+  update parents[parent] { until: 0 }
+mutation expirePrivate(parent: privateParents):
+  update privateParents[parent] { until: 0 }
+query parent(id: id):
+  return parents[id]
+query cascadeKid(id: id):
+  return cascadeKids[id]
+query nullableKid(id: id):
+  return nullableKids[id]
+query blocker(id: id):
+  return blockers[id]
+query aggregateKid(id: id):
+  return aggregateKids[id]
+query privateParent(id: id):
+  return privateParents[id]
+query group(id: id):
+  return groups[id] { total }
+`;
+
+const ok = result => {
+  assert.equal(result.denied, undefined, JSON.stringify(result));
+  return result.ok;
+};
+const denied = result => result.denied ?? result.ok?.denied;
+const authored = value => {
+  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(authored);
+  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
+  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).filter(([key]) => key !== 'pending').map(([key, item]) => [key, authored(item)]));
+};
+
+test('wasm predicts commit-end expiry actions exactly like the server', { timeout: hangBudget(20) }, async t => {
+  const host = await server(t, undefined, source);
+  const headers = { 'x-snapback-persona': 'alice', 'content-type': 'application/json' };
+  const post = async (path, body) => {
+    const response = await fetch(host.url + path, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(hangBudget()) });
+    const answer = await response.json();
+    assert.equal(response.status, 200, JSON.stringify(answer));
+    return answer;
+  };
+  const parent = id => ({ table: 'parents', row: { id, until: future } });
+  const rows = [
+    { table: 'groups', row: { id: 'g' } },
+    ...['cascade', 'nullable', 'restrict', 'same', 'empty', 'aggregate', 'future'].map(parent),
+    { table: 'cascadeKids', row: { id: 'cascade-child', parent: 'cascade' } },
+    { table: 'nullableKids', row: { id: 'nullable-child', parent: 'nullable' } },
+    { table: 'blockers', row: { id: 'blocker', parent: 'restrict' } },
+    { table: 'aggregateKids', row: { id: 'aggregate-old', parent: 'aggregate', group: 'g' } },
+    { table: 'privateParents', row: { id: 'private', until: future } },
+    { table: 'privateKids', row: { id: 'hidden', parent: 'private', owner: 'dev:bob' } },
+  ];
+  assert.equal((await post('/seed', rows)).seeded, rows.length);
+
+  const backendResponse = await fetch(host.url + '/schema', { headers });
+  assert.equal(backendResponse.status, 200);
+  const backend = await backendResponse.json();
+  const opener = webDevice({ wasm, persist: memoryPersistence() });
+  const core = await opener.open('expiry-reference-actions', backend);
+  t.after(() => core.close());
+  const engine = await opener.engineInfo();
+  const snapshot = await fetch(host.url + '/sync', {
+    method: 'POST',
+    headers: { ...headers, 'x-snapback-device': JSON.stringify(engine) },
+    body: JSON.stringify({ generation: backend.generation, from: 0, limit: 1000, after: null, stream: false, pending: [] }),
+    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(hangBudget()),
+  }).then(response => response.json());
+  assert.equal(snapshot.snapshot, true, JSON.stringify(snapshot));
+  assert.equal(snapshot.more, false, JSON.stringify(snapshot));
+  ok(await core.call({ op: 'apply', first: true, page: snapshot }));
+
+  const local = async (name, args) => authored(ok(await core.call({ op: 'query', name, viewer, args, now })).data);
+  const online = async (name, args) => authored((await post(`/q/${name}`, { args })).data);
+  const predict = async (name, args) => core.call({ op: 'predict', name, viewer, args, now, newIds: [], entropy: 7 });
+  const mutate = (name, args, id) => post(`/m/${name}`, { id, args });
+  const parity = async (name, args) => assert.deepEqual(await local(name, args), await online(name, args), `${name} parity`);
+
+  assert.deepEqual(await local('group', { id: 'g' }), { total: 1 }, 'the snapshot carries the confirmed aggregate');
+  assert.deepEqual(
+    await local('aggregateKid', { id: 'aggregate-old' }),
+    { id: 'aggregate-old', parent: 'aggregate', group: 'g' },
+    'the complete snapshot carries the old child that commit-end retirement must cascade',
+  );
+
+  assert.equal((await predict('setExpiry', { parent: 'cascade', until: 0 })).denied, undefined);
+  assert.equal((await mutate('setExpiry', { parent: 'cascade', until: 0 }, 'server-cascade')).state, 'sent');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'cascade' });
+  await parity('cascadeKid', { id: 'cascade-child' });
+  assert.equal(await local('parent', { id: 'cascade' }), null);
+  assert.equal(await local('cascadeKid', { id: 'cascade-child' }), null);
+
+  assert.equal((await predict('setExpiry', { parent: 'nullable', until: 0 })).denied, undefined);
+  assert.equal((await mutate('setExpiry', { parent: 'nullable', until: 0 }, 'server-nullable')).state, 'sent');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'nullable' });
+  await parity('nullableKid', { id: 'nullable-child' });
+  assert.equal((await local('nullableKid', { id: 'nullable-child' })).parent, null);
+
+  const restricted = await predict('setExpiry', { parent: 'restrict', until: 0 });
+  assert.equal(denied(restricted)?.code, 'E_REFERENCED', JSON.stringify(restricted));
+  const serverRestricted = await mutate('setExpiry', { parent: 'restrict', until: 0 }, 'server-restrict');
+  assert.equal(serverRestricted.state, 'failed', JSON.stringify(serverRestricted));
+  assert.equal(serverRestricted.why.code, 'E_REFERENCED');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'restrict' });
+  await parity('blocker', { id: 'blocker' });
+
+  assert.equal((await predict('expireWithChild', { parent: 'same' })).denied, undefined);
+  assert.equal((await mutate('expireWithChild', { parent: 'same' }, 'server-same')).state, 'sent');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'same' });
+  await parity('cascadeKid', { id: 'same-mutation-child' });
+  assert.equal(await local('cascadeKid', { id: 'same-mutation-child' }), null);
+
+  assert.equal((await predict('setExpiry', { parent: 'empty', until: 0 })).denied, undefined);
+  assert.equal((await mutate('setExpiry', { parent: 'empty', until: 0 }, 'server-empty')).state, 'sent');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'empty' });
+  assert.equal(await local('parent', { id: 'empty' }), null);
+
+  assert.deepEqual(await local('group', { id: 'g' }), { total: 1 });
+  assert.equal((await predict('expireAggregate', { parent: 'aggregate', group: 'g' })).denied, undefined);
+  assert.equal((await mutate('expireAggregate', { parent: 'aggregate', group: 'g' }, 'server-aggregate')).state, 'sent');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'aggregate' });
+  await parity('aggregateKid', { id: 'aggregate-old' });
+  await parity('aggregateKid', { id: 'aggregate-born' });
+  await parity('group', { id: 'g' });
+  assert.deepEqual(await local('group', { id: 'g' }), { total: 0 }, 'logless wasm nets +1 then -2 to the committed aggregate delta -1');
+
+  assert.equal((await predict('setExpiry', { parent: 'future', until: future })).denied, undefined);
+  assert.equal((await mutate('setExpiry', { parent: 'future', until: future }, 'server-future')).state, 'sent');
+  await parity('parent', { id: 'future' });
+  assert.equal((await local('parent', { id: 'future' })).until, future);
+
+  const queued = ok(await core.call({ op: 'admit', entry: {
+    id: 'private-expiry', seq: 1, op: 'expirePrivate', args: { parent: 'private' }, viewer, now,
+    new_ids: [], predicted: [], predictable: true,
+  } }));
+  assert.equal(queued.predictable, false, JSON.stringify(queued));
+  assert.deepEqual(queued.predicted, []);
+  assert.notEqual(await local('privateParent', { id: 'private' }), null, 'queued incomplete coverage publishes no parent change');
+  assert.equal((await mutate('expirePrivate', { parent: 'private' }, 'server-private')).state, 'sent', 'the server sees and cascades the hidden child');
+});

+The same boundary applies when an authored delete or commit-end expiry action
+writes a source of a maintained column. Even if the device holds the complete
+reference closure, it queues the whole mutation with no predicted rows; the
+public projection cannot derive the private total. Server settlement and the
+following stream or snapshot publish the child action and mirrored parent
+value together. Actions whose written sources feed no maintained column remain
+eligible for prediction under their ordinary coverage and meter proofs.
+

-- The Postgres evaluation store has no activation API: no adoption parity is claimed.
+- The Postgres evaluation store has no general activation API. Its open-time
+  maintained-identity upgrade is nevertheless an atomic generation barrier for
+  the narrow read-through maintained-column form it admits: it rebuilds the
+  private target under the digest identity, then mirrors every live parent,
+  before publishing the identity marker and generation. Other activation
+  parity remains unclaimed.

@@ -719,6 +719,15 @@ end; expiry alone does not force an otherwise provable mutation online. The
 retirement and its schema-fixed action reservation draw from the device's
 separate bounded physical-work allowance. Exhausting it queues and rolls back
 the prediction; it cannot publish a partial closure or become a server refusal.
+The reservation prepays closure scans and writes, but it does not make device-
+only completeness, authority or lifetime proofs unbounded: nested proofs keep
+spending that same separate allowance while the closure's prepaid meter is
+active. If any action-written source feeds a private maintained column, the
+device also queues before changing a row. Its projection retains the fixed
+price but deliberately omits the private maintain, so only server settlement
+can supply both the action and the authoritative mirrored total. This applies
+to authored deletes and commit-end expiry alike; a closure with no such source

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/tests/expiry_maintained_columns.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/tests/expiry_maintained_columns.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..a897b02634
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/tests/expiry_maintained_columns.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+//! Expiry actions whose child writes feed a private maintained column must
+//! settle on the server: the public device schema has the price but not the
+//! private derivation that computes the new total (LLP 3000.007.001 §3.7).
+mod common;
+use common::*;
+use serde_json::json;
+use snapback4_core::{Context, WriteState, value::{Value, object}};
+use snapback4_device::{device::{Device, StreamPage}, store::DeviceStore};
+
+const SOURCE: &str = r#"
+table groups:
+  total: count children by .group
+  public
+  sync public
+table parents:
+  until: time
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+  sync public
+table children:
+  parent: parents on delete cascade
+  group: groups
+  cap 4 by parent
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+  sync public
+mutation expire(parent: parents, group: groups):
+  insert children { id: 'born', parent, group }
+  update parents[parent] { until: 0 }
+query group(id: groups):
+  return groups[id] { total }
+"#;
+
+fn acquire<S: DeviceStore>(engine: &mut snapback4_core::Engine, device: &mut Device<S>) {
+    let mut after = None;
+    let mut first = true;
+    loop {
+        let page = engine.snapshot_acquisition_page_at("alice", after.as_deref(), 100, 100).unwrap();
+        let next = page.next.map(|next| next.encode());
+        let page: StreamPage = serde_json::from_value(json!({
+            "snapshot":true, "after":after, "held":page.held, "acquisitions":page.acquisitions,
+            "events":page.events.iter().map(|event| json!({"table":event.table,"kind":event.kind.word(),"id":event.id,
+                "data":event.data.as_ref().map(snapback4_core::wire::to_json)})).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
+            "watermark":page.watermark, "more":next.is_some(), "next":next, "generation":engine.generation(),
+        })).unwrap();
+        device.apply(&page, first).unwrap();
+        let Some(next) = next else { break };
+        after = Some(next);
+        first = false;
+    }
+}
+
+fn run<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
+    let (mut server, backend) = compile(SOURCE);
+    server.seed_at([
+        ("groups".into(), object([("id", id("g"))])),
+        ("parents".into(), object([("id", id("p")), ("until", Value::Int(200))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("old")), ("parent", id("p")), ("group", id("g"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let mut device = host.open("expiry-maintained-column", Some(backend)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut server, &mut device);
+    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(1))]));
+
+    let error = device.predict("expire", "alice", &json!({"parent":"p","group":"g"}), 100, vec![], 1).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_PREDICT", "{}: {error:?}", host.label());
+    assert_eq!(device.store().raw_rows("parents").len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(device.store().raw_rows("children").len(), 1, "queued prediction publishes neither birth nor cascade");
+    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(1))]));
+
+    let from = server.seq().unwrap();
+    let outcome = server.mutate("expire", None, Context::new("alice", args(&[("parent", id("p")), ("group", id("g"))])).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(outcome.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{outcome:?}");
+    device.apply(&stream_page(&mut server, "alice", from), false).unwrap();
+    assert!(device.store().raw_rows("parents").is_empty());
+    assert!(device.store().raw_rows("children").is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(device.query("group", "alice", &json!({"id":"g"}), 100).unwrap().data, object([("total", Value::Int(0))]));
+    host.close("expiry-maintained-column", device);
+}
+
+#[test] fn expiry_maintained_column_memory() { run(&mut Memory::new()); }
+#[test] fn expiry_maintained_column_sqlite() { run(&mut Sqlite::new("expiry-maintained-column")); }

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Wave12DeviceQueue.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+/-!
+# Wave 12 device-queue contract witnesses
+
+This module is an independent, abstract contract witness for the device queue
+boundary. It is deliberately not part of `Quarry.Eval`, and it does not claim
+that the Lean row oracle models device prediction, sync, maintained-column
+projection, or the production meter.
+
+The first witness gives two server worlds with the same public rows and the
+same confirmed maintained total. Their withheld maintained predicates differ,
+so retiring the same parent produces different authoritative totals. No
+point-valued function of the public observation can be right in both worlds;
+queueing preserves the confirmed image until server catch-up.
+
+The second witness models only the law of the separate device physical-work
+allowance: nested work consumes the remainder from earlier work. Resetting the
+allowance between nested proofs would accept costs 2 and 3 under a limit of 4,
+while sequential consumption queues the second proof.
+-/
+
+namespace Quarry.Wave12DeviceQueue
+
+-- @ref LLP 3000.039#64-devices-and-prediction — private maintains and nested proof work queue when public device state cannot decide them within one allowance.
+
+inductive Kind where
+  | a
+  | b
+  deriving DecidableEq
+
+structure SourceRow where
+  id : Nat
+  parent : Nat
+  kind : Kind
+  deriving DecidableEq
+
+structure PublicRow where
+  id : Nat
+  parent : Nat
+  deriving DecidableEq
+
+structure PrivateWorld where
+  rows : List SourceRow
+  counted : Kind
+
+def publicProjection (rows : List SourceRow) : List PublicRow :=
+  rows.map fun row => ⟨row.id, row.parent⟩
+
+def total (world : PrivateWorld) : Nat :=
+  (world.rows.filter fun row => row.kind == world.counted).length
+
+def retireParent (parent : Nat) (world : PrivateWorld) : PrivateWorld :=
+  { world with rows := world.rows.filter fun row => row.parent != parent }
+
+def rows : List SourceRow := [
+  { id := 10, parent := 1, kind := .a },
+  { id := 20, parent := 2, kind := .b }
+]
+
+def countsA : PrivateWorld := ⟨rows, .a⟩
+def countsB : PrivateWorld := ⟨rows, .b⟩
+
+def confirmedTotal : Nat := 1
+
+def publicObservation (world : PrivateWorld) : List PublicRow × Nat :=
+  (publicProjection world.rows, confirmedTotal)
+
+example : publicObservation countsA = publicObservation countsB := rfl
+example : total countsA = confirmedTotal := rfl
+example : total countsB = confirmedTotal := rfl
+example : total (retireParent 1 countsA) = 0 := rfl
+example : total (retireParent 1 countsB) = 1 := rfl
+
+/-- A device point-predictor sees only public rows and the confirmed total. -/
+abbrev PointPredictor := List PublicRow → Nat → Nat
+
+/-- The indistinguishable worlds require different post-retirement totals, so
+one public point prediction cannot be authoritative in both. -/
+theorem projection_queues
+    (predict : PointPredictor) :
+    predict (publicProjection rows) confirmedTotal ≠ total (retireParent 1 countsA) ∨
+      predict (publicProjection rows) confirmedTotal ≠ total (retireParent 1 countsB) := by
+  have hA : total (retireParent 1 countsA) = 0 := rfl
+  have hB : total (retireParent 1 countsB) = 1 := rfl
+  rw [hA, hB]
+  omega
+
+inductive Decision where
+  | point (value : Nat)
+  | queue
+  deriving DecidableEq
+
+def soundFor (decision : Decision) (world : PrivateWorld) : Prop :=
+  match decision with
+  | .point value => value = total (retireParent 1 world)
+  | .queue => True
+
+theorem queue_is_sound_for_both_worlds :
+    soundFor .queue countsA ∧ soundFor .queue countsB := by
+  simp [soundFor]
+
+theorem no_point_is_sound_for_both_worlds (value : Nat) :
+    ¬ (soundFor (.point value) countsA ∧ soundFor (.point value) countsB) := by
+  simp [soundFor, countsA, countsB, rows, total, retireParent]
+  omega
+
+/-- Queueing publishes no speculative replacement for the confirmed image. -/
+def presentedTotal (confirmed : Nat) : Decision → Nat
+  | .point value => value
+  | .queue => confirmed
+
+example : presentedTotal confirmedTotal .queue = 1 := rfl
+
+/-- Spend `cost` from the remaining physical-work allowance. -/
+def spend (remaining cost : Nat) : Option Nat :=
+  if cost ≤ remaining then some (remaining - cost) else none
+
+theorem nested_spends_fit
+    {initial first second afterFirst afterSecond : Nat}
+    (hFirst : spend initial first = some afterFirst)
+    (hSecond : spend afterFirst second = some afterSecond) :
+    first + second ≤ initial := by
+  simp [spend] at hFirst hSecond
+  omega
+
+def nestedDecision (initial first second : Nat) : Decision :=
+  match spend initial first with
+  | none => .queue
+  | some remaining =>
+      match spend remaining second with
+      | none => .queue
+      | some _ => .point confirmedTotal
+
+/-- Resetting to the initial allowance between nested proofs would accept both
+individual costs even though their sum exceeds the request allowance. -/
+def resetWouldAccept (initial first second : Nat) : Bool :=
+  first ≤ initial && second ≤ initial
+
+example : resetWouldAccept 4 2 3 = true := rfl
+example : 4 < 2 + 3 := by decide
+example : nestedDecision 4 2 3 = .queue := rfl
+example : nestedDecision 5 2 3 = .point confirmedTotal := rfl
+
+end Quarry.Wave12DeviceQueue

@@ -170,6 +170,21 @@ target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
 Removing the aggregate itself retires its derived target rows; a dormant
 reference to that retired target receives no map and keeps the ordinary
 restore refusal against acquiring a newly created parent lifetime.
+
+Persisted `sequence by` custody is part of the same identity migration even
+when no allocating row, source row, or aggregate target row survives. Adoption
+decodes canonical legacy counter ids with the predecessor aggregate's typed
+group definition, recursively settles any aggregate-reference components, and
+re-keys `_sequences(parent, id, value)` through the resulting target-specific
+map. If legacy and digest keys both exist, their maximum high-water value wins;
+the legacy key is removed and an exhausted counter remains exhausted. Counters
+for other parent tables and legacy strings that do not decode as a canonical
+group tuple stay opaque. A predecessor aggregate removed by the candidate is
+normalized before the current identity marker publishes, so later
+reintroduction cannot revive legacy custody under that marker. Counter rewrites
+and their rollback share the adoption transaction with row-reference rewrites,
+target rebuilds, marker and generation.
+
 Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
 the same transaction. A legacy target address is itself the predecessor's
 canonical logical group tuple. Adoption decodes it using the predecessor

   `E_SEQUENCE_SUPPLIED`. The column is immutable by construction.
+  Counter custody survives deletion of the allocating row and its parent row.
+  When aggregate parent identities adopt a new representation, the same atomic
+  adoption re-keys retained counters by parent table and typed logical group,
+  recursively translating aggregate-reference components. Colliding legacy
+  and current keys keep their maximum high-water value, the legacy key is
+  removed, and exhaustion remains exhaustion. Adoption failure rolls the
+  counter translation back with the rest of the generation.

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+type LegacyIdentities = Vec<(String, Vec<(String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>)>)>;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+type LegacyIdentityMap = BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>>>;
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &Value,
+    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
+    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
+) {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(old)) => {
+            let Some(kinds) = definitions.get(table) else { return };
+            if identities.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(old)) { return; }
+            let Some(values) = crate::json_codec::from_text::<Vec<Value>>(old).ok()
+                .filter(|values| values.len() == kinds.len()) else { return };
+            let key: Vec<_> = kinds.iter().cloned().zip(values).collect();
+            identities.entry(table.clone()).or_default().insert(old.clone(), key.clone());
+            for (kind, value) in &key {
+                collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
+            }
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) =>
+            collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(inner, value, definitions, identities),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            for value in values { collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(of, value, definitions, identities); },
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn insert_sequence_identity(
+    target: &str,
+    old: String,
+    key: Vec<(crate::schema::ColumnType, Value)>,
+    definitions: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<crate::schema::ColumnType>>,
+    identities: &mut LegacyIdentityMap,
+) {
+    if identities.get(target).is_some_and(|ids| ids.contains_key(&old)) { return; }
+    identities.entry(target.to_owned()).or_default().insert(old, key.clone());
+    for (kind, value) in &key {
+        collect_sequence_identity_dependencies(kind, value, definitions, identities);
+    }
+}

+fn settle_legacy_maintained_ids(
+    legacy: &LegacyIdentities,
+    base: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,

+    let identity_count = legacy.iter().map(|(_, rows)| rows.len()).sum::<usize>();
+    for _ in 0..=identity_count.saturating_add(1) {

+#[test]
+fn identity_adoption_rekeys_sequence_history_without_reusing_deleted_ordinals() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .bucket\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  total: totals\n  ordinal: sequence by total\n  unique total, ordinal\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e7".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))])),
+        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e9".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(9))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let digest7 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let digest9 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(9)]);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("gone".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
+        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    e.seed_delete("sequenced", "gone").unwrap();
+
+    let legacy7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy9 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(9)]);
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let entries = schema.tables["entries"].clone();
+    let sequenced = schema.tables["sequenced"].clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest7).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &tx.get("totals", &digest9).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("entries", &entries, &tx.get("entries", "e9").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("sequenced", "kept").unwrap().unwrap();
+    let mut next = old.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+        fields.insert("total".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("sequenced", &sequenced, &next, Some(&old)).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy7, 7).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest7, 4).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy9, crate::value::I53_MAX).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest9, 12).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("ordinary", &legacy7, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy7).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy9).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest7).unwrap(), 7, "the deleted allocating row and lower destination counter cannot lower the high-water mark");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("ordinary", &legacy7).unwrap(), 11, "translation is scoped by parent table and id");
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    let kept = e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().pop().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(kept.field("total").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest7.clone()));
+    assert_eq!(kept.field("ordinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(2));
+
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7))]))], 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().into_iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("next".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
+    let error = e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("full".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest9.clone()))]))], 2).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(error.refusal().code, "E_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED");
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX, "overflow refusal must not change the migrated counter");
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+    const WITHOUT_AGGREGATE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    e.seed_at([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(3))]))], 0).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(3)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(3)]);
+    let target = e.schema().tables["totals"].clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy, 5).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let removed = compile(WITHOUT_AGGREGATE);
+    e.adopt_at(removed.schema, removed.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 5);
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+
+    let restored = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(restored.schema, restored.programs, 2).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest))]))], 3).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap()[0].field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(6)));
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn counter_only_aggregate_reference_chains_rekey_to_the_final_digest() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table aEntries:\n  key: int\n  public\nview aTotals: count aEntries by .key\n  public\ntable bEntries:\n  parent: aTotals\n  public\nview bTotals: count bEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  parent: bTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    let legacy_a = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let legacy_b = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let digest_a = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let digest_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_a)]);
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("bTotals", &legacy_b, 9).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &legacy_b).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap(), 9, "the absent referenced aggregate identity must settle before its dependent counter key");
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn sequence_identity_rekey_rolls_back_with_the_adoption_writer() {
+    let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.rewrite_sequence_ids(&BTreeMap::from([(
+        "totals".into(),
+        BTreeMap::from([(legacy.clone(), digest.clone())]),
+    )])).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 11);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy).unwrap(), 11);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest).unwrap(), 0);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+/-! Persisted `sequence by` counters are server custody keyed by the parent
+table and physical parent id. They outlive allocating rows. This small model
+does not model SQL or the device protocol; it states the adoption invariant
+for one target-specific legacy-to-digest key. -/
+
+def sequenceHighWater (id : List Nat) (counters : List (List Nat × Nat)) : Nat :=
+  counters.foldl (fun high counter =>
+    if counter.1 = id then max high counter.2 else high) 0
+
+/-- If a partially upgraded store already has both keys, adoption merges them
+at their maximum. No child-row population participates in this value. -/
+def adoptedSequenceHighWater (legacy digest : List Nat)
+    (counters : List (List Nat × Nat)) : Nat :=
+  max (sequenceHighWater legacy counters) (sequenceHighWater digest counters)
+
+theorem adoptedSequence_preserves_legacy (legacy digest counters) :
+    sequenceHighWater legacy counters ≤ adoptedSequenceHighWater legacy digest counters :=
+  Nat.le_max_left _ _
+
+theorem adoptedSequence_preserves_digest (legacy digest counters) :
+    sequenceHighWater digest counters ≤ adoptedSequenceHighWater legacy digest counters :=
+  Nat.le_max_right _ _
+
+example : adoptedSequenceHighWater [91, 55, 93] (maintainedIdV1 [.int 7])
+    [([91, 55, 93], 9), (maintainedIdV1 [.int 7], 4)] = 9 := by decide
+
 example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
 example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
   maintainedIdV1_length _

+#[test]
+fn surviving_aggregate_identity_wins_over_a_counter_only_dependency() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table aEntries:\n  key: int\n  public\nview aTotals: count aEntries by .key\n  public\ntable bEntries:\n  parent: aTotals\n  public\nview bTotals: count bEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable cEntries:\n  parent: bTotals\n  public\nview cTotals: count cEntries by .parent\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  parent: bTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    let digest_a = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("aEntries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("a".into())), ("key", Value::Int(5))])),
+        ("bEntries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("b".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(digest_a.clone()))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let legacy_a = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(5)]);
+    let digest_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_a.clone())]);
+    let legacy_b = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let dangling_b = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(legacy_a.clone())]);
+    let legacy_c = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id(legacy_b.clone())]);
+    let digest_c = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(dangling_b.clone())]);
+    let redirected_c = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id(digest_b.clone())]);
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("aTotals", &schema.tables["aTotals"], &tx.get("aTotals", &digest_a).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("aEntries", &schema.tables["aEntries"], &tx.get("aEntries", "a").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let old_source = tx.get("bEntries", "b").unwrap().unwrap();
+    let mut next_source = old_source.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next_source {
+        fields.insert("parent".into(), Value::Id(legacy_a.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("bEntries", &schema.tables["bEntries"], &next_source, Some(&old_source)).unwrap();
+    let mut target = tx.get("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("bTotals", &schema.tables["bTotals"], &target).unwrap();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut target {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy_b.clone()));
+        fields.insert("parent".into(), Value::Id(legacy_a.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("bTotals", &schema.tables["bTotals"], &target, None).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("bTotals", &legacy_b, 7).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("cTotals", &legacy_c, 11).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("bTotals", &dangling_b).unwrap().is_some());
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &legacy_b).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &dangling_b).unwrap(), 7, "counter custody follows the surviving rebuilt parent");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("bTotals", &digest_b).unwrap(), 0, "the absent dependency cannot redirect custody");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &legacy_c).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &digest_c).unwrap(), 11, "counter-only dependents inherit the authoritative surviving parent map");
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("cTotals", &redirected_c).unwrap(), 0);
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(dangling_b))]))], 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap()[0].field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
+}

+/-- A surviving aggregate row fixes the physical parent that rebuilt rows and
+typed references address. Counter-only inference applies only without that
+row evidence. This abstracts map precedence, not SQL tuple decoding. -/
+def adoptedSequenceParent (rowParent? : Option (List Nat))
+    (counterOnlyParent : List Nat) : List Nat :=
+  rowParent?.getD counterOnlyParent
+
+theorem adoptedSequenceParent_row_wins (rowParent counterOnlyParent) :
+    adoptedSequenceParent (some rowParent) counterOnlyParent = rowParent := by
+  rfl
+

+#[test]
+fn sequence_identity_adoption_keeps_invalid_canonical_groups_opaque() {
+    const SOURCE: &str = "table owners:\n  public\ntable entries:\n  label: text 3..20 format handle\n  owner: owners\n  public\nview labelTotals: count entries by .label\n  public\nview ownerTotals: count entries by .owner\n  public\ntable labelSequence:\n  parent: labelTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\ntable ownerSequence:\n  parent: ownerTotals\n  ordinal: sequence by parent\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
+    let valid = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("valid_1".into())]);
+    let invalid_control = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("\u{1}".into())]);
+    let invalid_format = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("Not_A_Handle".into())]);
+    let invalid_reference = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Id("x".repeat(136))]);
+    let valid_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::String("valid_1".into())]);
+    let control_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::String("\u{1}".into())]);
+    let format_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::String("Not_A_Handle".into())]);
+    let reference_digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Id("x".repeat(136))]);
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("labelTotals", &valid, 5).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("labelTotals", &invalid_control, 6).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("labelTotals", &invalid_format, 7).unwrap();
+    tx.set_sequence("ownerTotals", &invalid_reference, 8).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(SOURCE);
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("labelTotals", &valid).unwrap(), 0);
+    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("labelTotals", &valid_digest).unwrap(), 5, "a fully admitted predecessor group migrates");
+    for (parent, old, digest, high) in [
+        ("labelTotals", &invalid_control, &control_digest, 6),
+        ("labelTotals", &invalid_format, &format_digest, 7),
+        ("ownerTotals", &invalid_reference, &reference_digest, 8),
+    ] {
+        assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value(parent, old).unwrap(), high, "invalid canonical tuple retains opaque custody");
+        assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value(parent, digest).unwrap(), 0, "invalid canonical tuple does not create digest custody");
+    }
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("labelSequence".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("control".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(invalid_control))])),
+        ("labelSequence".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("format".into())), ("parent", Value::Id(invalid_format))])),
+    ], 2).unwrap();
+    let label_rows = e.store().rows("labelSequence").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(label_rows.iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("control".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(7)));
+    assert_eq!(label_rows.iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("format".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
+}
+

+/-! SQL adoption supplies the predecessor column-admission verdict. This
+model does not duplicate text formats, identity bounds or storage decoding;
+it states the custody decision after that independent boundary has judged the
+decoded canonical tuple. -/
+
+def adoptedSequenceCounterKey (predecessorAdmits : Bool)
+    (legacy digest : List Nat) : List Nat :=
+  if predecessorAdmits then digest else legacy
+
+theorem adoptedSequenceCounterKey_rejected_stays_opaque (legacy digest) :
+    adoptedSequenceCounterKey false legacy digest = legacy := by
+  rfl
+
+theorem adoptedSequenceCounterKey_admitted_migrates (legacy digest) :
+    adoptedSequenceCounterKey true legacy digest = digest := by
+  rfl

     6	From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the

     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on

    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
    20	  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
    23	* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
    24	  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that

    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))

   176	/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:
   177	`(child table, column, action)`. -/
   178	def referencing (sch : Schema) (t : String) : List (String × String × OnDelete) :=

   184	/-- Row `k` names the row with id `i` through column `c`. -/
   185	def names (k : Row) (c : String) (i : List Nat) : Bool := k.get c == .id i

   187	def inClosure (cl : List (String × Row)) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   188	  cl.any fun p => p.1 == t && p.2.id == r.id
   189	
   190	/-- The rows one step of cascades reaches from `(t, r)`. -/
   191	def cascadeKids (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : List (String × Row) :=
   192	  (referencing sch t).flatMap fun (c, col, a) =>
   193	    if a == .cascade then ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id).map fun k => (c, k) else []
   194	
   195	/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`
   196	bounds the walk (the store's row count suffices). -/
   197	def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)
   198	  | 0, _, acc => acc
   199	  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc
   200	  | f + 1, (t, r) :: rest, acc =>
   201	    let new := (cascadeKids sch s t r).foldl (fun n p => if inClosure (acc ++ n) p.1 p.2 then n else n ++ [p]) []
   202	    closure sch s f (rest ++ new) (acc ++ new)

   206	  cl.any fun (t, r) => (referencing sch t).any fun (c, col, a) =>
   207	    a == .restrict && (s c).any fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k
