    49	fn validate_image(schema: &Schema, table_name: &str, row: &Value, viewer: Option<&str>, before_slots: bool, cache: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    50	    let table = schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?;
    51	    let object = row.as_object()?;
    52	    if !object.contains_key("id") {
    53	        return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table_name} row lacks id")));
    54	    }
    55	    if let Some(name) = object.keys().find(|name| !table.columns.contains_key(*name)) {
    56	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} row contains undeclared field {name}")));
    57	    }
    58	    for (name, kind) in &table.columns {
    59	        if before_slots && crate::schema::timeline::is_slot(name) { continue; }
    60	        if cache && matches!(name.as_str(), "value" | "recountPending") && !object.contains_key(name) { continue; }
    61	        let value = object.get(name).or_else(|| table.maintained.contains_key(name).then_some(&Value::Int(0)));
    62	        if value.is_none() && viewer.is_some_and(|viewer| table.written_by.get(name).is_some_and(|authority|
    63	            !authority.audience && row.field(&authority.owner).ok() != Some(&Value::Id(viewer.into())))) { continue; }
    64	        validate_column(table_name, name, kind, value)?;
    65	    }
    66	    for constraint in &table.constraints {
    67	        if let Constraint::Text { field, min, format } = constraint
    68	            && let Some(Value::String(text)) = object.get(field)
    69	        {
    70	            validate_text(&format!("{table_name}.{field}"), text, *min, *format).map_err(|error| RuntimeError::Constraint(error.to_string().trim_start_matches("E_INPUT: ").to_owned()))?;
    71	        }
    72	    }
    73	    Ok(())
    74	}

    76	pub fn validate_column(table_name: &str, name: &str, kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    77	    let label = format!("{table_name}.{name}");
    78	    if let Some(value) = value {
    79	        crate::value::validate_identities(value)?;
    80	        if contains_system_principal(value) {
    81	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} cannot carry the reserved system principal")));
    82	        }
    83	    }
    84	    if let Some(code_point) = disallowed_control(kind, value) {
    85	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} contains disallowed control character U+{code_point:04X}")));
    86	    }
    87	    validate_column_minimum(kind, value, &label)?;
    88	    if !fits(kind, value) {
    89	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(match value {
    90	            None | Some(Value::Null) => format!("{label} is required ({kind})"),
    91	            Some(value) => format!("{label} must be {kind}, not {}", describe(value)),
    92	        }));
    93	    }
    94	    Ok(())
    95	}

    97	// @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — nested/optional columns use the same minimum on server and device writes.
    98	fn validate_column_minimum(kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>, label: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    99	    match (kind, value) {
   100	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), Some(value)) => validate_column_minimum(inner, Some(value), label),
   101	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Some(Value::Array(items))) => {
   102	            if let ColumnType::ListRange { min, .. } = kind { validate_list_minimum(label, items.len(), *min)?; }
   103	            for item in items { validate_column_minimum(of, Some(item), label)?; }
   104	            Ok(())
   105	        }
   106	        _ => Ok(()),
   107	    }
   108	}

   110	fn validate_list_minimum(label: &str, length: usize, min: u32) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {

   112	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} needs at least {min} {}; got {length}", if min == 1 { "item" } else { "items" })));
   113	    }
   114	    Ok(())

   117	fn describe(value: &Value) -> String {
   118	    match value {
   119	        Value::String(text) if text.chars().count() > 24 => format!("{} characters of text", text.chars().count()),
   120	        Value::String(text) => format!("the text '{text}'"),
   121	        Value::Id(id) => format!("the id '{id}'"),
   122	        Value::Int(n) => format!("the number {n}"),
   123	        Value::Bool(b) => format!("the boolean {b}"),
   124	        Value::Null => "null".into(),
   125	        Value::Bytes(b) => format!("{} bytes", b.len()),
   126	        Value::Array(items) => format!("a list of {}", items.len()),
   127	        Value::Row(_) | Value::Map(_) => "an object".into(),
   128	    }
   129	}

   131	pub fn validate_text(label: &str, text: &str, min: u32, format: Option<TextFormat>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   132	    let length = text.chars().count();
   133	    if length < min as usize {
   134	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} needs at least {min} characters; got {length}")));
   135	    }
   136	    if let Some(format) = format
   137	        && !format.matches(text)
   138	    {
   139	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(match format {
   140	            TextFormat::Handle => format!("{label} must be a handle: lowercase letters, digits and underscores"),
   141	            TextFormat::Url => format!("{label} must be an http or https URL"),
   142	            TextFormat::Email => format!("{label} must be an ASCII email address with one @, a dot-safe local part, and valid domain labels"),
   143	        }));
   144	    }
   145	    Ok(())
   146	}

   148	fn disallowed_control(kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>) -> Option<u32> {
   149	    match (kind, value) {
   150	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), Some(value)) => disallowed_control(inner, Some(value)),
   151	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Some(Value::Array(values))) => values.iter().find_map(|value| disallowed_control(of, Some(value))),
   152	        (ColumnType::Text { .. }, Some(Value::String(text))) => disallowed_text_control(text),
   153	        _ => None,
   154	    }
   155	}
   156	
   157	/// Text forbids C0 controls except tab, LF and CR.
   158	pub fn disallowed_text_control(text: &str) -> Option<u32> {
   159	    text.chars().find(|c| c.is_control() && !matches!(c, '\t' | '\n' | '\r')).map(|c| c as u32)
   160	}

   162	pub(crate) fn fits(kind: &ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>) -> bool {
   163	    match (kind, value) {
   164	        (ColumnType::Optional(_), None | Some(Value::Null)) => true,
   165	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), Some(value)) => fits(inner, Some(value)),
   166	        (ColumnType::List { of, max } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, max, .. }, Some(Value::Array(values))) => values.len() <= *max as usize && values.iter().all(|value| fits(of, Some(value))),
   167	        // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — typed references do not imply target existence
   168	        (ColumnType::Id | ColumnType::Principal | ColumnType::Ref { .. }, Some(Value::Id(_))) => true,
   169	        (ColumnType::Text { max }, Some(Value::String(text))) => text.chars().count() <= *max as usize,
   170	        (ColumnType::Bytes { max }, Some(Value::Bytes(bytes))) => bytes.len() <= *max as usize,
   171	        (ColumnType::Image { .. } | ColumnType::Video { .. } | ColumnType::File { .. }, Some(Value::Map(fields))) => fields.get("id").is_some_and(|id| matches!(id, Value::Id(_))),
   172	        (ColumnType::Enum { variants }, Some(Value::String(value))) => variants.contains(value),
   173	        (ColumnType::Int | ColumnType::Time | ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. }, Some(Value::Int(value))) => (I53_MIN..=I53_MAX).contains(value),
   174	        // @ref LLP 3000.040#14-where-the-bound-is-enforced — the slot's bound is part of its type: every stored write and argument meets it here.
   175	        (ColumnType::IntRange { min, max }, Some(Value::Int(value))) => (I53_MIN..=I53_MAX).contains(value) && (*min..=*max).contains(value),
   176	        (ColumnType::Bool, Some(Value::Bool(_))) => true,
   177	        (ColumnType::Json { max_bytes }, Some(value)) => canonical_json(value).len() <= *max_bytes as usize,
   178	        _ => false,
   179	    }
   180	}

   197	fn validate_arguments(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, inputs: &mut BTreeMap<String, Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   198	    for (name, kind) in &program.args {
   199	        if !inputs.contains_key(name) && (kind.is_optional() || matches!(kind, ArgType::Cursor)) {
   200	            inputs.insert(name.clone(), Value::Null);
   201	        }
   202	        let value = inputs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input(format!("missing argument {name}")))?;
   203	        validate_arg(schema, kind, value, name)?;
   204	    }
   205	    if let Some(extra) = inputs.keys().find(|name| !program.args.contains_key(*name)) {
   206	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{} takes no argument {extra}", program.name)));
   207	    }
   208	    Ok(())
   209	}

   211	pub fn validate_arg(schema: &Schema, kind: &ArgType, value: &Value, label: &str) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   212	    if !kind.bounds_valid() {
   213	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} has a minimum greater than its maximum")));
   214	    }
   215	    crate::value::validate_identities(value)?;
   216	    if contains_system_principal(value) {
   217	        return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} cannot carry the reserved system principal")));
   218	    }
   219	    match kind {
   220	        ArgType::Cursor => match value {
   221	            Value::Null => Ok(()),
   222	            Value::String(token) => crate::cursor::decode_cursor(schema, token).map(|_| ()).map_err(|error| RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label}: {error}"))),
   223	            _ => Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} must be an opaque cursor string or null"))),
   224	        },
   225	        ArgType::Optional(_) if *value == Value::Null => Ok(()),
   226	        ArgType::Optional(inner) => validate_arg(schema, inner, value, label),
   227	        ArgType::Scalar => match value {
   228	            Value::Row(_) | Value::Map(_) => Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} must be a scalar"))),
   229	            _ => Ok(()),
   230	        },
   231	        ArgType::Text { max, min, format } => match value {
   232	            Value::String(text) => {
   233	                if let Some(code_point) = disallowed_text_control(text) {
   234	                    return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} contains disallowed control character U+{code_point:04X}")));
   235	                }
   236	                if text.chars().count() > *max as usize {
   237	                    return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} is longer than {max} characters")));
   238	                }
   239	                validate_text(label, text, *min, *format)
   240	            }
   241	            other => Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} must be text, not {}", describe(other)))),
   242	        },
   243	        ArgType::List { of, max } | ArgType::ListRange { of, max, .. } => match value {
   244	            Value::Array(items) => {
   245	                if let ArgType::ListRange { min, .. } = kind { validate_list_minimum(label, items.len(), *min)?; }
   246	                if items.len() > *max as usize {
   247	                    return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} has more than {max} items")));
   248	                }
   249	                if let Some(of) = of {
   250	                    for item in items {
   251	                        validate_arg(schema, of, item, label)?;
   252	                    }
   253	                }
   254	                Ok(())
   255	            }
   256	            other => Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} must be a list, not {}", describe(other)))),
   257	        },
   258	        other => {
   259	            let column = crate::schema::arg_as_column(other).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} has no column form")))?;
   260	            if fits(&column, Some(value)) { Ok(()) } else { Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{label} must be {column}, not {}", describe(value)))) }
   261	        }
   262	    }
   263	}

     5	fn open(source: &str) -> Engine {
     6	    let b = compile(source);

    10	fn preview(e: &mut Engine, next: &Schema) -> super::super::adoption_estimate::AdoptionEstimate {
    11	    let before = ["r", "i", "_log", "_commits", "_generations"].map(|t| rows(e, t));
    12	    let generation = e.generation();
    13	    let estimate = e.store_mut().adoption_estimate(next).unwrap().expect("populated write work needs advice");
    14	    assert_eq!(generation, e.generation());
    15	    for (t, old) in ["r", "i", "_log", "_commits", "_generations"].into_iter().zip(before) {
    16	        assert_eq!(rows(e, t), old, "preview wrote {t}");
    17	    }
    18	    estimate
    19	}

    21	const CHILDREN: &str = "table parents:\n  public\ntable children:\n  parent: parents\n  until: time default 50\n  immutable parent\n  expire at .until\n  read through .parent\n";
    22	fn children(source: &str, count: usize) -> Engine {
    23	    let mut e = open(source);
    24	    e.seed_at(std::iter::once(("parents".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("p".into()))])))
    25	        .chain((0..count).map(|n| ("children".into(), object([
    26	            ("id", Value::Id(format!("c{n}"))), ("parent", Value::Id("p".into())), ("until", Value::Int(50)),
    27	        ])))), 0).unwrap();
    28	    e
    29	}

    31	#[test]
    32	fn inherited_expiry_default_warns_before_retiring_one_thousand_children() {
    33	    let mut e = children(CHILDREN, 1000);
    34	    let next = compile(&CHILDREN.replace("default 50", "default 200"));
    35	    let estimate = preview(&mut e, &next.schema);
    36	    assert_eq!(estimate.deadline_rewrite_rows, 0);
    37	    let message = estimate.summary();
    38	    assert!(message.contains("unestimated write pause") && message.contains("read-through retirement/recapture children (1000 stored rows; deletion subset depends on activation time)"), "{message}");
    39	    assert!(!message.contains("to recompute deadlines"), "{message}");
    40	    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 100).unwrap();
    41	    assert!(e.store().rows("children").unwrap().is_empty());
    42	    assert_eq!(e.store().conn().query_row("SELECT count(*) FROM i JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=i.ti WHERE c.name LIKE 'children.%'", [], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0)).unwrap(), 0);
    43	}

   158	fn identity_adoption_rekeys_sequence_history_without_reusing_deleted_ordinals() {
   159	    const SOURCE: &str = "table entries:\n  bucket: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .bucket\n  public\ntable sequenced:\n  total: totals\n  ordinal: sequence by total\n  unique total, ordinal\n  public\n";
   160	    let mut e = open(SOURCE);
   161	    e.seed_at([
   162	        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e7".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))])),
   163	        ("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("e9".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(9))])),
   164	    ], 0).unwrap();
   165	    let digest7 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
   166	    let digest9 = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(9)]);
   167	    e.seed_at([
   168	        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("gone".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
   169	        ("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("kept".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7.clone()))])),
   170	    ], 0).unwrap();
   171	    e.seed_delete("sequenced", "gone").unwrap();
   172	
   173	    let legacy7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
   174	    let legacy9 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(9)]);
   175	    let noncanonical7 = "[ { \"Int\" : 7 } ]".to_owned();
   176	    let wrong_type7 = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::String("7".into())]);
   177	    let schema = e.schema().clone();
   178	    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
   179	    let entries = schema.tables["entries"].clone();
   180	    let sequenced = schema.tables["sequenced"].clone();
   181	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   182	    let mut row = tx.get("totals", &digest7).unwrap().unwrap();
   183	    tx.delete("totals", &target, &row).unwrap();
   184	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row {
   185	        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
   186	    }
   187	    tx.put("totals", &target, &row, None).unwrap();
   188	    tx.delete("totals", &target, &tx.get("totals", &digest9).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
   189	    tx.delete("entries", &entries, &tx.get("entries", "e9").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
   190	    let old = tx.get("sequenced", "kept").unwrap().unwrap();
   191	    let mut next = old.clone();
   192	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
   193	        fields.insert("total".into(), Value::Id(legacy7.clone()));
   194	    }
   195	    tx.put("sequenced", &sequenced, &next, Some(&old)).unwrap();
   196	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy7, 7).unwrap();
   197	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest7, 4).unwrap();
   198	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &legacy9, crate::value::I53_MAX).unwrap();
   199	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &digest9, 12).unwrap();
   200	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &noncanonical7, 13).unwrap();
   201	    tx.set_sequence("totals", &wrong_type7, 14).unwrap();
   202	    tx.set_sequence("ordinary", &legacy7, 11).unwrap();
   203	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   204	    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
   205	
   206	    let next = compile(SOURCE);
   207	    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 1).unwrap();
   208	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   209	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy7).unwrap(), 0);
   210	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &legacy9).unwrap(), 0);
   211	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest7).unwrap(), 7, "the deleted allocating row and lower destination counter cannot lower the high-water mark");
   212	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX);
   213	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &noncanonical7).unwrap(), 13, "a noncanonical dangling id must not collapse into the real group");
   214	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &wrong_type7).unwrap(), 14, "a canonical tuple with the wrong predecessor type stays opaque");
   215	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("ordinary", &legacy7).unwrap(), 11, "translation is scoped by parent table and id");
   216	    tx.commit().unwrap();
   217	    let kept = e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().pop().unwrap();
   218	    assert_eq!(kept.field("total").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest7.clone()));
   219	    assert_eq!(kept.field("ordinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(2));
   220	
   221	    e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("next".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest7))]))], 2).unwrap();
   222	    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("sequenced").unwrap().into_iter().find(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&Value::Id("next".into()))).unwrap().field("ordinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(8)));
   223	    let error = e.seed_at([("sequenced".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("full".into())), ("total", Value::Id(digest9.clone()))]))], 2).unwrap_err();
   224	    assert_eq!(error.refusal().code, "E_SEQUENCE_EXHAUSTED");
   225	    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
   226	    assert_eq!(tx.sequence_value("totals", &digest9).unwrap(), crate::value::I53_MAX, "overflow refusal must not change the migrated counter");
   227	    tx.rollback().unwrap();
   228	}

     1	import Quarry.Run

     3	/-!
     4	# Write authority
     5	
     6	**No write succeeds unless the corresponding rule holds.** A successful write
     7	either leaves the store unchanged (`insert … if absent` on a visible clash)
     8	or is one authorized `Step`: an insert whose insert rule admits the new
     9	image, an update whose update rule admits (old, next) for a row that exists,
    10	or a delete whose delete rule admits the row. Rules are evaluated in the
    11	opened projection of the store as it stood immediately before that write
    12	(`applyWrite_authorized`).
    13	
    14	A whole mutation's store transition is a chain of such steps
    15	(`mutation_authorized`).
    16	-/
    17	
    18	namespace Quarry
    19	
    20	inductive Step (sch : Schema) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) : Store → Store → Prop
    21	  | insert {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {r : Row} :
    22	      sch.table? t = some td → td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r } = true →
    23	      Step sch v now s (s.insertRow t r)
    24	  | update {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old nw : Row} :
    25	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
    26	      td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw } = true →
    27	      Step sch v now s (s.replaceRow t old nw)
    28	  /-- A delete whose delete rule admits the row, with the referential
    29	  actions the schema declares on the rows naming it (LLP 3000.039 §4.1: the
    30	  parent's delete authorizes a declared cascade or set null). -/
    31	  | delete {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
    32	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
    33	      td.delete.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some old } = true →
    34	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
    35	      Step sch v now s s'
    36	  /-- An expired same-id row is retired inside an insert transaction before
    37	  the replacement image's remaining constraints are checked. -/
    38	  | retire {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
    39	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
    40	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
    41	      Step sch v now s s'
    42	  /-- A same-id replacement is one authorized transition: its insert rule is
    43	  checked against the pre-retirement store, then the expired predecessor's
    44	  actions run, then the new image is inserted. -/
    45	  | replaceExpired {s retired : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old img : Row} :
    46	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
    47	      td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some img } = true →
    48	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok retired →
    49	      Step sch v now s (retired.insertRow t img)

   236	theorem sbind_ok {α β : Type} {x : EM α} {f : α → EM β} {rs : RS} {r : β × RS}
   237	    (h : (x >>= f).run rs = .ok r) : ∃ a rs1, x.run rs = .ok (a, rs1) ∧ (f a).run rs1 = .ok r := by
   238	  simp only [StateT.run_bind] at h
   239	  obtain ⟨⟨a, rs1⟩, h1, h2⟩ := bind_ok h
   240	  exact ⟨a, rs1, h1, h2⟩

   242	theorem liftE_ok {α : Type} {x : Except Stop α} {rs : RS} {a : α} {rs' : RS}
   243	    (h : (liftE x).run rs = .ok (a, rs')) : x = .ok a := by
   244	  unfold liftE at h
   245	  cases x with
   246	  | error e => cases h
   247	  | ok b => simp [StateT.run, Except.map] at h; rw [h.1]

   249	/-- Statement execution changes the world only through `Hooks.apply`: any
   250	relation on worlds that is reflexive, transitive and contains every applied
   251	write contains the whole execution. -/
   252	theorem execStmts_inv {W : Type} (H : Hooks W) (cx : Ctx) (R : W → W → Prop) (hrefl : ∀ w, R w w)
   253	    (htrans : ∀ a b d, R a b → R b d → R a d)
   254	    (happ : ∀ w rw val w', H.apply cx w rw = .ok (val, w') → R w w') :
   255	    ∀ fuel w env ss rs fl w' env' rs',
   256	      (execStmts H fuel cx w env ss).run rs = .ok ((fl, w', env'), rs') → R w w' := by
   257	  intro fuel
   258	  induction fuel with
   259	  | zero =>
   260	    intro w env ss rs fl w' env' rs' h
   261	    simp [execStmts, refuse, StateT.run, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift] at h
   262	    cases h
   263	  | succ fuel ih =>
   264	    intro w env ss rs fl w' env' rs' h
   265	    cases ss with
   266	    | nil =>
   267	      simp only [execStmts, StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
   268	      cases h; exact hrefl w
   269	    | cons s ss =>
   270	      cases s with
   271	      | assign x e =>
   272	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   273	        obtain ⟨p, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   274	        exact ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h
   275	      | require c code =>
   276	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   277	        obtain ⟨⟨v, _⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   278	        obtain ⟨b, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   279	        split at h
   280	        · exact ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h
   281	        · simp [refuse, StateT.run, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift] at h; cases h
   282	      | ret e =>
   283	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   284	        obtain ⟨⟨v, nx⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   285	        simp only [StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
   286	        cases h; exact hrefl w
   287	      | ite c th el =>
   288	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   289	        obtain ⟨⟨v, _⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   290	        obtain ⟨b, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   291	        obtain ⟨⟨fl1, w1, env1⟩, rs3, h1, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   292	        have r1 := ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h1
   293	        split at h
   294	        · simp only [StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
   295	          cases h; exact r1
   296	        · exact htrans _ _ _ r1 (ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h)
   297	      | write bind op =>
   298	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   299	        obtain ⟨rs0, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   300	        obtain ⟨rw, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   301	        obtain ⟨⟨val, w1⟩, rs3, h1, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   302	        exact htrans _ _ _ (happ _ _ _ _ (liftE_ok h1)) (ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h)

     3	/-!
     4	# Running a program
     5	
     6	`run` takes (schema, helpers, store, viewer, program, arguments, ceiling)
     7	to an outcome. This is the function the later harness oracle calls.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	namespace Quarry
    11	
    12	/-- An outcome. A query answers with data, `complete` and the returned
    13	page's continuation (`next`, null when none), or is unavailable (a cut
    14	scalar read), or refuses. A mutation commits a result and a new store, or
    15	refuses (and changes nothing). -/
    16	inductive Outcome where
    17	  | answer (data : Value) (complete : Bool) (next : Value)
    18	  | unavailable
    19	  | committed (result : Value) (store : Store)
    20	  | refused (code : String)
    21	
    22	/-- The world of a query: the view; every write refuses. -/
    23	def queryHooks : Hooks View where
    24	  view _ vw := vw
    25	  apply _ _ _ := throw (.refuse "E_QUARRY_PLACEMENT")
    26	
    27	/-- The world of a mutation: the store; reads see its visible rows. -/
    28	def storeHooks : Hooks Store where
    29	  view cx s := visibleRowsAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now
    30	  apply := applyWrite
    31	
    32	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — born-expired and updated-expired final images retire in the writer transaction.
    33	/-- Rows whose final images a mutation changed. Commit-end expiry retirement
    34	is scoped to this set; pre-existing expired backlog remains for the ordinary
    35	sweep. -/
    36	abbrev ChangedRows := List (String × List Nat)
    37	
    38	structure MutationWorld where
    39	  store : Store
    40	  changed : ChangedRows := []
    41	
    42	/-- The explicit address of an insert-like write that reached its write arm.
    43	This retains a structurally identical expired replacement for commit-end
    44	retirement, while excluding `insert if absent` live-clash no-ops. -/
    45	def RWrite.changedExplicitId? (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)
    46	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent => do
    47	    let td ← cx.schema.table? t
    48	    let fs ← (scalarsE fields).toOption
    49	    let rid ← (insertId fs).toOption
    50	    let img ← (buildImage td rid fs eInput).toOption
    51	    if ifAbsent && (findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td cx.now))
    52	        (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none).isSome
    53	    then none
    54	    else some (t, rid)
    55	  | .upsert t key patch =>
    56	    match key.lookup "id" with
    57	    | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    58	    | _ => match patch.lookup "id" with
    59	      | some (.s (.id rid)) => some (t, rid)
    60	      | _ => none
    61	  | _ => none
    62	
    63	def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=
    64	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => (after td.name).filterMap fun row =>
    65	    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
    66	    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
    67	    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)
    68	
    69	def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where
    70	  view cx w := visibleRowsAt cx.schema w.store cx.viewer cx.now
    71	  apply cx w rw := match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
    72	    | .error e => .error e
    73	    | .ok (value, store) =>
    74	      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
    75	      let changed := match rw.changedExplicitId? cx w.store with
    76	        | some address => changed ++ [address]
    77	        | none => changed
    78	      .ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })
    79	
    80	/-- Runtime retires changed expiry rows in reverse through-table order, then
    81	ascending id order. Read-through tables are outside this model fragment, so
    82	its through order is the schema's lexical table order. -/
    83	def changedRetirementOrder (sch : Schema) (changed : ChangedRows) : ChangedRows :=
    84	  (expiryRetirementTables sch).flatMap fun td =>
    85	    (changed.filter fun address => address.1 == td.name).mergeSort fun a b =>
    86	      lex cmpNat a.2 b.2 != .gt
    87	
    88	/-- Retire only rows written by this mutation whose final image is already
    89	expired. A restrict refusal aborts the mutation; cascade and set-null actions
    90	are in the same transition. -/
    91	def retireExpiredChanged (sch : Schema) (now : Int) : Store → ChangedRows → Except Stop Store
    92	  | s, [] => pure s
    93	  | s, (t, rid) :: rest =>
    94	    match sch.table? t with
    95	    | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    96	    | some td =>
    97	      match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
    98	      | none => retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
    99	      | some row =>
   100	        if expired td now row then do
   101	          let s ← refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t row
   102	          retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
   103	        else retireExpiredChanged sch now s rest
   104	
   105	def bindArgs (params : List Param) (args : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop Env :=
   106	  params.mapM fun p => match args.lookup p.name with
   107	    | some v => pure (p.name, (v, none))
   108	    | none => if p.optional then pure (p.name, (.null, none)) else throw (.refuse "E_INPUT")

   110	def defaultFuel : Nat := 100000
   111	
   112	structure Case where
   113	  schema : Schema
   114	  helpers : List Helper := []
   115	  store : Store
   116	  viewer : List Nat
   117	  now : Int := 0
   118	  program : Program
   119	  args : List (String × Value) := []
   120	  budget : Option Nat := none
   121	  /-- Run only the server expiry sweep and return its resulting store. -/
   122	  sweepOnly : Bool := false
   123	  /-- In-engine sweep continuation supplied by the differential driver. -/
   124	  sweepCursor : SweepCursor := {}
   125	  /-- Visited-row bound for the sweep; examples default to a complete pass. -/
   126	  sweepLimit : Option Nat := none
   127	
   128	def Case.ctx (c : Case) : Ctx :=
   129	  { schema := c.schema, viewer := c.viewer, now := c.now, helpers := c.helpers, budget := c.budget,
   130	    mutation := c.program.kind == .mutation }
   131	
   132	def flowValue : Flow → Value × Value
   133	  | .normal => (.null, .null)
   134	  | .ret v nx => (v, nx.getD .null)
   135	
   136	def runQuery (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   137	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   138	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   139	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   140	  | .ok env =>
   141	    let vw := visibleRowsAt c.schema c.store c.viewer c.now
   142	    match (execStmts queryHooks defaultFuel c.ctx vw env c.program.body).run {} with
   143	    | .ok ((fl, _, _), rs) => let (v, nx) := flowValue fl; .answer v rs.complete nx
   144	    | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   145	    | .error .unavailable => .unavailable
   146	
   147	def runMutation (c : Case) : Outcome :=
   148	  match bindArgs c.program.params c.args with
   149	  | .error (.refuse code) => .refused code
   150	  | .error .unavailable => .unavailable

   130	Spellings are illustrative. None of the blocks below is a compiling example.
   131	
   132	### 3.0 Aggregate target identity and migration
   133	
   134	Every ordinary maintained aggregate row has one internal identity function:
   135	64 lowercase hexadecimal characters from SHA-256 over the domain
   136	`snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1` and the typed canonical group-key vector.
   137	The checker therefore admits the largest legal group key against a fixed-size
   138	identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
   139	adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
   140	address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
   141	
   142	The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
   143	order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
   144	lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
   145	whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
   146	`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.
   147	
   148	The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker
   149	`maintained_id_version = sha256-v1` bind persisted aggregate targets to that
   150	function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a
   151	0.4.28 store whose ids were the unbounded canonical JSON of the group key —
   152	atomically clears and rebuilds every ordinary aggregate target from its source
   153	rows, writes the marker, and publishes a new semantic generation. A failure
   154	rolls back old rows, rebuilt rows, marker and generation together. Adoption
   155	advice counts the SQLite rebuild even when schema/program bytes are unchanged;
   156	the evaluation adapter performs the corresponding rebuild under its opening
   157	writer/head fence. Its narrowly admitted private maintained-column targets use
   158	the same digest migration: rebuild the authoritative target and then mirror
   159	every live parent before the marker or generation publishes. Before clearing
   160	targets, adoption derives each target's
   161	legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
   162	then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps, including
   163	rows, columns and narrowed rows retained in release-dormant storage. Its
   164	captured dormant-reference ledger changes in the same transaction, so a later
   165	restore still proves the same aggregate lifetime under its digest address. Thus an
   166	aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
   167	aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
   168	to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
   169	target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
   170	Removing the aggregate itself retires its derived target rows; a dormant
   171	reference to that retired target receives no map and keeps the ordinary
   172	restore refusal against acquiring a newly created parent lifetime.
   173	
   174	Persisted `sequence by` custody is part of the same identity migration even
   175	when no allocating row, source row, or aggregate target row survives. Adoption
   176	decodes canonical legacy counter ids with the predecessor aggregate's typed
   177	group definition and admits every component through that predecessor source
   178	column's complete value boundary: identity syntax and bounds, disallowed text
   179	controls, required type and range/list bounds, plus declared text minimum and
   180	format constraints. A canonical JSON tuple outside that domain remains an
   181	opaque dangling parent id and keeps its original counter key. Admitted tuples
   182	recursively settle any aggregate-reference components and re-key
   183	`_sequences(parent, id, value)` through the resulting target-specific map. If legacy and digest keys both exist, their maximum high-water value wins;
   184	the legacy key is removed and an exhausted counter remains exhausted. Counters
   185	whose old parent also has a surviving aggregate row use that row-derived map;
   186	independently decoded counter dependencies cannot redirect custody away from
   187	the parent that rebuild and typed row-reference migration will address. This
   188	preserves the ordinary dangling-reference contract when a grouped reference's
   189	target is absent. Counters
   190	for other parent tables and legacy strings that do not decode as a canonical
   191	group tuple stay opaque. A predecessor aggregate removed by the candidate is
   192	normalized before the current identity marker publishes, so later
   193	reintroduction cannot revive legacy custody under that marker. Counter rewrites
   194	and their rollback share the adoption transaction with row-reference rewrites,
   195	target rebuilds, marker and generation.
   196	
   197	Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
   198	the same transaction. A legacy target address is itself the predecessor's
   199	canonical logical group tuple. Adoption decodes it using the predecessor
   200	maintain and column types, so candidate projection cannot erase the migration
   201	input when the same activation also changes the grouping declaration. The map
   202	preserves the predecessor target identity; the candidate rebuild then decides
   203	which new groups exist, so a reference to a removed group follows the ordinary
   204	dangling-reference contract. The fixed-point bound counts stored aggregate identities,
   205	not aggregate declarations, because one target can hold a legal acyclic chain
   206	of references to other rows in that same target. SQLite captures newly recorded
   207	path values while predecessor targets still exist, then derives and applies all
   208	legacy maps before any recorded-path rebuild can remove those targets. Schemas
   209	with ordinary maintains require device capability
   210	`maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
   211	it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
   212	zero. Conversely, a current device refuses to execute backend bytes from an
   213	old server that omit this capability. The shared codec records the omission so
   214	the server can adopt and republish a persisted schema; a device may decode the
   215	same bytes only as an inactive kept predecessor that it atomically replaces
   216	with a current backend, preserving queued writes. Offline reuse and adoption
   217	of the old backend refuse before interpretation.

   219	### 3.1 F1: maintained columns
   220	
   221	F1 is LLP 3000.007.001, unchanged. Its value here is ranking. With `likeCount`
   222	on the post and ruling 29's hour index, Trending becomes one merge over 25 hour
   223	lanes (§21.3 P3):
   224	
   225	- zero-like posts are included;
   226	- ties break by post time;
   227	- there is no copied time and no fill.
   228	
   229	F1 composes with F3 on the same posts table: `likeCount` and the hour index
   230	sit on the posts a Following timeline maps. A timeline's **owned** tables are
   231	never a column's parent or source. The engine writes them only on the
   232	timeline's scoped transition path, and a mirror there would bypass it. Its
   233	**mapped** tables are ordinary parents and sources, for three reasons:
   234	- the mirror is not a source write, so it never enters a timeline
   235	  transition;
   236	- delivery copies ids, author and time, never parent fields;
   237	- a mapped source's own write runs its maintain, then its transition, like
   238	  any maintain over a mapped table.
   239	
   240	A differential test shows it. The same operations on the language card's
   241	timeline, with and without counts on its mapped cards, leave every owned row
   242	and home page identical. The operations are follows, posts, a delivered
   243	repost, votes, removal, unvote and unfollow.
   244	
   245	Its cost is recorded in LLP 3000.007.002 §2: each contribution re-sends the
   246	parent row. On a 4,000-byte parent that is 4,323 wire bytes per like, against
   247	329 for a separate synced maintain. F2 keeps aggregates in their own rows. It
   248	is the better form for a hot parent's counter until the stream coalesces or
   249	patches fields.

//! Reuse physical state whose complete interpretation has not changed.
use crate::schema::Schema;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

pub(super) struct Plan {
    pub project: bool,
    pub indexes: BTreeSet<String>,
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.6 — an added view must not reconstruct unrelated rows and indexes.
// Compare the whole table except indexes. This intentionally keeps the old
// exhaustive validation for defaults, captures, rules, lifetimes and constraints.
// An index can survive an unrelated column change only when each interpreted
// dependency (including calendar, words and contribution predicates) is equal.
// Device installations have no persisted server predecessor and keep that path.
pub(super) fn plans(next: &Schema, previous: Option<&Schema>) -> BTreeMap<String, Plan> {
    next.tables
        .iter()
        .map(|(name, table)| {
            let old = previous.and_then(|schema| schema.table(name));
            let project = old.is_none_or(|old| {
                let mut comparable = table.clone();
                comparable.indexes = old.indexes.clone();
                &comparable != old
            });
            let indexes = table
                .indexes
                .iter()
                .filter(|(index_name, index)| {
                    old.is_none_or(|old| {
                        old.indexes.get(*index_name) != Some(*index)
                            || old.through != table.through
                            || old.columns.keys().chain(table.columns.keys()).any(|field| {
                                index.uses_column(field)
                                    && (crate::successor::interpretation(
                                        previous.unwrap(),
                                        name,
                                        field,
                                    ) != crate::successor::interpretation(next, name, field)
                                        || old.maintained.get(field) != table.maintained.get(field))
                            })
                    })
                })
                .map(|(name, _)| name.clone())
                .collect();
            (name.clone(), Plan { project, indexes })
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Historical catalog numbers remain, but inactive names lose their rows/keys.
pub(super) fn active_names(schema: &Schema) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    schema.tables.iter().filter(|(_, t)| t.ephemeral.is_none())
        .flat_map(|(name, table)| std::iter::once(name.clone())
            .chain(table.indexes.keys().map(move |index| format!("{name}.{index}"))))
        .collect()
}

public\ntable follows:\n  followerId: principal\n  followedId: principal\n  at: time default 0\n  unique byPair: followerId, followedId\n  by byFollowed: followedId, followerId\n  immutable followerId, followedId, at\n  cap 1000 by followerId\n  cap 1000 by followedId\n  cap 100000\n  public 'edges'\n  insert <- .followerId = viewer\n  delete <- .followerId = viewer\n  sync public\ntable notes:\n  owner: principal\n  insert <- .owner = viewer\n\nmaintain feed: timeline\n  authors profiles by principal\n  events posts by authorId, at removed by removed\n  reposts reposts by actorId, postId, at\n  edges follows by followerId, followedId\n\nmutation registerReservation():\n  insert profiles {principal: viewer}\nmutation burst():\n  for n in range(0, 257):\n    insert posts 93d05d65b6:snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/lowering/r1p-sources.jsonl:77:["187f905db1779d53020743248e928a107a2f82d8ecca6fd2e031fd14f72c4aaa",[["timeline.q","use identity                          -- guests and password accounts; `use identity guests` or `use identity password` admits one kind\nuse personas alice, bob, carol        -- a development cast: `--as alice` and the persona header act as dev:alice\neffect notify                         -- a name a mutation or job may `emit` under; a worker with a service token performs it (guide effects)\n\ntable rooms:\n  name: text 1..80                    -- text <=N | text M..N, either with `format handle` or `format url`\n  ownerId: principal                  -- principal | id | <table> (a reference to its row) | int | time (milliseconds) | bool\n  kind: enum('open', 'closed')        -- enum('a', 'b') | decimal S | money CUR [S] | json <=N | bytes <=N | image <=N [once] | video <=N\n  tags: [text <=20] <=8               -- [type] <=N: a bounded list\n  parentId: rooms ?                   -- `?` makes a column optional: null when absent. Every table has an implicit `id` and a unique `byId`\n  createdAt: time default now          -- omitted on insert; evaluated on the writing host\n  by byOwner: ownerId, createdAt, id  -- `by` orders; a scan pins the leading columns and pages along the rest\n  read <- exists members[.id, viewer]                                     -- rules: allow | deny | public ['why'] | .col = viewer | .col != 'x' | exists t[..] | created t[..] | and | or | not\n  insert <- .ownerId = viewer\n  update (old, next) <- old.ownerId = viewer and next.ownerId = viewer   -- an update rule may name both images\n  delete <- deny\n  after insert <- exists members[roomId = .id, principal = .ownerId, role = 'admin']                 -- a row that must exist by the end of the mutation that inserted this one\n  sync to members[.id]                -- each row reaches every principal with a members row whose roomId is this row's id\n\ntable members:\n  roomId: rooms\n  principal: principal\n  role: enum('member', 'admin')\n  joinedAt: time\n  unique byRoomPrincipal: roomId, principal            -- `unique` orders and constrains\n  by byRoomPrincipalRole: roomId, principal, role\n  by byPrincipalRoom: principal, roomId, id\n  cap 100 by roomId                                    -- at most N rows per group; needs an index leading with the group\n  immutable roomId, principal                          -- columns no update may change\n  read <- exists members[.roomId, viewer]\n  insert <- exists members[roomId = .roomId, principal = viewer, role = 'admin'] or created rooms[.roomId]   -- created: this mutation inserted the probed row\n  delete <- .principal = viewer or exists members[roomId = .roomId, principal = viewer, role = 'admin']\n  sync to members[.roomId]\n\ntable messages:\n  roomId: rooms\n  authorId: principal\n  body: text <=4000 ?\n  photo: image <=10000000 ?           -- an upload the row holds (guide assets); `once` after the bound serves one view per principal\n  clip: video <=50000000 ?\n  editedAt: time ?\n  expiresAt: time ?\n  at: time\n  by byRoomTime: roomId, at, id\n  by byRoomWords: roomId, words(body), at, id   -- a words index: one entry per distinct word of the text columns; read with `matching` (guide search)\n  by byExpiresAt: expiresAt\n  immutable roomId, authorId\n  read <- exists members[.roomId, viewer]\n  insert <- .authorId = viewer and exists members[.roomId, viewer]\n  update <- .authorId = viewer\n  delete <- .authorId = viewer\n  retain delivered-history            -- a device keeps what it was given after it leaves the group; `until-revoked` (the default) drops it\n  expire at .expiresAt                -- a row past that time is absent everywhere at once, then swept; a null time never expires\n  sync last 500 by byRoomTime     -- the horizon: a device acquires the newest N per group; older rows are online-only\n\ntable posts:\n  authorId: principal\n  body: text <=500\n  score: int\n  at: time\n  by byAuthorTime: authorId, at, id\n  by byTime: at, id\n  public 'posts are public'           -- the read rule as a table line, with its reason\n  insert <- .authorId = viewer\n  update <- deny\n  delete <- .authorId = viewer\n  sync public last 200 by byTime      -- everyone holds the same rows\n\ntable follows:\n  followerId: principal\n  followedId: principal\n  unique byPair: followerId, followedId\n  by byFollowed: followedId, followerId\n  cap 1000 by followerId\n  read <- .followerId = viewer        -- exactly the audience of the sync line below\n  insert <- .followerId = viewer\n  delete <- .followerId = viewer\n  sync to .followerId                 -- each row reaches the principal in the column\n\ntable reactions:\n  postId: posts\n  principal: principal\n  direction: int\n  unique byPostPrincipal: postId, principal\n  by byPrincipal: principal, id\n  read <- .principal = viewer\n  insert <- .principal = viewer\n  update <- .principal = viewer\n  delete <- .principal = viewer\n  sync to .principal last 500 by byPrincipal\n\ntable profiles:\n  principal: principal\n  handle: text 3..20 format handle    -- a text format is checked on every write\n  site: text <=200 format url ?\n  unique byPrincipal: principal\n  unique byHandle: handle\n  public 'profiles are public'\n  insert <- .principal = viewer\n  update <- .principal = viewer\n  delete <- deny\n  online only                         -- optional; no sync line has the same meaning\n\ntable ledger:\n  ownerId: principal\n  amount: money USD                   -- money CUR [scale] (2 unless given) and decimal S hold integer minor units\n  weight: decimal 2\n  note: json <=2000 ?\n  at: time\n  by byOwnerTime: ownerId, at, id\n  read <- .ownerId = viewer\n  insert <- .ownerId = viewer\n  update <- deny\n  delete <- deny\n\nmaintain messageCounts: count messages by roomId       -- an aggregate the engine keeps: read it by group and get the number, 0 when the group has no row\n  read <- exists members[.roomId, viewer]\nmaintain scoreTotals: sum posts of score by authorId   -- count, or sum of an int, decimal or money column\n  read <- allow\n  online only                         -- opt out of inheriting public sync\n\nshape card = { id, name, owner: .ownerId, tagCount: count(.tags) }   -- a named shape: `.` is the row; `row card` and `page card` use it\nfn messageBody(m: messages): m.body                                  -- a row argument keeps its fields at this call site\nfn messageById(m: messages): (messages[m] ! else NOT_FOUND).body      -- a reference argument stays a reference\nfn isBrief(ttl: int ?): ttl != null                                  -- a helper expression, expanded where it is called\nfn stamp(roomId: rooms):                                             -- a helper body, expanded with its caller's write authority\n  update rooms[roomId] { createdAt: now }\n  return\nfn tally(n: int):\n  total = 0\n  for i in range(0, 1 + 1):\n    total = total + n\n  return total\n\nquery room(roomId: rooms):            -- a query reads; its result type is inferred onto api.ts\n  return rooms[roomId] card           -- one row by a unique key: null when absent or hidden; then the named shape\n\nquery helperRows(messageId: messages):\n  m = messages[messageId] ! else NOT_FOUND\n  return { body: messageBody(m), byId: messageById(messageId) }\n\nquery thread(roomId: rooms, c: cursor ?):                            -- `cursor ?` is the page argument; an omitted optional argument is null\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER              -- a refusal with the program's own code\n  return messages[roomId] after c last 50 by byRoomTime where .body != null and exists members[.roomId, viewer] { *, room: rooms[.roomId], count: messageCounts[.roomId] }   -- a page from a cursor, shaped: `*` spreads the row; a point read inside is null for a hidden row\n\nquery inbox(c: cursor ?):\n  return members[viewer] after c first 50 by byPrincipalRoom { roomId, room: rooms[.roomId], unread: messageCounts[.roomId] }\n\nquery following(c: cursor ?):\n  page = merge posts after c last 20 by byAuthorTime:               -- one ordered page over several prefixes of one index\n    [viewer]\n    [f.followedId] for f in follows[viewer] first 20 by byPair\n  return page { *, author: profiles[principal = .authorId], mine: reactions[.id, viewer] }\n\nquery ancestors(roomId: rooms):\n  chain = walk rooms[roomId] up .parentId depth 8                   -- the row, its parent, and so on: at most `depth` rows\n  return chain { id, name }\n\nquery digest(roomId: rooms):\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  page = messages[roomId, at >= now - 86400000] last 100 by byRoomTime                     -- a page bound to a name; count, sum, slice, sort and shapes take it\n  (weeks, days) = divmod(count(page), 7)                             -- divmod binds quotient and remainder at once\n  (lo, hi) = sorted(weeks, days)                                     -- two values in order\n  counter = 0\n  for message in page:\n    counter = counter + 1                                           -- a local can carry a counter across iterations\n  offsets = []\n  for i in range(0, 3):\n    if i = 2:\n      continue                                                      -- advances the nearest for or chunk\n    else if i < 0:\n      break                                                         -- else if is a nested conditional\n    offsets = offsets + [i]                                         -- append in place, under the heap meter\n  label = lower(trim(' DIGEST ')) + ': ' + join(['room', 'messages'], ' / ')\n  quotient = counter / 7\n  doubled = tally(counter)                                          -- a helper body also yields a value in an expression\n  remainder = counter % 7                                          -- the same Euclidean parts as divmod; zero refuses E_DIV_ZERO\n  head = first(page)\n  if head != null and head.body != null:\n    bodySize = count(head.body)                                     -- a null guard narrows the snapshot field through the rest of this block\n  sum = sum(page, .at)\n  grouped = group(page, 'authorId') { author: .key, count: count(.items) }\n  return { sum, grouped, first: first(page), last: last(page), at: at(page, 1), total: messageCounts[roomId], counter, offsets, label, labelSize: count(label), doubled, quotient, remainder, weeks, days, lo, hi, brief: isBrief(null), oldest: sort(slice(page, 0, 10), 'at') { id, at }, smaller: min(weeks, days), larger: max(weeks, days) }\n\nquery mentions(body: text <=4000):\n  return tokens(body)                 -- the @mentions in a text, without the @, at most 64: a bounded list\n\nquery search(roomId: rooms, q: text <=100, c: cursor ?):\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  return messages[roomId] matching q after c last 50 by byRoomWords   -- word-prefix search: every term a prefix of some word of the row, newest first\n\nquery everywhere(q: text <=100, c: cursor ?):\n  return merge messages matching q after c last 50 by byRoomWords:\n    [m.roomId] for m in members[viewer] first 50 by byPrincipalRoom\n\nquery online(p: principal):\n  return connected[p]                 -- how many connections the principal holds open on the server; `exists connected[p]` tests (guide presence)\n\nmutation pagePass(roomId: rooms): server\n  n = 0\n  for row in members[roomId] first 10 by byRoomPrincipal:\n    n = n + 1\n  return n\n\nmutation createRoom(name: text 1..80, kind: enum('open', 'closed'), tags: [text <=20] <=8):\n  room = insert rooms { id: new, name, ownerId: viewer, kind, tags }   -- `new` mints an id; omit `id` and one is minted anyway\n  insert members { roomId: room.id, principal: viewer, role: 'admin', joinedAt: now }\n  upsert rooms[room.id] { createdAt: now }                            -- patches the existing room; name, owner, kind and tags stay\n  return room card\n\nmutation sendBrief(roomId: rooms, body: text <=4000 ?, ttl: int ?):\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  row = insert messages { roomId, authorId: viewer, body, at: now, expiresAt: now + ttl if ttl != null else null }   -- a conditional value: the arm not taken never runs, and `ttl` is present in the taken one\n  for m in members[roomId] first 100 by byRoomPrincipal:\n    if m.principal != viewer and not exists connected[m.principal]:\n      emit notify { targetUserId: m.principal, roomId, preview: slice(body ?? '', 0, 80) }   -- kept in this commit; a worker claims and settles it (guide effects)\n  return { id: row.id, brief: isBrief(ttl), mentions: count(tokens(body ?? '')) }                                 -- `??` is the value when the left is null\n\nmutation edit(messageId: messages, body: text <=4000, expected: text <=4000 ?):\n  msg = messages[messageId] ! else NOT_FOUND                         -- the row, or refuse with the code; `msg` is present from here on\n  require msg.authorId = viewer else NOT_AUTHOR\n  update messages[msg] { body, editedAt: now } if .body = expected    -- a row as the key; `if` makes the update conditional: E_CONFLICT with the current row when false\n  return null                                                        -- a bare `return` is the same\n\nmutation join(roomId: rooms, principal: principal):\n  require exists members[roomId = roomId, principal = viewer, role = 'admin'] by byRoomPrincipalRole else NOT_ADMIN\n  return insert members { roomId, principal, role: 'member', joinedAt: now } if absent   -- the row, or null on a unique clash\n\nmutation leave(roomId: rooms):\n  delete members[roomId = roomId, principal = viewer]                -- a key may name its columns; a full unique key names one row, NOT_FOUND when it is missing\n  return null\n\nmutation react(postId: posts, direction: int):\n  require direction = 1 or direction = -1 else BAD_DIRECTION         -- =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, +, -, *, unary -, not, and, or\n  upsert reactions[postId, viewer] { direction }                     -- insert or patch; the key names the row; a final write is the implicit return\n\nmutation post(bodies: [text <=500] <=10):\n  for body in bodies:                                                -- a loop over a bounded list; `for row in page:` and `for i in range(0, 10):` are the other domains\n    insert posts { authorId: viewer, body, score: 0, at: now }\n  return count(bodies)\n\nmutation split(total: int, people: [principal] <=8):\n  insert ledger { ownerId: viewer, amount: share(total, people, viewer), weight: 1, at: now }   -- share: one person's part of an amount split evenly, deterministically\n\njob nightly(periodStart: time, periodEnd: time):                    -- the server's own work: sweeps as the system principal, one page per commit\n  end = periodEnd                                                   -- the prelude runs again at the start of every chunk, under that chunk's meter\n  chunk r in rooms first 100 by byId:                                -- the index's columns are id or immutable, so nothing moves under the cursor\n    if r.createdAt >= end:\n      break                                                          -- ends this sweep; `return` ends the job\n    stamp(r.id)\n  chunk p in posts first 100 by byId:\n    for i in range(0, 2):                                            -- int expressions, under the step meter\n      update posts[p.id] { score: p.score + i }\nschedule everyNight every 1d at 03:00: timeline.nightly                       -- once per period boundary of the server's clock: every 2m | 1h | 1d [at HH:MM]\njob rescoreNative(): native                                          -- a job whose body is the app's own Rust in snapback/native/, hosted as wasm (guide native)\nquery personalizeNative(first: int): native                          -- a read in the same module: on the server as the viewer, on a device over its rows\n"]]]

93d05d65b6:snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/tests/lowering/r1p-sources.jsonl:425:["92bc2b2640bd55a919647f317bc186987a0d28f17c015684d169563ce97853b3",[["schema.q","use identity                          -- guests and password accounts; `use identity guests` or `use identity password` admits one kind\nuse personas alice, bob, carol        -- a development cast: `--as alice` and the persona header act as dev:alice\neffect notify                         -- a name a mutation or job may `emit` under; a worker with a service token performs it (guide effects)\n\ntable rooms:\n  name: text 1..80                    -- text <=N | text M..N, either with `format handle` or `format url`\n  ownerId: principal                  -- principal | id | <table> (a reference to its row) | int | time (milliseconds) | bool\n  kind: enum('open', 'closed')        -- enum('a', 'b') | decimal S | money CUR [S] | json <=N | bytes <=N | image <=N [once] | video <=N\n  tags: [text <=20] <=8               -- [type] <=N: a bounded list\n  parentId: rooms ?                   -- `?` makes a column optional: null when absent. Every table has an implicit `id` and a unique `byId`\n  createdAt: time default now          -- omitted on insert; evaluated on the writing host\n  by byOwner: ownerId, createdAt, id  -- `by` orders; a scan pins the leading columns and pages along the rest\n  read <- exists members[.id, viewer]                                     -- rules: allow | deny | public ['why'] | .col = viewer | .col != 'x' | exists t[..] | created t[..] | and | or | not\n  insert <- .ownerId = viewer\n  update (old, next) <- old.ownerId = viewer and next.ownerId = viewer   -- an update rule may name both images\n  delete <- deny\n  after insert <- exists members[roomId = .id, principal = .ownerId, role = 'admin']                 -- a row that must exist by the end of the mutation that inserted this one\n  sync to members[.id]                -- each row reaches every principal with a members row whose roomId is this row's id\n\ntable members:\n  roomId: rooms\n  principal: principal\n  role: enum('member', 'admin')\n  joinedAt: time\n  unique byRoomPrincipal: roomId, principal            -- `unique` orders and constrains\n  by byRoomPrincipalRole: roomId, principal, role\n  by byPrincipalRoom: principal, roomId, id\n  cap 100 by roomId                                    -- at most N rows per group; needs an index leading with the group\n  immutable roomId, principal                          -- columns no update may change\n  read <- exists members[.roomId, viewer]\n  insert <- exists members[roomId = .roomId, principal = viewer, role = 'admin'] or created rooms[.roomId]   -- created: this mutation inserted the probed row\n  delete <- .principal = viewer or exists members[roomId = .roomId, principal = viewer, role = 'admin']\n  sync to members[.roomId]\n\ntable messages:\n  roomId: rooms\n  authorId: principal\n  body: text <=4000 ?\n  photo: image <=10000000 ?           -- an upload the row holds (guide assets); `once` after the bound serves one view per principal\n  clip: video <=50000000 ?\n  editedAt: time ?\n  expiresAt: time ?\n  at: time\n  by byRoomTime: roomId, at, id\n  by byRoomWords: roomId, words(body), at, id   -- a words index: one entry per distinct word of the text columns; read with `matching` (guide search)\n  by byExpiresAt: expiresAt\n  immutable roomId, authorId\n  read <- exists members[.roomId, viewer]\n  insert <- .authorId = viewer and exists members[.roomId, viewer]\n  update <- .authorId = viewer\n  delete <- .authorId = viewer\n  retain delivered-history            -- a device keeps what it was given after it leaves the group; `until-revoked` (the default) drops it\n  expire at .expiresAt                -- a row past that time is absent everywhere at once, then swept; a null time never expires\n  sync last 500 by byRoomTime     -- the horizon: a device acquires the newest N per group; older rows are online-only\n\ntable posts:\n  authorId: principal\n  body: text <=500\n  score: int\n  at: time\n  by byAuthorTime: authorId, at, id\n  by byTime: at, id\n  public 'posts are public'           -- the read rule as a table line, with its reason\n  insert <- .authorId = viewer\n  update <- deny\n  delete <- .authorId = viewer\n  sync public last 200 by byTime      -- everyone holds the same rows\n\ntable follows:\n  followerId: principal\n  followedId: principal\n  unique byPair: followerId, followedId\n  by byFollowed: followedId, followerId\n  cap 1000 by followerId\n  read <- .followerId = viewer        -- exactly the audience of the sync line below\n  insert <- .followerId = viewer\n  delete <- .followerId = viewer\n  sync to .followerId                 -- each row reaches the principal in the column\n\ntable reactions:\n  postId: posts\n  principal: principal\n  direction: int\n  unique byPostPrincipal: postId, principal\n  by byPrincipal: principal, id\n  read <- .principal = viewer\n  insert <- .principal = viewer\n  update <- .principal = viewer\n  delete <- .principal = viewer\n  sync to .principal last 500 by byPrincipal\n\ntable profiles:\n  principal: principal\n  handle: text 3..20 format handle    -- a text format is checked on every write\n  site: text <=200 format url ?\n  unique byPrincipal: principal\n  unique byHandle: handle\n  public 'profiles are public'\n  insert <- .principal = viewer\n  update <- .principal = viewer\n  delete <- deny\n  online only                         -- optional; no sync line has the same meaning\n\ntable ledger:\n  ownerId: principal\n  amount: money USD                   -- money CUR [scale] (2 unless given) and decimal S hold integer minor units\n  weight: decimal 2\n  note: json <=2000 ?\n  at: time\n  by byOwnerTime: ownerId, at, id\n  read <- .ownerId = viewer\n  insert <- .ownerId = viewer\n  update <- deny\n  delete <- deny\n\nmaintain messageCounts: count messages by roomId       -- an aggregate the engine keeps: read it by group and get the number, 0 when the group has no row\n  read <- exists members[.roomId, viewer]\nmaintain scoreTotals: sum posts of score by authorId   -- count, or sum of an int, decimal or money column\n  read <- allow\n  online only                         -- opt out of inheriting public sync\n\nshape card = { id, name, owner: .ownerId, tagCount: count(.tags) }   -- a named shape: `.` is the row; `row card` and `page card` use it\nfn messageBody(m: messages): m.body                                  -- a row argument keeps its fields at this call site\nfn messageById(m: messages): (messages[m] ! else NOT_FOUND).body      -- a reference argument stays a reference\nfn isBrief(ttl: int ?): ttl != null                                  -- a helper expression, expanded where it is called\nfn stamp(roomId: rooms):                                             -- a helper body, expanded with its caller's write authority\n  update rooms[roomId] { createdAt: now }\n  return\nfn tally(n: int):\n  total = 0\n  for i in range(0, 1 + 1):\n    total = total + n\n  return total\n\nquery room(roomId: rooms):            -- a query reads; its result type is inferred onto api.ts\n  return rooms[roomId] card           -- one row by a unique key: null when absent or hidden; then the named shape\n\nquery helperRows(messageId: messages):\n  m = messages[messageId] ! else NOT_FOUND\n  return { body: messageBody(m), byId: messageById(messageId) }\n\nquery thread(roomId: rooms, c: cursor ?):                            -- `cursor ?` is the page argument; an omitted optional argument is null\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER              -- a refusal with the program's own code\n  return messages[roomId] after c last 50 by byRoomTime where .body != null and exists members[.roomId, viewer] { *, room: rooms[.roomId], count: messageCounts[.roomId] }   -- a page from a cursor, shaped: `*` spreads the row; a point read inside is null for a hidden row\n\nquery inbox(c: cursor ?):\n  return members[viewer] after c first 50 by byPrincipalRoom { roomId, room: rooms[.roomId], unread: messageCounts[.roomId] }\n\nquery following(c: cursor ?):\n  page = merge posts after c last 20 by byAuthorTime:               -- one ordered page over several prefixes of one index\n    [viewer]\n    [f.followedId] for f in follows[viewer] first 20 by byPair\n  return page { *, author: profiles[principal = .authorId], mine: reactions[.id, viewer] }\n\nquery ancestors(roomId: rooms):\n  chain = walk rooms[roomId] up .parentId depth 8                   -- the row, its parent, and so on: at most `depth` rows\n  return chain { id, name }\n\nquery digest(roomId: rooms):\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  page = messages[roomId, at >= now - 86400000] last 100 by byRoomTime                     -- a page bound to a name; count, sum, slice, sort and shapes take it\n  (weeks, days) = divmod(count(page), 7)                             -- divmod binds quotient and remainder at once\n  (lo, hi) = sorted(weeks, days)                                     -- two values in order\n  counter = 0\n  for message in page:\n    counter = counter + 1                                           -- a local can carry a counter across iterations\n  offsets = []\n  for i in range(0, 3):\n    if i = 2:\n      continue                                                      -- advances the nearest for or chunk\n    else if i < 0:\n      break                                                         -- else if is a nested conditional\n    offsets = offsets + [i]                                         -- append in place, under the heap meter\n  label = lower(trim(' DIGEST ')) + ': ' + join(['room', 'messages'], ' / ')\n  quotient = counter / 7\n  doubled = tally(counter)                                          -- a helper body also yields a value in an expression\n  remainder = counter % 7                                          -- the same Euclidean parts as divmod; zero refuses E_DIV_ZERO\n  head = first(page)\n  if head != null and head.body != null:\n    bodySize = count(head.body)                                     -- a null guard narrows the snapshot field through the rest of this block\n  sum = sum(page, .at)\n  grouped = group(page, 'authorId') { author: .key, count: count(.items) }\n  return { sum, grouped, first: first(page), last: last(page), at: at(page, 1), total: messageCounts[roomId], counter, offsets, label, labelSize: count(label), doubled, quotient, remainder, weeks, days, lo, hi, brief: isBrief(null), oldest: sort(slice(page, 0, 10), 'at') { id, at }, smaller: min(weeks, days), larger: max(weeks, days) }\n\nquery mentions(body: text <=4000):\n  return tokens(body)                 -- the @mentions in a text, without the @, at most 64: a bounded list\n\nquery search(roomId: rooms, q: text <=100, c: cursor ?):\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  return messages[roomId] matching q after c last 50 by byRoomWords   -- word-prefix search: every term a prefix of some word of the row, newest first\n\nquery everywhere(q: text <=100, c: cursor ?):\n  return merge messages matching q after c last 50 by byRoomWords:\n    [m.roomId] for m in members[viewer] first 50 by byPrincipalRoom\n\nquery online(p: principal):\n  return connected[p]                 -- how many connections the principal holds open on the server; `exists connected[p]` tests (guide presence)\n\nmutation pagePass(roomId: rooms): server\n  n = 0\n  for row in members[roomId] first 10 by byRoomPrincipal:\n    n = n + 1\n  return n\n\nmutation createRoom(name: text 1..80, kind: enum('open', 'closed'), tags: [text <=20] <=8):\n  room = insert rooms { id: new, name, ownerId: viewer, kind, tags }   -- `new` mints an id; omit `id` and one is minted anyway\n  insert members { roomId: room.id, principal: viewer, role: 'admin', joinedAt: now }\n  upsert rooms[room.id] { createdAt: now }                            -- patches the existing room; name, owner, kind and tags stay\n  return room card\n\nmutation sendBrief(roomId: rooms, body: text <=4000 ?, ttl: int ?):\n  require exists members[roomId, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  row = insert messages { roomId, authorId: viewer, body, at: now, expiresAt: now + ttl if ttl != null else null }   -- a conditional value: the arm not taken never runs, and `ttl` is present in the taken one\n  for m in members[roomId] first 100 by byRoomPrincipal:\n    if m.principal != viewer and not exists connected[m.principal]:\n      emit notify { targetUserId: m.principal, roomId, preview: slice(body ?? '', 0, 80) }   -- kept in this commit; a worker claims and settles it (guide effects)\n  return { id: row.id, brief: isBrief(ttl), mentions: count(tokens(body ?? '')) }                                 -- `??` is the value when the left is null\n\nmutation edit(messageId: messages, body: text <=4000, expected: text <=4000 ?):\n  msg = messages[messageId] ! else NOT_FOUND                         -- the row, or refuse with the code; `msg` is present from here on\n  require msg.authorId = viewer else NOT_AUTHOR\n  update messages[msg] { body, editedAt: now } if .body = expected    -- a row as the key; `if` makes the update conditional: E_CONFLICT with the current row when false\n  return null                                                        -- a bare `return` is the same\n\nmutation join(roomId: rooms, principal: principal):\n  require exists members[roomId = roomId, principal = viewer, role = 'admin'] by byRoomPrincipalRole else NOT_ADMIN\n  return insert members { roomId, principal, role: 'member', joinedAt: now } if absent   -- the row, or null on a unique clash\n\nmutation leave(roomId: rooms):\n  delete members[roomId = roomId, principal = viewer]                -- a key may name its columns; a full unique key names one row, NOT_FOUND when it is missing\n  return null\n\nmutation react(postId: posts, direction: int):\n  require direction = 1 or direction = -1 else BAD_DIRECTION         -- =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, +, -, *, unary -, not, and, or\n  upsert reactions[postId, viewer] { direction }                     -- insert or patch; the key names the row; a final write is the implicit return\n\nmutation post(bodies: [text <=500] <=10):\n  for body in bodies:                                                -- a loop over a bounded list; `for row in page:` and `for i in range(0, 10):` are the other domains\n    insert posts { authorId: viewer, body, score: 0, at: now }\n  return count(bodies)\n\nmutation split(total: int, people: [principal] <=8):\n  insert ledger { ownerId: viewer, amount: share(total, people, viewer), weight: 1, at: now }   -- share: one person's part of an amount split evenly, deterministically\n\njob nightly(periodStart: time, periodEnd: time):                    -- the server's own work: sweeps as the system principal, one page per commit\n  end = periodEnd                                                   -- the prelude runs again at the start of every chunk, under that chunk's meter\n  chunk r in rooms first 100 by byId:                                -- the index's columns are id or immutable, so nothing moves under the cursor\n    if r.createdAt >= end:\n      break                                                          -- ends this sweep; `return` ends the job\n    stamp(r.id)\n  chunk p in posts first 100 by byId:\n    for i in range(0, 2):                                            -- int expressions, under the step meter\n      update posts[p.id] { score: p.score + i }\nschedule everyNight every 1d at 03:00: nightly                       -- once per period boundary of the server's clock: every 2m | 1h | 1d [at HH:MM]\njob rescoreNative(): native                                          -- a job whose body is the app's own Rust in snapback/native/, hosted as wasm (guide native)\nquery personalizeNative(first: int): native                          -- a read in the same module: on the server as the viewer, on a device over its rows\n\naction invite(email: text <=200)\naction refreshModel() <- viewer = 'service:ranker'\n"]]]

//! Sequence custody starts with activation/allocation, never a legacy open.
// @ref LLP 3000.017#3.6 — preserve published capability fences.
use super::*;

impl Tx<'_> {
    pub(super) fn has_sequence_table(&self) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if let Some(exists) = self.sequence_table.get() { return Ok(exists); }
        let exists = self.conn().prepare_cached("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = '_sequences')")?.query_row([], |r| r.get(0))?;
        self.sequence_table.set(Some(exists));
        Ok(exists)
    }
    pub(super) fn ensure_sequence_table(&self) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        if self.has_sequence_table()? { return Ok(()); }
        self.conn().execute_batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sequences (parent TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, value INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(parent, id)) WITHOUT ROWID;")?;
        self.sequence_table.set(Some(true));
        Ok(())
    }
}

table conversations:
  title: text <=100
  read <- allow
  insert <- allow
  sync public
table members:
  conversationId: conversations
  principal: principal
  readUpTo: int default 0
  joinedAt: int default 0
  unique conversationId, principal
  cap 100 by conversationId
  read <- allow
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  delete <- allow
  sync public
table messages:
  conversationId: conversations
  ordinal: int
  senderId: principal
  tombstone: bool default false
  until: time ?

  read <- allow
  insert <- allow
  update <- allow
  delete <- allow
  sync public
view unread: count messages by members m
  where .conversationId = m.conversationId and .ordinal > m.readUpTo
    and .senderId != m.principal and not .tombstone and .ordinal > m.joinedAt
query unreadFor(member: members):
  return unread[member]
query unreadRows():
  return unread first 100
mutation join(id: id, conversationId: conversations, principal: principal, readUpTo: int, joinedAt: int):

  insert messages { id, conversationId, ordinal, senderId, until }

mutation remove(message: messages):

mutation leave(member: members):

fn title(value: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = value.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().collect::<String>() + chars.as_str(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}
