   198	    if let Err(error) = require_query(program) { return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default()); }
   199	    if let Err(error) = validate_inputs(schema, program, &mut context.args) {
   200	        return (Err(error.refusal()), false, false, Default::default());
   201	    }
   202	    let args = context.args.clone();
   203	    let now = context.now.unwrap_or(0);
   204	    context.row_provenance |= schema.tables.values().any(|t| t.leave == crate::schema::LeavePolicy::DeliveredHistory);

   206	    runner.device = true;
   207	    let (value, mut runner) = super::native::run_read(module, runner, &program.name, &args, now);
   208	    let result = (|| {
   209	        let data = match value {
   210	            Ok(data) => data,
   211	            Err(_) if runner.query_unavailable => Value::Null,
   212	            Err(error) => return Err(error.refusal()),
   213	        };
   214	        let data = if runner.query_unavailable { Value::Null } else { data };
   215	        runner.charge_output(&data)?;

   218	            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] delivery_meter: None, ephemeral: None,
   219	            unavailable: runner.query_unavailable,

   222	            capped_at: runner.meter.capped_at.clone(),
   223	            word_cut_at: runner.word_cut_at.clone(),

   225	            data,

   238	    pub(super) fn withhold_unheld_card(&mut self, table: &str) {

   244	    // @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.2 — device-only authority work may prevent
   245	    // prediction, but cannot spend the server-equivalent mutation budget.
   246	    pub(super) fn device_work<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   247	        let Some(allowance) = self.device_allowance.take() else { return work(self) };
   248	        let outer_active = self.device_work_active;
   249	        let (caller, entered) = self.enter_device_work(allowance);
   250	        let result = entered.and_then(|_| work(self));
   251	        self.leave_device_work(caller, result.as_ref().err(), outer_active)?;
   252	        result
   253	    }
   254	
   255	    // Shared by every device_work instantiation (wasm size): swap in the
   256	    // device allowance and charge its step; returns the caller's meter.
   257	    #[inline(never)]
   258	    fn enter_device_work(&mut self, mut meter: Meter) -> (Meter, Result<(), RuntimeError>) {
   259	        std::mem::swap(&mut self.meter, &mut meter);
   260	        self.device_work_active = true;
   261	        let step = self.meter.step(1);
   262	        (meter, step)
   263	    }
   264	
   265	    /// Restore the caller's meter; an exhausted allowance cannot refuse the write.
   266	    #[inline(never)]
   267	    fn leave_device_work(&mut self, mut caller: Meter, error: Option<&RuntimeError>, outer_active: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   268	        self.device_work_active = outer_active;
   269	        std::mem::swap(&mut self.meter, &mut caller);
   270	        self.device_allowance = Some(caller);
   271	        match error {
   272	            Some(RuntimeError::Bound { .. }) => Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("device authority allowance exhausted; queued without a predicted row".into())),
   273	            _ => Ok(()),
   274	        }
   275	    }
   276	
   277	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#18.2 — retained history suppresses fallback only when no independent unknown or incomplete reason remains.
   278	    fn only_retained_incomplete(&self) -> bool {
   279	        self.missing_fact.is_none() && self.meter.capped_at.is_none() && self.word_cut_at.is_none() && !self.non_uniform && !self.page_overflow && !self.page_position_lost() && !self.timeline_pending && !self.presence_unknown
   280	    }
   281	
   282	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#6.2 — preserve the first undecidable site's evaluated key.
   283	    pub(crate) fn unknown_fact(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value], site: &str) {
   284	        self.beyond_horizon = true;
   285	        self.components.note(|frame| { frame.beyond = true; frame.unknown = true; });
   286	        if self.missing_fact.is_none() {
   287	            let key = crate::wire::to_json(&Value::Array(key.to_vec()));
   288	            self.missing_fact = Some(format!("site {site}: this device cannot establish {table} by {index} at key {key}; the row or its absence is past the acquired horizon or online only"));
   289	        }
   290	    }
   291	}

   163	pub(super) struct PrepaidState {
   164	    mark: crate::meter::MeterMark,
   165	    ceilings: Ceilings,
   166	    cut: Cut,
   167	    authorizing: bool,
   168	    nested: bool,

   171	impl Runner<'_> {
   172	    // @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — declaration-only scratch is admitted before any
   173	    // candidate/witness access. The logical heap retains only disclosed output.
   174	    pub(super) fn authorized_scratch<T: Default>(&mut self, bytes: u64, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   175	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   176	        self.reserved_scratch(bytes, allowance, true, work)
   177	    }
   178	
   179	    /// Count certification follows an admitted member and source-group verdict.
   180	    /// Nested authorization still shares any enclosing physical allowance.
   181	    pub(super) fn disclosed_scratch<T: Default>(&mut self, bytes: u64, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   182	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   183	        self.reserved_scratch(bytes, allowance, false, work)
   184	    }
   185	
   186	    pub(super) fn reserved_scratch<T: Default>(&mut self, bytes: u64, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], physical: bool, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   187	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   188	        if self.device_work_active || self.context.is_system() { return self.prepaid_scan(allowance, physical, work); }
   189	        let mark = self.meter.mark();
   190	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   191	        let result = self.prepaid_scan(allowance, physical, work);
   192	        self.meter.release_row_heap(mark, bytes);
   193	        result
   194	    }

   196	    pub(super) fn rule_scratch(&self, rule: &crate::schema::RuleExpr) -> u64 {
   197	        let mut sites = Vec::new();
   198	        super::rules::probe_sites(rule, &mut sites);
   199	        sites.iter().map(|(table, _)| self.witness_scratch(table)).max().unwrap_or(0)
   200	    }
   201	
   202	    pub(super) fn witness_scratch(&self, table: &str) -> u64 {
   203	        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
   204	        let own = crate::rows::disclosed::admission(definition);
   205	        let source = self.schema.maintain_for(table)
   206	            .and_then(|m| self.schema.table(&m.source)).filter(|source| source.is_expiring());
   207	        own.saturating_add(source.map_or(0, crate::rows::disclosed::admission))
   208	    }

   210	
   211	    /// Ordinary data reads keep their existing meter and cut semantics. This
   212	    /// scope grants storage access without disabling or restoring any charge.
   213	    /// Hidden authorization must use authorized_scan's prepaid reservation.
   214	    pub(crate) fn metered_scan<T>(&mut self, scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   215	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   216	        scan(self, &Authorization::internal())
   217	    }
   218	
   219	    /// A rule whose logical allowance the caller has already charged, possibly
   220	    /// to a cut, still evaluates its witnesses under the physical allowance;
   221	    /// the caller decides what its cut means for the answer (LLP 3000.014 §5).
   222	    pub(super) fn prepaid_witnesses<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   223	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   224	        let active = self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || !self.context.is_system());
   225	        let result = work(self, &Authorization::internal());
   226	        self.tx.authorizing.set(active);
   227	        result
   228	    }
   229	
   230	    // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — admission depends on declared bounds, never on
   231	    // occupants. Private scratch cannot cut the caller's prepaid scan.
   232	    pub(crate) fn authorized_scan<T: Default>(&mut self, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   233	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   234	        self.prepaid_scan(allowance, true, scan)
   235	    }
   236	
   237	    /// Public or already-authorized data reads still reserve their logical
   238	    /// meter; they do no authorization traversal. A nested scope cannot opt
   239	    /// out of its enclosing authorization's physical allowance.
   240	    pub(super) fn prepaid_scan<T: Default>(&mut self, allowance: &[(MeterKind, u64)], physical: bool, scan: impl FnOnce(&mut Self, &Authorization) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>,
   241	    ) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   242	        // This meter is the device's separate physical-work budget. Its
   243	        // caller maps exhaustion to uncertainty, never a logical E_BOUND.
   244	        if self.device_work_active {
   245	            let active = self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || (physical && !self.context.is_system()));
   246	            let result = scan(self, &Authorization::internal());
   247	            self.tx.authorizing.set(active);
   248	            return result;
   249	        }
   250	        for &(kind, amount) in allowance {
   251	            if !self.read_charge(kind, amount)? { return Ok(T::default()); }
   252	        }
   253	        if self.read_capped() { return Ok(T::default()); }
   254	        let scope = Authorization { probes: Cell::new(0), remaining_probes: self.meter.ceilings.rule_probes.saturating_sub(self.meter.used.rule_probes) };
   255	        let state = self.enter_prepaid(physical);
   256	        let result = scan(self, &scope);
   257	        self.leave_prepaid(state, result.as_ref().err());
   258	        if scope.probes.get() > 0 { self.read_charge(MeterKind::RuleProbes, scope.probes.get())?; }
   259	        result
   260	    }
   261	
   262	    // Kept out of the generic closure wrapper: every protected access shares
   263	    // the same scope transition instead of instantiating its restoration code.
   264	    #[inline(never)]
   265	    pub(super) fn enter_prepaid(&mut self, physical: bool) -> PrepaidState {
   266	        let nested = self.caller_heap_ceiling.is_some();
   267	        self.caller_heap_ceiling.get_or_insert((self.meter.ceilings.heap_bytes, self.meter.used.heap_bytes));
   268	        PrepaidState {
   269	            mark: self.meter.mark(),
   270	            ceilings: std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter.ceilings, Ceilings::unbounded()),
   271	            cut: std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter.cut, Cut::Abort),
   272	            authorizing: self.tx.authorizing.replace(self.tx.authorizing.get() || (physical && !self.context.is_system())),
   273	            nested,
   274	        }
   275	    }
   276	
   277	    #[inline(never)]
   278	    pub(super) fn leave_prepaid(&mut self, state: PrepaidState, error: Option<&RuntimeError>) {
   279	        self.tx.authorizing.set(state.authorizing);
   280	        self.meter.restore(state.mark);
   281	        self.meter.ceilings = state.ceilings;
   282	        self.meter.cut = state.cut;
   283	        if !state.nested { self.caller_heap_ceiling = None; }
   284	        if let Some(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: MeterKind::HeapBytes, site, .. }) = error {
   285	            self.meter.capped_at.get_or_insert((MeterKind::HeapBytes, site.clone()));
   286	        }
   287	    }
   288	
   289	}

   933	    fn contribution_heap(&self, table: &Table) -> u64 {
   934	        table.indexes.values().fold(0, |bytes: u64, index| match index.components.first() {
   935	            Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) => bytes.saturating_add(
   936	                super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.target]).saturating_mul(16)),
   937	            _ => bytes,
   938	        })
   939	    }
   940	
   941	    fn charge_source_indexes(&mut self, table: &Table, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>, mut entries: u64) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   942	        for index in table.indexes.values() {
   943	            if let Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() {
   944	                self.charge_maintain(MeterKind::Steps, maintain.evaluation_steps() * (u64::from(old.is_some()) + u64::from(new.is_some())))?;
   945	            }
   946	        }
   947	        if self.maintain_prepaid {
   948	            let id = old.or(new).expect("source image").field("id")?.as_str()?;
   949	            for index in table.indexes.values() {
   950	                if matches!(index.components.first(), Some(crate::schema::IndexComponent::Contribution(_))) {
   951	                    let before = old.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   952	                    let after = new.map(|row| crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table, index, row, id)).unwrap_or_default();
   953	                    let changed = before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)).count() + after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)).count();
   954	                    entries = entries.saturating_sub(changed as u64);
   955	                }
   956	            }
   957	        }
   958	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, entries)?;
   959	        Ok(())
   960	    }

//! Internal contribution format adoption under the evaluation adapter's writer lock.
use super::store::Tx;
use crate::{error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError}, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::{adoption, word_heap as heap}, schema::{IndexComponent, Schema, Table}, value::{Value, canonical_json}};

pub(super) fn install(tx: &Tx<'_>, schema: &mut Schema) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    let backend = tx.query("SELECT schema,generation FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
    let previous: Schema = super::store::decode(backend[0].get(0))?;
    let mut generation = backend[0].get::<_, i64>(1);
    schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
    if *schema != previous {
        for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
            for (index_name, index) in &table.indexes {
                let Some(IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() else {continue};
                if previous.table(name).and_then(|t|t.index(index_name)) == Some(index) {continue;}
                tx.execute("DELETE FROM i WHERE t = $1 AND ix = $2", &[name,index_name])?;
                let work=adoption::Work::DECODE.with_contribution(maintain);
                let mut after: Option<String> = None;
                loop {
                    let mut meter=Meter::new(Ceilings::job(),Cut::Abort);
                    meter.at(&format!("adopt {name}.{index_name}"));
                    meter.heap(4096 + after.as_deref().map_or(0, heap::text))?;
                    let page=source_page(&tx,name,table,after.as_deref(),&mut meter,work)?;
                    if page.is_empty() { break; }
                    for raw in &page {
                        let scratch=meter.mark();
                        let id=raw.get::<_,&str>(0);
                        let data=raw.get::<_,&str>(1);
                        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
                        adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::decode_bytes(data))?;
                        let row: Value=super::store::decode(data)?;
                        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
                        meter.step(maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
                        adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::contribution_bytes(&row,table))?;
                        for key in crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table,index,&row,id) {
                            if key.len() > crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES { return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(name,index_name,1)); }
                            meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries,1)?;
                            tx.execute("INSERT INTO i(t,ix,k,id) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)", &[name,index_name,&key,&id])?;
                        }
                        drop(row);
                        meter.release_heap(scratch);
                    }
                    let last=page.last().expect("nonempty page").get::<_,&str>(0);
                    meter.heap(heap::text(last))?;
                    after=Some(last.to_owned());
                    // The full driver-owned page remains reserved until every
                    // decoded row and its index scratch have been consumed.
                    drop(page);
                }
            }
        }
        generation=generation.checked_add(1).ok_or_else(||RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?;
        tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET schema = $1, generation = $2 WHERE singleton", &[&canonical_json(schema), &generation])?;
    }
    u64::try_from(generation).map_err(|_|RuntimeError::Generation("negative generation".into()))
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9.3 — adoption reserves fetched images separately from per-row contribution scratch.
pub(super) fn source_page(tx: &super::store::Tx<'_>, table: &str, schema: &Table, after: Option<&str>, meter: &mut Meter, work: adoption::Work) -> Result<Vec<postgres::Row>, RuntimeError> {
    let sizes=if after.is_some() {
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    } else {
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    };
    let mut limit=32i64;
    let page_mark=meter.mark();
    loop {
        limit=work.limit(meter,limit as usize) as i64;
        let size=tx.query(sizes,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
        let bytes=size[0].get::<_,i64>(0) as u64;
        let count=size[0].get::<_,i64>(1) as u64;
        // Network/read buffers, retained driver rows and their metadata. Typed
        // JSON decode is priced from borrowed text later, one row at a time;
        // the query scan's conservative 256x all-rows decoder is inappropriate
        // for this walk. This initial estimate is followed by a scratch check
        // before any adoption callback runs.
        let reservation=bytes.saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(count.saturating_mul(1024));
        if limit>1 && reservation>meter.ceilings.heap_bytes/2 { limit/=2; continue; }
        meter.heap(reservation)?;
        let query=if after.is_some() {
            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
        } else {
            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
        };
        let page=tx.query(query,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
        if adoption::page_fits(page.iter().map(|raw| raw.get::<_,&str>(1)), meter, work,
            Some(&|row| adoption::contribution_bytes(row,schema)))? { return Ok(page); }
        limit=(page.len() as i64/2).max(1);
        drop(page);
        meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
    }
}

    98	    // commit together, only after every open/adoption check has succeeded.
    99	    fn attach(client: Client, mut schema: Schema, programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>, create: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   100	        let mut store = Store::new(client);
   101	        let tx = store.opening_transaction()?;
   102	        tx.batch("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s'; SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   103	        if let Some(name) = create {
   104	            tx.batch(&format!("CREATE SCHEMA {name}; SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
   105	            tx.batch(store::DDL)?;
   106	            tx.execute("INSERT INTO _backend VALUES (true,$1,$2,$3)",
   107	                &[&store::VERSION, &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs)])?;
   108	        }
   109	        tx.query("SELECT seq FROM _head WHERE singleton FOR UPDATE", &[])?;
   110	        // Admission must use the backend that survived the wait for the head.
   111	        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.
   112	        let held = tx.query("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?.remove(0);
   113	        if held.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
   115	        }
   116	        let held_schema: Schema = decode(held.get(1))?;
   117	        let held_programs: BTreeMap<String, Program> = decode(held.get(2))?;
   118	        supported(&held_schema, &held_programs)?;
   119	        if held_schema.hash() != schema.hash() || canonical_json(&held_programs) != canonical_json(&programs) {
   120	            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend changed while opening; reopen its current generation".into()));
   121	        }
   122	        // Even a no-op ALTER takes an exclusive table lock. Reopening an
   123	        // upgraded store must remain possible while another reader holds it.
   124	        for (column, ddl) in [
   125	            ("generation", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
   126	            ("through_shortened", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN through_shortened TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"),
   127	            ("maintained_identity_version", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN maintained_identity_version TEXT"),
   128	        ] {
   129	            let exists: bool = tx.query("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = '_backend'::regclass AND attname = $1 AND NOT attisdropped)", &[&column])?[0].get(0);
   130	            if !exists { tx.batch(ddl)?; }
   131	        }
   132	        // Repeat admission under the head fence used by physical adoption.
   133	        if let Some(row) = tx.query(
   134	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
   135	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
   136	        )?.first() {
   137	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
   138	        }
   139	        tx.batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sequences (parent TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, value BIGINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(parent, id));")?;
   140	        tx.batch(store::READ_SESSIONS_DDL)?;
   141	        tx.batch("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq_kind;")?;
   142	        caps::install(&tx, &schema)?;
   143	        let generation = contribution_upgrade::install(&tx, &mut schema)?;
   144	        let generation = maintained_identity_upgrade::install(&tx, &schema, create.is_some(), generation)?;
   145	        // Retain the adapter's ordinary connection limits on successful open.
   146	        tx.batch("SET statement_timeout = '5s'; SET lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   147	        tx.commit()?;
   148	        store.generation = generation;
   149	        schema.prepare_delivery_lookup();
   150	        Ok(Self { store, schema, programs, ceilings: Ceilings::default(), mode: WriteMode::Serialized, retries: 0, precharge: Metered::default(), expiry_after: BTreeMap::new() })
   151	    }

    53	fn references(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>) {
    54	    match (kind, value) {
    55	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => references(inner, value, out),
    56	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) => {
    57	            for value in values {
    58	                references(of, value, out);
    59	            }
    60	        }
    61	        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => out.push((table.clone(), id.clone())),
    62	        _ => {}
    63	    }
    64	}

    66	fn rewrite_legacy_reference(
    67	    kind: &ColumnType,
    68	    value: &mut Value,
    69	    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
    70	) -> bool {
    71	    match (kind, value) {
    72	        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
    73	            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
    74	            *id = next.clone();
    75	            true
    76	        }
    77	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
    78	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
    79	            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
    80	        _ => false,
    81	    }
    82	}

//! The successor under the stored rows: checked narrowing is additive when
//! the data already fits. Used by both read-only check and atomic activation.
use super::*;
use crate::schema::{ColumnDefault, Constraint, materialize_optional_fields};
use crate::successor::{Change, Step};
use crate::engine::validate::{validate_column, validate_row};

pub(super) fn assess(tx: &Tx<'_>, schema: &Schema) -> Result<Vec<Step>, RuntimeError> {
    let previous: Option<String> = tx.tx.query_row("SELECT schema FROM _generations WHERE generation = (SELECT CAST(value AS INTEGER) FROM _meta WHERE key = 'generation')", [], |row| row.get(0)).optional()?;
    let Some(previous) = previous else { return Ok(Vec::new()) };
    let previous: Schema = serde_json::from_str(&previous).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::decode(e, RuntimeError::Store))?;
    let mut steps = crate::successor::classify(&previous, schema);
    let mut count_checks = BTreeMap::<String, bool>::new();
    for step in &mut steps {
        if let Some(position) = step.path.strip_prefix("maintains[").and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(']')).and_then(|s| s.parse::<usize>().ok()) {
            let maintain = &schema.maintains[position];
            // Existing activation is atomic and exhaustive. Keep its assessment
            // read-only and use the same interpreted contribution, without a write.
            if previous.tables.contains_key(&maintain.source) {
                let source = &schema.tables[&maintain.source];
                // @ref LLP 3000.000#implementation-follow-up — population proof shares validation, not sums.
                // A count's largest possible group is the entire source. Below
                // I53_MAX no predicate/key can overflow it. Validate the same
                // interpreted/captured source once for counts sharing a table;
                // sums retain their wide per-group cancellation assessment.
                let count_safe = matches!(maintain.kind, crate::schema::MaintainKind::Count)
                    && tx.tx.query_row("SELECT count(*) FROM r WHERE t = ?1", [tx.num(&maintain.source)?], |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0))? <= crate::value::I53_MAX;
                if count_safe && let Some(fits) = count_checks.get(&maintain.source) {
                    assessed(step, maintain, *fits);
                    continue;
                }
                let paths: Vec<_> = source.recorded.keys().filter(|path| !previous.tables[&maintain.source].recorded.contains_key(*path)).cloned().collect();
                let mut capture = crate::engine::runner::Runner::new(tx, schema, crate::engine::Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()), crate::meter::Meter::new(crate::meter::Ceilings::unbounded(), crate::meter::Cut::Abort), 0);
                let mut totals = BTreeMap::<Vec<u8>, i128>::new();
                let mut fits = true;
                super::activation::walk(tx, tx.num(&maintain.source)?, |_, mut row| {
                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row { fields.retain(|field, _| source.columns.contains_key(field)); }
                    // Assess the same activation-time capture that the atomic
                    // migration will write; grouping uncaptured paths as null
                    // could falsely reject sums that fit their real groups.
                    let paths:Vec<_>=paths.iter().filter(|path|row.field(path).is_err()).cloned().collect();
                    let row = capture.capture_recorded(source, crate::schema::row_image(&row, source).into_owned(), &paths)?;
                    if validate_row(schema, &maintain.source, &row).is_err() { fits = false; return Ok(()); }
                    if !count_safe && maintain.selected(&row) {
                        let value = match &maintain.kind {
                            crate::schema::MaintainKind::Count => 1,
                            crate::schema::MaintainKind::Sum { of } => i128::from(row.field(of)?.as_int()?),
                        };
                        let total = totals.entry(crate::key::encode(&maintain.source_key(&row))).or_default();
                        match total.checked_add(value) { Some(next) => *total = next, None => fits = false }
                    }
                    Ok(())
                })?;
                fits &= totals.values().all(|total| (crate::value::I53_MIN as i128..=crate::value::I53_MAX as i128).contains(total));
                if count_safe { count_checks.insert(maintain.source.clone(), fits); }
                assessed(step, maintain, fits);
            }
            continue;
        }
        let path: Vec<_> = step.path.split('.').collect();
        let Some(name) = path.get(1).copied() else { continue };
        let Some(table) = schema.table(name) else { continue };
        // @ref LLP 3000.016#21a-owned-events-follow-their-source-rows — check previews the engine fill, never an unfilled bit as absence.
        // Actual activation fills before this assessment and still validates
        // every row. A read-only check cannot write the old store's images.
        if let ["tables", _, "columns", column] = path.as_slice()
            && !previous.tables[name].columns.contains_key(*column)
            && table.columns.get(*column) == Some(&crate::schema::ColumnType::Bool)
            && schema.timelines.iter().any(|t| t.posts[0] == name && t.slot(false) == *column) {
            step.change = Change::Additive;
            step.message = format!("event slot {name}.{column} is added; activation fills it from byActorPost before validation; devices reacquire");
            continue;
        }
        let column_step = matches!(path.as_slice(), ["tables", _, "columns", column] if previous.tables[name].columns.contains_key(*column));
        if step.change != Change::Narrowing && !(column_step && step.change == Change::Additive) { continue; }
        let t = tx.num(name)?;
        let populated: bool = tx.tx.query_row("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM r WHERE t = ?1)", [t], |r| r.get(0))?;
        if !populated {
            step.change = Change::Additive;
            step.message = format!("{}; the table is empty", step.message.split(';').next().unwrap_or(&step.message));
            continue;
        }
        if matches!(path.as_slice(), ["tables", _, "sequences", _]) { continue; }
        if let ["tables", _, "columns", column] = path.as_slice() {
            if !previous.tables[name].columns.contains_key(*column) && matches!(table.defaults.get(*column), Some(ColumnDefault::Now | ColumnDefault::Viewer)) {
                continue;
            }
        }
        let mut fits = true;
        // Only the changed invariants need grouping; scan bounded image
        // buffers and retain a count per prospective key, never all rows.
        let mut groups: BTreeMap<(String, Vec<u8>), u64> = BTreeMap::new();
        super::activation::walk(tx, t, |_, mut row| {
            if !fits { return Ok(()); }
            if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut row { fields.retain(|column, _| table.columns.contains_key(column)); }
            materialize_optional_fields(&mut row, table);
            match path.as_slice() {
                ["tables", _, "columns", column] => {
                    let kind = &table.columns[*column];
                    fits = validate_column(name, column, kind, row.field(column).ok()).is_ok()
                        && super::activation::validate_assets(tx, kind, row.field(column).ok()).is_ok();
                    // @ref LLP 3000.007#18.3 — changing interpretation rechecks existing dependent invariants at the column's site.
                    for (index_name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique && index.uses_column(column)) {
                        let values = index_values(index, &row);
                        if !values.contains(&Value::Null) {
                            let count = groups.entry((format!("unique:{index_name}"), key::encode(&values))).or_default();
                            *count += 1;
                            fits &= *count <= 1;
                        }
                    }
                    for constraint in &table.constraints {
                        match constraint {
                            Constraint::Cap { by, max } if by.iter().any(|c| c == column) => {
                                let values: Vec<_> = by.iter().map(|c| row.field(c).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect();
                                if table.cap_exempts_null(by) && values.contains(&Value::Null) {continue;}
                                let count = groups.entry((format!("cap:{}", canonical_json(by)), key::encode(&values))).or_default();
                                *count += 1;
                                fits &= *count <= u64::from(*max);
                            }
                            Constraint::Text { field, min, format } if field == column => {
                                if let Ok(Value::String(text)) = row.field(column) {
                                    fits &= crate::engine::validate::validate_text(&format!("{name}.{column}"), text, *min, *format).is_ok();
                                }
                            }
                            _ => {}
                        }
                    }
                }
                ["tables", _, "indexes", index] => {
                    let values = index_values(&table.indexes[*index], &row);
                    if !values.contains(&Value::Null) {
                        let count = groups.entry(((*index).into(), key::encode(&values))).or_default();
                        *count += 1;
                        fits = *count <= 1;
                    }
                }
                ["tables", _, "constraints"] => {
                    fits = validate_row(schema, name, &row).is_ok();
                    for constraint in &table.constraints {
                        if let Constraint::Cap { by, max } = constraint {
                            let values: Vec<_> = by.iter().map(|c| row.field(c).cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)).collect();
                                if table.cap_exempts_null(by) && values.contains(&Value::Null) {continue;}
                            let count = groups.entry((canonical_json(by), key::encode(&values))).or_default();
                            *count += 1;
                            fits &= *count <= u64::from(*max);
                        }
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;
        if fits {
            step.change = Change::Additive;
            step.message.push_str("; existing rows satisfy it");
        } else {
            step.change = Change::Narrowing;
        }
    }
    for step in steps.iter_mut().filter(|s|s.change==Change::Narrowing) {
        step.message=super::adopt_refusals::detail(tx,schema,step)?;
    }
    Ok(steps)
}

fn assessed(step: &mut Step, maintain: &crate::schema::Maintain, fits: bool) {
    if !fits {
        step.change = Change::Narrowing;
        step.message = format!("maintain {} cannot adopt these source rows: an interpreted contribution is invalid or the final value is out of range", maintain.label());
    } else { step.message.push_str("; assessed source rows fit the derived rebuild"); }
}

NOT READY

- **Retained counters are skipped when an ordinary aggregate becomes a same-name row-keyed view.** In [maintains.rs:398](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/maintains.rs:398), any current maintain with the same target suppresses predecessor-counter normalization, while the earlier loop at line 347 excludes row-keyed maintains. Thus a legacy aggregate counter with high-water 5 survives under its legacy key while activation publishes `sha256-v1`. Reintroducing the original aggregate later skips migration and allocates ordinal 1 under its digest address, violating retained high-water custody. Normalize predecessor aggregate counters independently of whether the candidate reuses that target name for a row-keyed view.
